author: davcs86
body:
$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Consolidates 5 open Dependabot PRs (#53–#57) for `xstockstrat-trading` into a single consistent update, and bumps the Go toolchain from **1.23 → 1.25** (required by two of the dependencies).

### Dependency changes (`services/xstockstrat-trading/go.mod`)

| Package | Old | New | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `github.com/jackc/pgx/v5` | 5.6.0 | **5.9.2** | 🔒 Security: SQL injection via dollar-quoted strings (GHSA-j88v-2chj-qfwx) |
| `google.golang.org/grpc` | 1.65.0 | **1.79.3** | 🔒 Security: `:path` auth-bypass fix; requires Go 1.24 |
| `golang.org/x/crypto` | 0.23.0 | **0.46.0** | Security: SSH GSSAPI DoS + panic fixes |
| `golang.org/x/net` | 0.25.0 | **0.48.0** | Bug fixes (HTTP/2, HTML parsing) |
| `go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk` | 1.27.0 | **1.43.0** | New features + race condition fixes |
| `go.opentelemetry.io/otel` | 1.27.0 | **1.43.0** | Aligned with sdk bump |
| `google.golang.org/protobuf` | 1.34.1 | **1.36.10** | Transitive via grpc bump |
| Transitive deps | — | — | x/sys, x/sync, x/text, genproto, etc. updated accordingly |

### Go toolchain bump (1.23 → 1.25)

`pgx/v5 5.9.2` and `otel/sdk 1.43.0` both declare `go 1.25` in their own `go.mod` — this is a **hard toolchain requirement**, not just an inherited directive. Attempting to build with Go 1.24 fails with:
```
go: github.com/jackc/pgx/v5@v5.9.2 requires go >= 1.25.0
go: go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk@v1.43.0 requires go >= 1.25.0
```

Files updated per the [version bump workflow](../../blob/main-dev/CLAUDE.md#version-bump-workflow):
- `CLAUDE.md` §Language Versions & Tooling
- `go.work`
- `Dockerfile.codegen`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (both `go-version` entries)
- `services/xstockstrat-{trading,portfolio,marketdata}/Dockerfile`

### Breaking changes found

**None at the source level.** `go build ./...` completed cleanly with Go 1.25.0 (`GOWORK=off GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`). No API surfaces changed — all 5 Dependabot updates are drop-in version bumps.

The only "breaking" aspect is the toolchain requirement itself: CI and Dockerfiles will now use Go 1.25 instead of 1.23.

### Why consolidate instead of merging individually?

All 5 PRs targeted `main` (not `main-dev`) and all touched the same two files (`go.mod`, `go.sum`), making sequential cherry-picks conflict-prone. The consolidated approach produces the correct union of all version constraints in a single clean commit.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify CI go-lint and go-test jobs pass with Go 1.25
- [ ] Confirm `go build ./...` passes in `services/xstockstrat-trading` with `GOWORK=off`
- [ ] Close Dependabot PRs #53, #54, #55, #56, #57 once this is merged

## Summary

Wires the three follow-ups left open after PR #2:

1. **Backend `/api/v1/users/me/*`** — full self-service profile + password change, plus admin user CRUD.
2. **Acknowledge action** — `POST /api/v1/handovers/:id/acknowledge` is now called by the real button on the handover detail page (BR-10 enforced server-side: preparer cannot acknowledge their own handover).
3. **Playwright E2E pipeline** — 14 specs running in a new `e2e` CI job against a Postgres 15 service with the seeded fixtures.

### Backend
- `backend/src/schemas/users.schema.ts` — Zod schemas (`ProfileUpdateSchema` for `{ name?, locale?, theme?, density?, defaultShift? }`, `ChangePasswordSchema` with strength regex + length 8–128).
- `backend/src/services/users.service.ts` — 8 service functions: get/update self, change password (bcrypt at `BCRYPT_ROUNDS`, rejects new=current), admin list/create/get/update, soft-delete (deactivate, never hard-delete; rejects deactivating self), reactivate via PATCH `isActive=true`.
- `backend/src/routes/users.routes.ts` — 7 handlers; admin endpoints gated by `requireRole(['ADMIN'])`. Wired into `backend/src/server.ts`.
- `tests/unit/services/users.service.test.ts` — 17 new unit tests. Total now **65 passing**.

### Frontend
- `frontend/app/api/v1/users/me/route.ts` (GET/PATCH), `frontend/app/api/v1/users/me/password/route.ts` (POST), `frontend/app/api/v1/users/route.ts` (GET/POST), `frontend/app/api/v1/users/[id]/route.ts` (PATCH/DELETE), `frontend/app/api/v1/handovers/[id]/acknowledge/route.ts` (POST) — Next.js proxy route handlers that forward to the backend with the existing HMAC-signed `X-OCC-AUTH-*` header bridge so client pages keep using `fetch('/api/v1/...')` over cookie auth.
- `frontend/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx` — wired to GET/PATCH `/api/v1/users/me` and POST `/api/v1/users/me/password`.
- `frontend/app/(app)/handover/[id]/page.tsx` — `acknowledgeAction` (server action) calls real backend; also fixes a pre-existing scaffold bug where the page expected flat `aircraftItems[]` while the backend returns `categories.{aircraft,airport,...}`. Adapted with `BackendHandoverDetail` type + transform.
- Extracted `toItemView` from `components/handover/CategorySection.tsx` (a `'use client'` module) to a new non-client module `frontend/lib/handover/toItemView.ts` and a shared `CategorySection.types.ts`. Pure exports of `'use client'` modules become server-side module references, which crashed SSR with `p is not a function` when called from the server component.
- `frontend/app/(app)/admin/users/AdminUsersClient.tsx` — create/update/deactivate now hit the real proxies.

### E2E
- `playwright.config.ts` — boots backend (`backend/dist/server.js`) and frontend (`next start`) as Playwright web servers, injects `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` / `AUTH_SECRET` / `AUTH_TRUST_HOST=true` / `DATABASE_URL` so production-mode Auth.js trusts the host.
- `tests/e2e/helpers/auth.ts` — `SEED_ACCOUNTS` for `occ.staff@example.com` / `supervisor@example.com` / `admin@example.com` (all `Password123!`) + `signIn` helper.
- `tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts` (5), `tests/e2e/settings.spec.ts` (5), `tests/e2e/handover.spec.ts` (4) — total **14 specs**, run in ~21s locally.
- `npm run test:e2e` is now a script that loads `.env` via `scripts/run-node-with-root-env.mjs` before invoking Playwright.

### CI
- New `e2e` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `postgres:15` service, `db:migrate:deploy` + `db:seed`, build both apps, `playwright install --with-deps chromium`, `npm run test:e2e`, upload `playwright-report` and `test-results` traces as artifacts on failure.

Verified locally: `npm test` (65 pass), `npm run typecheck` (0 errors), `npm run build` (both apps), `CI=1 npm run test:e2e` (14 pass).

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Confirm the proxy-route pattern for `/api/v1/...` in the frontend is acceptable — alternative would be calling `backendFetch` directly from server components/actions on every page. The proxy keeps client `fetch('/api/v1/...')` calls simple but adds an extra hop.
- [ ] Sanity-check the backend admin routes: ADMIN should be able to GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE; non-ADMIN should get 403 (covered by `requireRole`, not exhaustively E2E-tested yet — only the role-gating on the `/admin/users` page route is tested in `auth.spec.ts`).
- [ ] Run the new E2E job in CI and inspect the uploaded `playwright-report` artifact if anything fails. The retries are set to 1 so flaky failures should self-heal once but still surface.
- [ ] Verify `BCRYPT_ROUNDS=4` in CI's e2e env doesn't block any new tests you might add — it's set low for E2E speed; production should use the existing `BCRYPT_ROUNDS=12`.

### Notes
- `POST /api/v1/users/me/sessions/revoke` is **not** wired yet — the backend endpoint doesn't exist. The Settings UI currently doesn't try to call it. Recommend a follow-up PR once `shared/API_SPEC.md` documents the contract.
- `/handover/new` wizard and `/reports` are still placeholder/demo data — out of scope for this PR.

author: 0xfandom
body:
## Summary
- Single-chain WebSocket listener that drives the indexer's hot path: dial WSS, subscribe to new heads, fetch + decode logs per block, publish to Kafka.
- Structure is multi-chain ready (one goroutine per \`ChainConfig\`) but Day 1 runs Base only — multi-chain rollout starts Day 2 once the pipeline is stable.

## Details
- \`internal/ingestion/listener.go\`
  - \`ChainListener\` wraps \`types.ChainConfig\` + \`ABIDecoder\` + \`Producer\`.
  - \`Run(ctx)\` loops: dial → subscribe → per-block \`processBlock\` → return on error.
  - Exponential backoff reconnection: \`1s -> 30s\` cap, max 10 attempts. Backoff aborts cleanly on context cancel.
  - Updates \`chain_listener_connected{chain}\` gauge and \`block_processing_duration_seconds{chain}\` histogram.
  - Optional contract whitelist via \`ChainConfig.Contracts\`.
  - Pluggable \`Dialer\` + \`EthClient\` interface so tests don't need a real ws node.

## Tests
- Dial failure path: \`Run\` invokes the dialer at least once and exits cleanly on context cancel.
- Block-processing path: fake client emits a header → \`FilterLogs\` is called once with the right block range, then context cancel → graceful exit.
- \`parseContracts\` handles empty and well-formed inputs.
- All under \`-race\`.

## Stacking
- Stacked on #19 (\`feat/kafka-producer\`). Linear chain: types → log → metrics → decoder → producer → listener.

Closes #5

author: i-would-like-to-report-a-bug-please
body:
Metadata saves can kick off noisy duplicate-status polling and the metadata enforcer can miss supported files immediately after Calibre renames a book folder. In practice this makes metadata edits look stuck or intermittently fail post-save enforcement even though the supported EPUB/AZW3 file exists shortly afterward.

Stop duplicate notifications from continuously polling stale/pending cache states on normal page loads, and make the cover/metadata enforcer retry supported file discovery when Calibre's DB says a supported format should be present. Add diagnostic output listing visible files when the expected format never appears.

author: markselby9
body:
## Summary

Adds `--output-format gitlab`, emitting a CodeClimate-style JSON report that GitLab CI can ingest directly via `artifacts:reports:codequality`. Today users have to pipe pyrefly through a third-party converter (mypy-gitlab-code-quality, pyright-to-gitlab-ci) to surface findings inline on merge requests; this gives them first-class support to match what `ty --output-format gitlab` already does for that ecosystem.

## Output format

Each emitted entry follows the GitLab Code Quality spec subset:

```json
{
  "description": "bad-assignment: Cannot assign str to int",
  "check_name": "bad-assignment",
  "fingerprint": "9f3c1a2b4d5e6f70",
  "severity": "major",
  "location": {
    "path": "src/foo.py",
    "lines": { "begin": 12 }
  }
}
```

## Design notes

- **Fingerprint**: hashed from `(error_kind, project-relative path)` only. Excluding line and message keeps fingerprints stable across runs when surrounding code shifts; collisions within a single run are resolved by salt-rehashing so multiple issues of the same kind in one file still get distinct IDs.
- **Severity mapping**: `Info` → `info`, `Warn` → `minor`, `Error` → `major`. `Ignore` is filtered out, mirroring the GitHub writer's treatment of suppressed errors.
- **Path normalization**: paths are emitted with forward slashes regardless of host OS. GitLab CI runners are Linux containers, so a Windows `src\foo.py` would silently fail to match repo files.

## Tests

- `gitlab_output_format_writes_valid_json` — entry shape and required keys
- `gitlab_output_format_severity_mapping` — Info/Warn/Error mapping; Ignore filtered
- `gitlab_output_format_fingerprint_stability` — same (kind, path) → same fingerprint across messages
- `gitlab_output_format_fingerprint_collision_resolution` — salt-rehash gives distinct IDs in-run
- `gitlab_output_format_description_includes_check_name` — `<kind>: <msg>` format
- `gitlab_output_format_empty_error_list` — empty input emits `[]\n`, not null
- `gitlab_output_format_path_outside_relative_to` — falls back to absolute path

## Why this format

The [GitLab Code Quality spec](https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/testing/code_quality/#code-quality-report-format) is the standard ingestion shape for `artifacts:reports:codequality`. Astral's `ty` ships this natively as `--output-format gitlab`, and ruff users adopt the same pattern via converters — picking up the same shape keeps pyrefly drop-in compatible with existing GitLab pipelines.

Fixes #3049

body:
## Summary

**P1a + P1b of the voice-tool expansion plan**, shipped together on this branch.

### P1a — Structured Health logging (VTID-02753, 5 tools)

| Tool | Pillar | Args |
|---|---|---|
| `log_water` | hydration | `amount_ml` |
| `log_sleep` | sleep | `minutes` |
| `log_exercise` | exercise | `minutes`, `activity_type?` |
| `log_meditation` | mental | `minutes` |
| `get_pillar_subscores` (read-only) | any | `pillar` |

Each `log_*` writes one row to `health_features_daily`, then triggers `health_compute_vitana_index_for_user` so the badge moves immediately. Backed by `services/gateway/src/services/voice-tools/health-log.ts`.

### P1b — Community Member Search (VTID-02754, 1 tool + endpoint + table)

`find_community_member` — a single voice tool that turns any "who is..." question into a redirect to **exactly one community member's profile**. The user lands on `/u/<vitana_id>?from=who_search&search_id=<id>` and reads a "How we searched" card explaining what Vitana looked at.

**Pipeline (4 tiers + 2 modifiers, every call ends on one user):**

- **Tier 1 — Exact**: services / facts / activities / groups
- **Tier 2 — Vitana Index**: overall ("healthiest") or per-pillar ("fittest", "best sleep", "calmest", "best diet")
- **Tier 3 — Affinity**: 6 lanes — **teaching, expertise, experience, motivation, entertainment, conversation** + a generic bio-trigram fallback. Each lane has its own signal stack so "best teacher" doesn't get the same ranking as "funniest"
- **Tier 4 — Ethics**: sensitive comparatives ("most beautiful", "richest") fall through to Tier 3 with a re-framing voice line. Still always redirects to one real person

**Modifiers** compose with any tier or stand alone:
- **Location** — city/country match for "near me", "in my city", "in Berlin"
- **Tenure** — `registration_seq` for "newest", "longest", "OG member"

**Two presentation channels, one tool result:**
- `voice_summary` — Gemini reads aloud BEFORE the navigate directive (1–2 sentences, never apologetic)
- `match_recipe` — structured signal list the frontend renders as a "How we searched" card

**Privacy invariants:** `global_community_profiles.is_visible = true`, `can_read_profile_field` for per-field reveal, `excluded_vitana_ids` drives "show me someone else".

**No `degraded`/`partial`/`warning` keys** in tool result — Gemini Live treats those as failure and apologises.

## Architecture

P1a tools — `services/gateway/src/routes/orb-live.ts` (line ~3411 declarations, line ~6086 handlers) backed by `services/gateway/src/services/voice-tools/health-log.ts`.

P1b tool — `find_community_member` registered alongside `search_community` in `orb-live.ts`, handler queues navigation directive directly. Backed by:
- `services/gateway/src/services/voice-tools/superlatives.ts` (Tier 2 + tenure primitives)
- `services/gateway/src/services/voice-tools/community-member-ranker.ts` (4-tier orchestrator)
- `services/gateway/src/routes/community-find-member.ts` (POST search + GET recipe by search_id)
- `supabase/migrations/20260510000000_vtid_02754_community_search_history.sql` (new table, RLS viewer-scoped, 30-day pg_cron TTL)

## Test plan

### P1a — Voice (Vertex)
- [ ] "log 500ml of water" → `log_water` fires, Hydration pillar rises
- [ ] "I slept 7 hours last night" → `log_sleep` fires
- [ ] "30 minutes of running" → `log_exercise` fires with `activity_type='running'`
- [ ] "10 minutes of meditation" → `log_meditation` fires
- [ ] "why is my Sleep score low" → `get_pillar_subscores` fires
- [ ] LiveKit parity via `POST /api/v1/orb/tool`

### P1b — Voice (Vertex)

- [ ] "Who is the healthiest in our community?" → Tier 2 overall index
- [ ] "Who is the fittest?" → Tier 2 exercise pillar

- [ ] "Who is the smartest about nutrition?" → Tier 3 expertise

- [ ] "Who is the newest member?" → tenure modifier
- [ ] "Newest salsa teacher in my city" → composition (Tier 1 + tenure + location)
- [ ] After redirect: WhyThisMatchCard renders structured signal list (frontend PR follow-up)

body:
## Summary

Adds `dags/assets/` — a comprehensive reference for every Airflow 3 **Asset** (data-aware scheduling) use case, plus `dags/kubernetes/` with four Kubernetes execution method samples.

---

## Assets (`dags/assets/`)

### `asset_defs.py` — shared definitions
Central `Asset` and `AssetAlias` objects (bronze / silver / gold medallion tiers) imported by all DAGs so URIs never drift between producer and consumer.

### `a1_asset_producers` — all ways to CREATE an asset event
| Pattern | Mechanism |
|---------|-----------|
| `ingest_orders_raw` | `@task(outlets=[asset])` — minimal form |
| `ingest_customers` | `BashOperator(outlets=[asset])` — any operator |
| `backfill_all_bronze` | `outlets=[a, b]` — one task, multiple events |
| `clean_and_enrich` | `outlet_events[asset].extra = {...}` — attach metadata |
| `build_daily_report` | `raise AirflowSkipException` — quality gate suppresses event |

### `a2_asset_consumers` — all scheduling strategies (5 DAGs)
| DAG | Schedule | Triggers when |
|-----|----------|---------------|
| `a2a_single_asset_schedule` | `schedule=asset` | that asset updates |
| `a2b_and_all_assets` | `schedule=[a, b]` | ALL listed assets update |
| `a2c_or_any_asset` | `schedule=a \| b` | ANY updates |
| `a2d_complex_asset_expr` | `schedule=(a & b) \| c` | boolean combination |
| `a2e_asset_or_time_schedule` | `AssetOrTimeSchedule(cron, assets)` | asset OR cron — first wins |

### `a3_asset_alias` — AssetAlias decoupling (2 DAGs)
- **Producer**: resolves alias → concrete assets at runtime; dynamic URI from conf
- **Consumer**: `schedule=alias_bronze_ingestion` — never hard-codes a URI

### `a4_asset_events_branching` — event metadata + decision making
```
inspect_incoming_event  (best-of-N events, 48 h staleness SLA)
        ↓
  route_by_quality  (@task.branch on quality_score from inlet_events)
        ↓
  ├─ full_enrichment      (≥ 0.95 → gold → emits daily_report asset)
  ├─ light_cleanse        (≥ 0.80 → silver → no asset event)
  └─ quarantine_and_alert (< 0.80 → alert → no asset event)
```

### `a5_asset_lifecycle_api` — lifecycle management via REST API
| Task | API | Purpose |
|------|-----|---------|
| `list_all_assets` | `GET /assets` | discover all assets + lineage |
| `query_asset_events` | `GET /assets/events` | audit event history |
| `materialize_asset_event` | `POST /assets/events` | external trigger (Spark/dbt/shell) |
| `archive_asset` | `DELETE /assets/<id>` | remove from metastore; data unaffected |

Supports `dry_run=true` (default) to preview without writing.

---

## Kubernetes (`dags/kubernetes/`)

| DAG | Method | Highlights |
|-----|--------|-----------|
| `k1_kubepod_operator` | `KubernetesPodOperator` | 5 patterns: basic, env/ConfigMap, volume, init-container, resource profile |
| `k2_kubejob_advanced` | `KubernetesJobOperator` | TTL/backoff/deadline, indexed parallel completions, init container, PriorityClass |
| `k3_dynamic_k8s_fan_out` | `.partial().expand()` | runtime fan-out, XCom aggregation, `max_active_tis_per_dagrun` cap |
| `k4_task_kubernetes_decorator` | `@task.kubernetes` | Python functions in K8s pods, per-task resource budgets |

---

## Test plan
- [ ] `pytest tests/test_1_dag_integrity.py` — all new DAGs parse without errors
- [ ] Verify `a1_asset_producers` triggers `a2a_single_asset_schedule` after run
- [ ] Verify `a2b_and_all_assets` only fires after both assets update
- [ ] Verify `a3_alias_consumer` triggers via alias after `a3_alias_producer` runs
- [ ] Verify `a4_asset_events_branching` routes correctly for each quality tier
- [ ] Verify `a5_asset_lifecycle_api` with `dry_run=true` (safe default)
- [ ] Kubernetes DAGs: deploy to a cluster with the cncf-kubernetes provider and validate pod/job creation

author: zarjun247
body:
### Motivation

- Close several safety gaps left after the previous stabilization pass to prevent client-trusted values, leaked dev OTP data in production, and unauthorized access to dosage schedules.  
- Ensure cart/checkout flows validate SKU/store/product/quantity server-side before committing locks or orders.  
- Prevent unsafe prescription uploads by adding file size/type/signature checks.  
- Make onboarding assigned-store resolution authoritative on the server and improve repo hygiene status docs.

### Description

- OTP/session: `verifyOtp` now signs sessions with `ENV.appId` and preserves `devCode` only for non-production builds to avoid production leaks.  
- Cart/upsert: `cart.upsert` fetches SKU server-side via `getSkuById` and rejects store mismatch, inactive SKU, product mismatch, or insufficient quantity, and uses the server-resolved `productId`.  
- Checkout/locks: checkout now validates each cart SKU (existence, active, store match, product match, available quantity) before `softLockCart`, applies soft locks, and releases locks with `releaseSoftLock(lockItems)` on post-lock failures.  
- Onboarding: `completeOnboarding` no longer trusts frontend `assignedStoreId` and instead resolves/validates the assigned store via `resolveStore` (building) or `checkServiceability` (address) before persisting.  
- Prescription upload: added MIME allowlist (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `application/pdf`), 8 MB max size, key extension chosen by MIME, and magic-byte signature checks before `storagePut`.  
- Dosage APIs: dosage endpoints (`recordTaken`, `recordSkipped`, `adherence`, `remaining`) now pass `ctx.user.id` to service functions and the dosage service methods enforce that the schedule belongs to the caller.  
- Docs/hygiene: updated `STALE_PR_STATUS.md` to mark stale duplicate PRs, and updated `BUG_HYGIENE_AUDIT_STATUS.md` and `PRODUCTION_READINESS_STATUS.md` notes for this safety pass.

Files changed: `server/routers.ts`, `server/db.ts`, `server/services/dosageTracking.ts`, `server/safety-regressions.test.ts`, `STALE_PR_STATUS.md`, `BUG_HYGIENE_AUDIT_STATUS.md`, and `PRODUCTION_READINESS_STATUS.md`.

### Testing

- Ran `pnpm install` successfully in this environment.  
- Ran `pnpm run check` (TypeScript checks) and it completed without type errors after fixes.  
- Ran `pnpm test -- --runInBand` and all test files passed (196 tests).  
- Ran `pnpm run build` and the production build completed successfully with non-blocking Vite warnings about analytics env placeholders and chunk sizes.

### Cambios principales:

1. **Validación de alcance pre-ejecución**: Antes de mover el robot, se comprueba con `SolveIK` que TODAS las poses del dibujo (trazado + subida) son alcanzables. Si no lo son, se informa con detalle (posición problemática).

2. **Auto-escalado** (`AUTO_ESCALAR = True`): Si hay puntos fuera de alcance, el dibujo se reduce progresivamente (en pasos ~4.5%) hasta que quepa en el workspace. Se informa del factor de escala aplicado.

3. **Selección de robot** (`NOMBRE_ROBOT_DIBUJO`): Permite elegir qué robot dibuja por nombre. Si se deja vacío, usa el primero disponible.

4. **Modo de referencia cruzada** (`MODO_REFERENCIA = 'otro'`): Permite usar el Target de otro robot (ej. UR5e) como referencia. El programa calcula automáticamente la transformación de coordenadas (`PoseAbs + invH`) para que el robot que dibuja (ej. UR3e) alcance las poses equivalentes en su propio espacio. Esto es útil porque el UR3e tiene ~500mm de alcance vs ~850mm del UR5e.

5. **Mejor manejo de errores**: Mensajes claros con soluciones sugeridas cuando hay problemas de alcance.

6. **README actualizado**: Documentación completa de todos los nuevos parámetros, modos de referencia y auto-escalado con tablas y ejemplos.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] Abrir RoboDK con un UR3e cargado y ejecutar el script con `AUTO_ESCALAR = True` para verificar que el auto-escalado reduce el dibujo correctamente cuando hay puntos fuera de alcance.
- [ ] Probar con `MODO_REFERENCIA = 'otro'` teniendo dos robots (UR3e + UR5e) en la estación para verificar la transformación de coordenadas.
- [ ] Verificar que con un Target bien posicionado (dentro del workspace) el script dibuja sin errores ni escalado innecesario.
- [ ] Comprobar que `NOMBRE_ROBOT_DIBUJO` selecciona correctamente el robot deseado.

### Notes

- Los imports `from robodk.robolink import *` se mantienen por convención de RoboDK (generan warnings F403/F405 en ruff, pero son el patrón estándar).
- El archivo adjunto "v5" llegó vacío (0 bytes), así que se trabajó sobre el código del repositorio.
- `ESCALA_MINIMA = 0.1` significa que el dibujo no se reducirá a menos del 10% de su tamaño original; si ni así cabe, se da error con instrucciones claras.

author: markselby9
body:
## Summary

The `ClassType <: SelfType` (and parallel `type[ClassType] <: type[SelfType]`) checks were too permissive — they accepted `return Shape()` (or `return Shape`) when the declared return type was `Self`, even though a subclass `Circle(Shape)` inheriting the method would have `Self = Circle` and the contract would break.

This PR tightens both arms to require a strict subclass UNLESS the class is `@final`.

Fixes #2304.

## The fix

Two arms in `pyrefly/lib/solver/subset.rs` now consult a small `is_final` pass-through added to `TypeOrder`:

- `ClassType <: SelfType` (line ~2029): `has_superclass(got, want) && (got != want || is_final(want))`. This is the primary fix — it catches `return Shape()` from `def m(self) -> Self`.
- `type[ClassType] <: SelfType` (line ~2041): mirrors the structure but keeps the existing `has_metaclass` check, with the same final-or-strict-subclass guard. This locks the rule in for the metaclass-relationship path so the two arms cannot drift again.

The `type[Self]` return case (e.g. `def make(cls) -> type[Self]: return C`) is also rejected — it falls through the `Type::Type(l), Type::Type(u)` recursion arm into the patched `ClassType <: SelfType` arm, so both arms collaborate to keep the rule consistent.

## Test cases

New `typing_self.rs` tests covering the fix:

- `test_self_return_concrete_class_final_ok` — @yangdanny97's `@final` example from the issue
- `test_self_return_concrete_class_generic` — generic-class case
- `test_self_return_concrete_class_object` and `test_self_return_concrete_class_object_final_ok` — `type[Self]` return-type case (non-final and `@final`)

Updated existing tests (dropped `bug = "..."` markers, added `# E:` markers per @migeed-z's review on #2405):

- `test_self_return_concrete_class` — the original repro
- `test_cls_new_with_concrete_class`
- `test_self_in_container_pinning`
- `test_overload_returning_self`

## Notable test fallout

The stricter check exposed adjacent patterns in four tests outside `typing_self.rs`. **Please weigh in on whether the rule should narrow for any of these — happy to follow up either way:**

1. **`test_bound_method_preserves_function_attributes_from_descriptor` (descriptors.rs)** — a `cache_on_self`-style decorator's `Callable[[Constraint], int]` parameter receives a method whose `self` is `Self@Constraint`. Function parameter positions are contravariant, so satisfying the assignment requires `Constraint <: Self@Constraint`, which now fails for non-final classes. Strictly correct under PEP 484 contravariance, but ergonomically painful for the `cache_on_self` decorator pattern. Marked with `# E:` to lock in current behavior; happy to narrow the rule (e.g. relax for parameters of decorator callables) if preferred.

2. **`test_functools_partial_pattern` (generic_basic.rs)** — the contrived overload pattern in this test (a hand-rolled `partial` clone using concrete return types instead of `Self`) now flags `inconsistent-overload`. Real typeshed's `functools.partial` uses `-> Self` and is unaffected. Marked with `# E:` so the test reflects the new behavior.

3. **`test_overloaded_new_mixed_annotation` (constructors.rs)** — overload return `C` is now correctly flagged as incompatible with impl return `Self`. This is a true positive of the fix.

These are the same contravariance subtlety as #1; please call out if you'd rather keep the prior ergonomic behavior and we'll narrow the rule before merge.

## Adjacent unsoundness surfaced (NOT fixed in this PR)

- **`test_enum_call_with_self_type` (enums.rs)**: `cls(code)` in a `@classmethod` is inferred as the concrete `__new__` return type instead of `Self@cls`. Documented with a fresh `bug = "..."` marker per the project convention so it doesn't regress silently. Worth a follow-up issue rather than expanding the scope of this PR.

## Conformance

Pass rate 0.92 → 0.94: `generics_self_basic.py` and `generics_self_usage.py` now pass. Updated `conformance.exp`, `conformance.result`, and `results.json` are included.

author: r1ghtss
body:
## Fix: 2 Build Failures (Comprehensive)

Full CI logs analyzed - both failures fixed in one PR.

---

### Error 1: `:expo-modules-core:compileReleaseKotlin` FAILED

**Root cause:** `npx expo install --fix` pulls Kotlin **1.9.25** transitively, but the Compose Compiler **1.5.14** (bundled with expo-modules-core) requires **exactly Kotlin 1.9.24**.

```
e: This version (1.5.14) of the Compose Compiler requires Kotlin version 1.9.24
but you appear to be using Kotlin version 1.9.25 which is not known to be compatible.
```

**Fix:** After `expo prebuild`, append a Gradle `resolutionStrategy` to `android/build.gradle` that forces **all** `org.jetbrains.kotlin` dependencies to 1.9.24:

```groovy
subprojects {
    configurations.all {
        resolutionStrategy.eachDependency { details ->
            if (details.requested.group == 'org.jetbrains.kotlin') {
                details.useVersion '1.9.24'
            }
        }
    }
}
```

---

### Error 2: `:app:processReleaseResources` FAILED

**Root cause:** `expo-splash-screen` generates a reference to `drawable/splashscreen_logo` from the `splash` config in `app.json`, but **no splash image file exists** in `assets/` (only `icon.png` and `adaptive-icon.png`).

```
resource drawable/splashscreen_logo (aka com.jhinkz.telegramdrive:drawable/splashscreen_logo) not found
```

**Fix:** Removed the `splash` block from `app.json` since there's no image to reference.

---

### Also
- Added `--stacktrace` to `gradlew` for better error diagnostics on future failures
- Passed `--legacy-peer-deps` to `npx expo install --fix` to prevent peer dep conflicts

### Files changed
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` - CI Kotlin patch + stacktrace
- `mobile-app/app.json` - removed splash config

author: pleymove
body:
## Contexte

Pipeline tourne en ~7s, GUI PyQt6 OK, D3 OK, mais **bug orphans** : sur le SRO `63258/LLW/PMZ/24228`, 66 BAT orphelins → 9 PA au lieu d'1.

## Regle metier (Pierre, 04/05/2026)

- 1 PA = max 120 prises (24 micro-modules × 5)
- **Par defaut : 1 seul PA par SRO**, snap sur infra publique existante
- Plusieurs PA seulement si :
  - Total prises > 120 → split k-means
  - Gap spatial > 7000 m entre clusters
  - Cluster isole ≥ 50 prises → son propre PA

## Changements

### `auvergne_pipeline/orphans.py` (rewrite quasi-complet)

| Avant | Apres |
|---|---|
| Clustering 200 m | Clustering 7000 m (union-find + cKDTree) |
| 1 PA par ex-ZAPA ou cluster spatial | 1 PA par SRO (sauf exceptions) |
| Barycentre brut | Snap sur cheminement/ATHD → fallback parcelle publique → placement impossible |
| Pas de merge | Merge clusters < 50 prises dans le plus proche |
| Pas de split | K-means pondere si > 120 prises |

## Summary

- Reverts #512: drops `--mmproj /models/mmproj-F16.gguf` from the llama.cpp compose command.
- Vision-on + 256K ctx + q8_0 KV cache exhausts the 4090 (24071/24564 MiB used; ~493 MiB free). mmproj warmup hits `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` allocating the 248 MiB compute graph at 1472×1472, and real vision requests stall at HTTP 503.
- Text inference was unaffected (LLM context allocated before warmup), so the symptom looked like a partial server outage.

## Path forward

Re-enable vision in a follow-up PR by combining:
- `--image-max-pixels 1048576` (cap vision graph at 1024×1024)
- `--ctx-size 131072` (halves KV cache footprint)

author: gdesmott
body:
`NewWildcardIterator_NonOptimized` previously boxed a bare `Wildcard` as                                                     
  `RQEIteratorWrapper<Wildcard>`, while `NewWildcardIterator` boxed the                                                        
  `NewWildcardIterator` enum as `RQEIteratorWrapper<NewWildcardIterator>`.                                                     
  Both produce iterators with `IteratorType::Wildcard`, but the heap
  layouts differ. The profile printing dispatch matches on `IteratorType`                                                      
  and casts the raw pointer to a concrete `RQEIteratorWrapper<T>`; with
  two different `T` behind the same discriminant, any single cast is                                                           
  unsound for one of them.                              
                                                                                                                               
  Wrap in `NewWildcardIterator::NotOptimized` before boxing so both
  factories produce the same heap type and the dispatch can always cast                                                        
  to `RQEIteratorWrapper<NewWildcardIterator>`.         
                                         
  `NewWildcardIterator_NonOptimized` is only used in a hybrid reader test                                                      
  so that should not affect performances.



#### Mark if applicable

- [ ] This PR introduces API changes
- [ ] This PR introduces serialization changes

#### Release Notes

- [ ] This PR requires release notes
- [x] This PR does not require release notes

If a release note is required (bug fix / new feature / enhancement), describe the **user impact** of this PR in the title.  


<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches FFI iterator construction and heap layout for wildcard iterators; while intended to fix an unsound cast, any mismatch in expected wrapper type could surface as runtime crashes if other code assumes the old layout.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes wildcard iterator FFI construction so *all* wildcard factories heap-allocate the same concrete wrapper type.
> 
> `NewWildcardIterator_NonOptimized` now wraps `Wildcard::new(...)` in `NewWildcardIterator::NotOptimized` before boxing, aligning its heap layout with `NewWildcardIterator`/optimized variants and avoiding type-unsafe downcasts that dispatch solely on `IteratorType::Wildcard`.
>

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

Two issues in the announce flow: (1) The sender's name was stored as `body.user.name` (the Slack username/handle) rather than their real display name, causing "unknown"-style names to appear in Notion's "Sent By" field. (2) Clicking "📊 Details" on an announcement in `/announce-status` called `sendStatusReport()`, but that function only showed aggregate stats with bare `<@user>` mentions — there was no way to see who specifically had read it, when they read it, or who was still pending.

## Solution

In `announce_modal_submit`, added a `client.users.info()` call immediately after extracting `senderId` to resolve the sender's real display name (`real_name` → `display_name` → username fallback), stored as `senderDisplayName`. This value is now passed to `db.createAnnouncement()`, `notion.createAnnouncementPage()`, and both `buildAnnouncementBlocks()` call sites. `buildAnnouncementBlocks` gained an optional `senderDisplayName` parameter — when present it renders as bold text instead of a `<@mention>`. `sendStatusReport` was rewritten to use `db.getAllReaders()` and split recipients into read/pending lists, showing each person's stored display name and exact read timestamp for the ✅ Read section, with chunking every 20 entries to stay within Slack's block text limits.

### Changes
- **Modified** `index.js`

author: raunplaymore
body:
## Summary

v0.10 마지막 트랙. ADR 0010 §D4 (메뉴바 UI) 구현. Track A의 `--check`와 Track B의 `--apply --yes`를 호출하는 UI wrapper.

이 트랙 머지 후 v0.10.0 release ceremony 진입 (사용자가 시작 신호로 지적한 "UI 갖춘 만큼 업데이트도 쉬워야" 격차 해소).

## D4 명세 구현

- **메뉴 아이템**: `"Check for Updates…"` — Quit 직전 위치
- **클릭 → 백그라운드 thread**: `sentinel update --check --json` subprocess (UI block 안 함)
- **결과 분기 (envelope `result` 키 기준)**:
  - `up_to_date` → native notification "Sentinel is up to date (vX)"
  - `update_available` → modal dialog `Update Now` (default) / `Skip This Version` / `Cancel`
    - **Update Now** → `sentinel update --apply --yes --json` 백그라운드 실행 + 메뉴 아이템 "Updating…" disable
      - `success` → notification "Updated to vX. **Quit and relaunch the menu bar app to load the new code.**" (D4 amendment)
      - `failure` → alert dialog with error
      - `locked` → notification "Another update in progress (PID N)"
    - **Skip This Version** → `<data_dir>/updater/skipped_versions.txt`에 추가, 향후 같은 버전 silent
    - **Cancel** → 무시
  - 그 외 (`error`, `editable`, `system_unsafe`, `homebrew`) → notification only, dialog 없음
- **No badge on icon** — 보안 alert badge 시맨틱 보호 (D4 invariant)
- **No automatic check on startup** — D2 일관 (on-demand only)

## 테스트 가능성을 위한 refactor

rumps는 display 필요해서 헤드리스 환경에서 import 어려움. 초기 구현은 helper를 `menubar_app.py` 인스턴스 메서드로 두고 테스트 파일에 동일 로직 복제했는데, **production 코드와 테스트 코드가 silent하게 drift할 위험** 발견 → 모듈로 추출.

신규: **`sentinel_mac/updater/menubar_helpers.py`** (pure 함수 4개, rumps 의존 없음):
- `read_skipped_versions(data_dir: Path) -> set[str]`
- `add_skipped_version(data_dir: Path, version: str) -> None`
- `parse_check_envelope(stdout: str) -> dict`
- `should_show_dialog(envelope: dict, skipped: set[str]) -> bool`

`menubar_app.py`와 `tests/test_menubar_update.py`는 모두 이 모듈에서 import — production과 테스트가 같은 코드를 검증.

## Threading

rumps 모달 호출(`rumps.alert`)은 main thread에서만 안전. 백그라운드 worker는 `_pending_update_action` 인스턴스 변수에 결과 stash → 기존 `@rumps.timer` 틱이 main thread에서 픽업해서 dispatch. POLL_SECONDS(5초) 기존 timer 재활용으로 추가 timer 안 씀.

## Files

신규:
- `sentinel_mac/updater/menubar_helpers.py` — 4 pure 함수
- `tests/test_menubar_update.py` (~400 LOC) — 30 테스트:
  - TestSkippedVersions(11) — read/add/idempotent/sorted
  - TestParseEnvelope(6) — JSON parse + 에러 처리
  - TestShouldShowDialog(7) — dialog 결정 로직
  - TestMenubarUpdateIntegration(4) — subprocess mock 검증
  - TestMenubarHeadlessImport(2) — `pytest.importorskip("rumps")` smoke

수정:
- `sentinel_mac/menubar_app.py` (+210 LOC) — Quit 직전에 메뉴 아이템 추가, `_on_check_updates`/`_check_updates_worker`/`_handle_check_result`/`_apply_update_async`/`_apply_update_worker`/`_handle_apply_result` 6 메서드. `_pending_update_action` dispatch.
- `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` Track C 항목

## Verification

- mypy clean (25 source files)
- ruff clean (sentinel_mac + tests — 둘 다)
- pytest **877 passed** (847 + 30 신규)
- `python -c "import sentinel_mac.menubar_app"` smoke OK
- `.venv/bin/sentinel update --check` editable 환경에서 exit 3 정상 (Track A 회귀 없음)

## Next steps

이 PR 머지 후 v0.10.0 release ceremony:
- typosquatting 목록 verify (CLAUDE.md)
- pyproject.toml `version` 0.9.0 → 0.10.0
- `sentinel_mac/__init__.py` `__version__` 0.9.0 → 0.10.0
- CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` → `[0.10.0] - 2026-05-05` with user-facing summary
- tag + GitHub Release → PyPI auto-publish

- [x] mypy / ruff / pytest local

- [ ] CI green 확인

author: maulepilot117
body:
## Summary

First per-provider sub-PR for Phase H Unit 19 (R13 in `plans/external-secrets-operator-integration.md`). Vault — the highest-leverage provider, exercising every scaffold path the U18 PR (#216) established.

The remaining 7 wizard providers will follow as their own sub-PRs (one per provider per the plan's mandate): AWS Secrets Manager, AWS Parameter Store, Azure Key Vault, GCP Secret Manager, Kubernetes (cross-namespace), Doppler, 1Password Connect. Akeyless, Bitwarden Secrets Manager, CyberArk Conjur, and Infisical ship as YAML templates in U20 per the plan's L7.2 culling pass.

## What ships

**Backend** (`secretstore_vault.go`):
- `validateVaultSpec` covers all 5 v1 auth methods: token / kubernetes / appRole / jwt / cert.
- Top-level fields validated: server (https-only, private addresses accepted for in-cluster Vault), path (no leading slash), version (v1/v2), namespace (Vault Enterprise).
- `pickVaultAuthMethod` enforces "exactly one of {token, kubernetes, appRole, jwt, cert}" with deterministic-order error message.
- AppRole: roleId XOR roleRef + secretRef required. JWT: secretRef OR kubernetesServiceAccountToken. Cert: clientCert + secretRef.
- `init()` self-registers via `RegisterSecretStoreProvider(SecretStoreProviderVault, validateVaultSpec)`.

**Tests** (`secretstore_vault_test.go`, 27 tests):
- Per-method × happy + per-method missing-required + edge cases.
- Top-level field validation (https-only, KV version, path leading-slash, namespace empty).
- Auth multi-method rejection.
- Dispatcher integration via `SecretStoreInput.Validate()`.
- Structural ToYAML walk to `spec.provider.vault.auth.token.tokenSecretRef`.

**Frontend** (`VaultForm.tsx`, ~530 LoC):
- Auth-method picker + 5 per-method field components.
- Switching auth method clears the auth slate (preserves top-level fields).
- Field-level error keys match the Go validator paths exactly (e.g., \`auth.token.tokenSecretRef.name\`).

**Wizard wiring** (`SecretStoreWizard.tsx`):
- \`PROVIDER_FORMS\` registry replaces hardcoded provider check — adding a provider's form is now a single registry entry, no Configure-step edits required.
- 422 error.detail is parsed; per-field errors populate \`errors.value\` and the wizard navigates back to Configure for in-place correction (the carefully-aligned VaultForm error keys actually fire now).
- Dynamic \`stepsFor(provider)\` returns 4-step (Identity / Provider / Configure / Review) when the selected provider is in \`READY_SECRET_STORE_PROVIDERS\`, 3-step otherwise.

**Types** (`eso-types.ts`):
- Added \`\"vault\"\` to \`READY_SECRET_STORE_PROVIDERS\`. Picker derives readiness from this Set, so Vault is now selectable.

## Pre-push review (`/ce:review`)

9 reviewer personas surfaced 16 findings. Commit \`a058e31\` resolved 15:

**Load-bearing fixes:**
- **Server 422 errors no longer dropped** — fetchPreview parses error.detail into per-field errors and routes the user back to Configure. Without this fix, the careful field-level error wiring in VaultForm was dead code.
- **PROVIDER_FORMS registry replaces hardcoded vault check** — would have silently broken the next provider sub-PR (Configure step would render an empty panel).
- **Cast-heavy reads** consolidated via VaultSpec / VaultAuthSpec typed interfaces.

**Backend hardening:**
- Dropped the structurally-wrong validateHTTPSPublicURL double-call in validateVaultSpec (logic was accidentally correct but maintenance-hazard).
- pickVaultAuthMethod's multi-method error message is now deterministic (was random map-iteration order).
- Removed misleading \"Allow flat shape\" comment that contradicted the code.

**Test polish:**
- TestSecretStoreInput_VaultIntegration_ToYAML now structurally parses the YAML and walks to the auth.token.tokenSecretRef path. Replaces a dead \`if ... { _ = y }\` block.
- TestHandleSecretStorePreview_ClusterScope now uses a complete valid spec so the assertion isolates the scope-check contract.

**Advisory (deferred):**
- Provider override warning (#16) — RegisterSecretStoreProvider silently replaces prior registrations. A meta-test for this is more scaffolding than the risk warrants. Carry forward to U19 last sub-PR or U20.
- Agent-native: no GET /wizards/secret-store/providers endpoint. Agents can't query \"which providers are wizard-ready\". Carry forward to a separate U19 follow-up.

## Verification

- \`go vet ./...\` clean.
- \`go test ./... -count=1\` — 30 packages pass.
- \`go test ./internal/wizard/ -count=10\` — 10 runs, no flakes (matches plan's L7.5 stability requirement).
- \`deno check\` + \`deno lint\` clean on all touched frontend files.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes (\`go test\`, \`deno task check\`, Trivy, E2E with kind).
- [ ] Smoke: \`/external-secrets/stores/new\` — pick Vault → 4-step wizard renders. Other providers still show \"coming soon\" and are not selectable.
- [ ] Smoke: leave required fields blank, click Preview YAML — wizard navigates back to Configure with field-level error indicators next to the offending inputs (server, auth.token.tokenSecretRef.name, etc.).
- [ ] Smoke: switch auth method (token → AppRole → token) — auth fields clear cleanly, no stale state.
- [ ] Smoke: complete a Vault SecretStore against a homelab Vault → preview YAML → /yaml/apply → store appears in observatory.
- [ ] CommandPalette: existing \"Create SecretStore\" / \"Create ClusterSecretStore\" entries navigate correctly.

body:
## Summary

Two-line summary: drains the original Hygiene-queue item from `docs/handoff.md`; records the **Shape C** migration plan as the next session's highest-priority work.

## Changes

### 1. The original handoff item (the actual code change)

`TuiToolsView` and `TuiTasksView` no longer instantiate `WorkspaceApiClient` inline (`using var client = new WorkspaceApiClient();`). Both are now `internal sealed class TuiXxxView(WorkspaceApiClient client)` that receive the client via primary constructor, threaded through `TuiShell` → `TuiSlashCommandDispatcher`. `WorkspaceApiClient` is registered **Singleton** (Microsoft's HttpClient guidance is one-per-application, not one-per-call).

The other 13 inline `new WorkspaceApiClient()` callsites the handoff also enumerated are **NOT** touched in this PR — they get drained as their consumers move into Actions during Shape C migration.

### 2. Shape C migration plan (handoff doc)

Top-priority Next Work item in `docs/handoff.md`. Step-back review of the TUI piece during this PR concluded the structure is wrong:
- 23 slash commands duplicate ~22 CLI commands
- TUI helpers couple Spectre prompts inline; no path for non-Spectre frontends (web dashboard, LSP, IPC)
- A future frontend would have to rewrite all the orchestration

The fix is a shared **Actions layer** (`Weave.Actions`) between the silo HTTP API and frontends. Both CLI and TUI become consumers of the same actions; neither hosts the other. Five-phase migration sketched out, Phase 0 (foundation + one pilot action) is the next session's pickup.

## What this PR does NOT contain

This branch initially explored a much larger refactor across 5 commits (one-interface + keyed-DI dispatcher, 23 command classes, 10 helper interfaces, WorkspaceApiClient lifetime promotion). That work was deemed wrong-direction once Shape C was identified — it would have been deleted in Phase 4 anyway. **All five exploratory commits force-rolled-back.** Branch now has a single commit containing only the original two-file fix + handoff plan.

author: origamihase
body:
## Problem

Die Website bewirbt eine Sitemap:

```
docs/robots.txt:4: Sitemap: https://origamihase.github.io/wien-oepnv/sitemap.xml
```

Und der Generator existiert (`scripts/generate_sitemap.py`, 174 Zeilen). Aber:
- **Kein Workflow** rief den Generator je auf (`grep -rn "generate_sitemap" .github/` ergab keine Treffer).
- `docs/sitemap.xml` war via `.gitignore` ausgeschlossen, sodass GitHub Pages sie nie ausliefern konnte.
- README behauptete „bereits vorbereitet", was de facto falsch war.

→ Der `Sitemap:`-Verweis in `robots.txt` ging dauerhaft ins Leere — Suchmaschinen bekamen 404. Das ist **Bug 1.5** aus der ursprünglichen Diagnose.

## Lösung

Den existierenden Generator in den bereits laufenden `seo-guard.yml`-Workflow eingebaut:

### Änderungen

- **`.gitignore`**: `docs/sitemap.xml`-Eintrag entfernt — die Datei muss committed sein, damit GitHub Pages sie ausliefert.
- **`docs/sitemap.xml`**: Initialer Generator-Output committed (~200 URLs aus dem `docs/`-Tree). So liefert Pages **sofort** nach dem Merge eine Sitemap, ohne dass der Workflow erst noch laufen muss.
- **`.github/workflows/seo-guard.yml`**:
  * Push-Trigger erweitert um `scripts/generate_sitemap.py`-Änderungen
  * `permissions: contents: write` für den Auto-Commit-Step
  * `concurrency`-Gruppe `seo-guard-${{ github.ref }}` verhindert konkurrierende Läufe auf der gleichen Sitemap-Datei
  * **Refresh-Step**: `python scripts/generate_sitemap.py`
  * **Verify-Step**: prüft `<urlset>` Root, ≥1 `<loc>`-Eintrag und Verweis auf `SITE_BASE` — analog zum bestehenden `robots.txt`-Verify
  * **Commit-Step**: nur auf `push to main`, nutzt `stefanzweifel/git-auto-commit-action@v7` (gleiches Pin wie die anderen Cache-Workflows), `[skip ci]` um Build-Kaskaden zu vermeiden
- **`README.md`**: irreführende „bereits vorbereitet"-Aussage durch eine korrekte Beschreibung ersetzt.

### Was bleibt unverändert

- Der Generator selbst (`scripts/generate_sitemap.py`) wurde nicht angefasst. Er hat bereits SSRF-/Injection-Schutz für `SITE_BASE_URL`-Overrides und 3 grüne Tests in `tests/scripts/test_generate_sitemap_security.py`.
- Cron, push-paths und Description-Step bleiben funktional gleich; nur thematisch passende Steps wurden eingefügt.

## Test plan

- [x] `python scripts/generate_sitemap.py` lokal: erzeugt valide `docs/sitemap.xml` mit 200 URLs
- [x] `python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_generate_sitemap_security.py`: 3 passed
- [x] `python -m pytest`: **1001 passed, 1 skipped**
- [x] `mypy --strict`: 0 neue Errors
- [ ] CI grün
- [ ] Nach Merge: `https://origamihase.github.io/wien-oepnv/sitemap.xml` ist erreichbar (200, valides XML)

## Bezug zur Diagnose

Behebt **Bug 1.5** aus dem Diagnose-Bericht. Damit sind alle ursprünglich identifizierten kritischen Funktionsbugs (1.1–1.5) abgearbeitet.

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

The build enters an infinite loop because `client/project.json` is not recognized by npm as a package manifest. With no `package.json` in the client directory, npm resolves scripts from the root `package.json`, whose `build` script is `cd client && npm install && npm run build` — restarting the cycle indefinitely until the process is killed with exit code 249. Additionally, the Vite config is named `vitisconfig.js` instead of `vite.config.js`, so Vite never loads it, and `@vitejs/plugin-react` is missing from the client dependencies despite being imported in the config.

## Solution

Renamed `client/project.json` to `client/package.json` and added a `build: "vite build"` script so npm finds a local manifest with a terminal build command, breaking the recursion. Added `@vitejs/plugin-react` to the client dependencies. Renamed `client/vitisconfig.js` to `client/vite.config.js` so Vite correctly detects and loads the config file.

### Changes
- **Deleted** `client/project.json`
- **Deleted** `client/vitisconfig.js`
- **Created** `client/package.json`
- **Created** `client/vite.config.js`

### Context
- **Deployment**: [#5d7dd8](https://railway.com/project/28118893-85d7-4b41-98aa-09a91122f9af/environment/5486bb3e-44df-4db2-b039-40bb3b934387/deployment/5d7dd87a-4e26-451a-ac7b-c87a0d8d5296)

author: stardust1508
body:
## Why
Reported on prod (duel 02bd9a42, 2026-05-05): every user message in a PvE duel rendered TWICE. User wrote \"начнем\" once, saw two bubbles. Visible regression.

## Root cause
Not in dedup logic — the call site. WS handler at \`pvp/duel/[id]/page.tsx\` case \`duel.message\` built the addMessage payload from text/role/round but **dropped** the dedup keys from the echo:

\`\`\`tsx
// PRE-FIX:
store.addMessage({ id, sender_role, text, round, timestamp });
// → no client_msg_id → cannot match the optimistic pending row → append.
\`\`\`

Backend was correct ([ws/pvp.py:1996-1997](apps/api/app/ws/pvp.py:1996)) — emits both client_msg_id and server_msg_id. Store dedup ([usePvPStore.ts:219-240](apps/web/src/stores/usePvPStore.ts:219)) was correct. Only the FE handler was the leak.

## Fix
Forward client_msg_id and server_msg_id in the echo handler. 9-line change.

## Tests
New \`usePvPStore.dedup.test.ts\` (4 cases) pins the reconcile rules:
- upgrade optimistic pending row by client_msg_id
- append when echo has no client_msg_id (reproduces the exact prod bug)
- drop duplicate echoes by server_msg_id (reconnect-resume race)
- bot replies without client_msg_id append cleanly

19 passed across the store __tests__ surface.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] After deploy: open a PvE duel, write \"начнем\" → exactly ONE bubble (not two)
- [ ] Bot reply still appears as a separate bubble

## Why now
Bug predates PR-1; became visible only after PR-1.5 fixed the UUID-key TypeError that was killing every PvE duel before any echo could even arrive. With the bot now actually replying, this dedup gap surfaced.

Adds BPM stepper buttons (±1) to the transport bar, making it easier to make fine-grained tempo adjustments on mobile and tablet devices. Also exposes the Settings panel on all viewport widths (previously hidden on wider screens).

## Changes

- **Transport Bar**: Added ± buttons next to BPM input for quick increments/decrements
- **Settings Visibility**: Now visible on all viewports (desktop, tablet, mobile)

- **Test Coverage**: All 75 tests passing

- BPM range: 60–200 BPM (clamped)
- Hold delay: 400ms before repeat (prevents accidental rapid changes)
- Repeat interval: 80ms when held
- Mobile touch target: 44×44px minimum
- Responsive adjustments for tight layouts (320px, 375px iPhone)

✅ Follows DESIGN.md color tokens (bone, bone-darker, te-orange)

### 💡 What
Added missing ARIA attributes to the dynamically generated tab buttons in the main navigation bar. This ensures that screen readers can correctly understand the elements as tabs, identify their active state, and link them to their respective panels.

### 🎯 Why
While the layout had `role="tabpanel"` structures with `aria-labelledby` referencing specific IDs, those corresponding ID definitions, roles, and state toggles were completely absent from the actual generated buttons in JavaScript. Screen readers were unable to properly interpret the navigation logic.

### ♿ Accessibility
- Added `role="tab"` to correctly identify elements.
- Associated tabs to their containers via `id` and `aria-controls`.
- Managed `aria-selected` dynamically so the active states are audibly announced to users.

## 🚨 Bug runtime introdotto da PR #30

L'utente segnala in produzione:
```
ReferenceError: COLUMNS is not defined
  at FETab (...)
```

PR #31 aveva risolto solo i 4 ref runtime di `GenericTab` a S1/S2/S3EditModal e FETab. Mancavano altre 5 costanti.

## Identifier rotti (audit completo)

Eseguito audit metodico cercando **tutti** gli identifier dichiarati in `shared.jsx` ma usati nei file consumer senza essere esportati via `G.DM`:

| Identifier | Dichiarato | Usato | Era esportato? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `COLUMNS` | shared:561 | tabs:778 (FETab) | ❌ |
| `calcResult` | shared:473 | scopeModals:178, :349 (S2/S3EditModal calc panel) | ❌ |
| `errBox` | shared:478 | scopeModals:183, :358 | ❌ |
| `warnBox` | shared:482 | scopeModals:184, :359 | ❌ |
| `btnRow` | shared:486 | scopeModals:185, :360 (Save/Cancel row) | ❌ |

## Fix

- `shared.jsx`: aggiunti i 5 identifier all'`Object.assign(G.DM, {...})`
- `tabs.jsx`: aggiunto `COLUMNS` al destructuring
- `scopeModals.jsx`: aggiunti `calcResult, errBox, warnBox, btnRow` al destructuring

## Aggiunto Playwright come devDependency

Approfittando del fix, aggiunto `@playwright/test@1.50.1` a `devDependencies` (no test scritti ancora — quelli arrivano in PR follow-up). Zero impatto su CI/build attuali (è devDependency).

## Verifica

| Caso | Esito |
|---|---|
| `npm test` | ✅ 67/67 verdi |
| Build | ✅ 1 055 KB |
| `npm run lint` | ✅ 0 errors, 13 warnings (sotto soglia 50, baseline) |
| `npm run lint:no-dangerous-html` | ✅ pulito |
| Audit identifier | ✅ tutti i 5 importati correttamente |

## Test plan post-merge

Hard reload in incognito, poi:
- Gestione Dati → **FE**: si apre senza `ReferenceError: COLUMNS`
- Gestione Dati → **S1**: si apre + click "+ aggiungi" apre S1EditModal funzionante
- Gestione Dati → **S2**: idem
- Gestione Dati → **S3**: idem
- DevTools console: nessun errore

## Lesson learned

Splitting di file con dipendenze incrociate non è un'operazione meccanica. Serve:
- Audit identifier statici (questo PR)
- Smoke test runtime in browser (in arrivo come PR follow-up — Playwright)
- Possibile rule ESLint custom per cross-IIFE refs (oggi ESLint non li coglie perché ogni IIFE è scope a sé)

author: eskp
body:
## Summary

Fixes [KEEP-431](https://linear.app/keeperhubapp/issue/KEEP-431/fix-keep-398-step-completion-tracker-fix-didnt-reach-the-x402-call). PRs #1103/#1110 added DB-backed cross-process step-success authority via `output_raw` and a post-drain reconciler, but two gaps left the x402/`call_workflow` path failing on large fan-in workflows where direct `execute_workflow` succeeded:

- `logWorkflowCompleteDb` reconciliation counted raw error/running rows. Under cross-pod SDK checkpoint resume, a step that already succeeded on pod A can be re-fired on pod B, leaving an orphan `running` row from the interrupted retry. The original success row is intact, but the orphan running row blocked the spurious-error-to-success override. Switch to per-nodeId aggregation: a node truly failed only if it has no success row anywhere.
- `executor.workflow.ts` in-catch spurious recovery used only the in-process tracker via `getSuccessfulSteps`. The tracker is empty on a fresh pod, leaving cross-pod recovery dependent on the post-drain pass. Switch to `getCompletedStepOutput` so the in-catch fast path matches the post-drain reconciler: tracker hit when same-process, DB fallback when cross-pod.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm type-check` clean
- [x] `pnpm vitest run` 4214 passed, 0 failed
- [x] New `tests/unit/executor-in-catch-db-fallback.test.ts` exercises the tracker fast path, x402 cross-pod recovery, and negative/falsy edge cases
- [x] Updated `tests/integration/workflow-logging.test.ts` covers per-nodeId aggregation: success+running orphan, success+error from retry, mixed real-failure-plus-retry, KEEP-333 still preserved (running-only nodes flagged as real failure)
- [ ] Manual verification on staging once PR environment is up: re-run `defi-position-aggregator-ethereum` with 13 parallel reads via x402 `call_workflow` (failing repro: `6nq7kf1az9ku49hmjcrnc`); expect `status: success` with full output payload
- [ ] Confirm direct `execute_workflow` path still succeeds (no regression to working path)

author: caio-pizzol
body:
Stacked on #3151. Drains the fifth shim entry (`@superdoc/style-engine/ooxml`), bringing the count to 1. Only `@superdoc/common` remains.

The `/ooxml` subpath is the only part of style-engine publicly reachable - 10 dist d.ts references across pm-adapter, the diffing extension, super-converter, parts adapters, and plan-engine. The bare `@superdoc/style-engine` is internal-only.

Approach mirrors the pm-adapter narrow-scope pattern from #3144:

- Include only the `ooxml/**` subtree plus its sibling `cascade.ts` dependency in `vite.config.js`/`tsconfig.json`. A full `src/**/*` glob pulls the broader project graph through `@superdoc/contracts` project references and re-expands the shim list (verified during probe).
- Add an exact relocation rule for `@superdoc/style-engine/ooxml`.
- Guard the bare `@superdoc/style-engine` root in both `RELOCATION_GUARD_PACKAGES` and `UNSHIMMED_PRIVATE_SPECIFIERS` so a future bare-barrel leak fails audit Rule 1 instead of producing a broken relative path.

Also removes a misleading JSDoc `@example` block from `cascade.ts`. The example showed `import from '@superdoc/style-engine/cascade'`, but `cascade` is not in the package's `exports` field. Same false-positive class as the `useUiFontFamily` cleanup in #3140 - the bare specifier inside the `@example` was being captured by the workspace-import scanner.

**Verified**:
- `pnpm --filter superdoc build:es` clean (audit OK, 9 guarded packages, 1 shim module)
- Consumer matrix: 47 passed, 0 failed, 0 warnings
- Runtime smoke 4/4 against the freshly packed tarball
- Dist has the 6 expected declaration files: `cascade.d.ts`, `ooxml/{index,types,numbering-types,styles-types,table-style-selection}.d.ts`
- Negative tests: `import('@superdoc/style-engine/ooxml')` rewrites to a real target file in dist; `import('@superdoc/style-engine')` (bare) is preserved unchanged and audit Rule 1 fails with exit 1

After this lands, only `@superdoc/common` (5 dist refs, catch-all bin) remains. That's the hardest of the original 9 shims and needs per-type analysis (Comment, CommentJSON, CommentContent, CommentThreadingProfile - each gets an inline-vs-relocate-vs-remove decision).

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

All frontend API calls included a redundant `/api/` path prefix (e.g. `/api/auth/login`, `/api/dashboard`, `/api/projects`). Because the axios `baseURL` already points to the backend service root (`http://task-manager.railway.internal:8080`), and the FastAPI router mounts routes under `/api/auth`, `/api/dashboard`, etc., the requests were resolving to double-prefixed paths like `/api/api/auth/login` — which don't exist on the backend, causing every API call to fail and the app to show a blank "Application failed to respond" page.

## Solution

Removed the `/api` segment from every hardcoded path in `AuthContext.jsx`, `Dashboard.jsx`, `Projects.jsx`, and `ProjectDetail.jsx`. The paths now correctly match the backend router prefixes (e.g. `/auth/login`, `/dashboard`, `/projects`, `/tasks/:id`), so the axios baseURL combined with these paths resolves to the right endpoints without duplication.

### Changes
- **Modified** `frontend/src/context/AuthContext.jsx`
- **Modified** `frontend/src/pages/Dashboard.jsx`
- **Modified** `frontend/src/pages/Projects.jsx`
- **Modified** `frontend/src/pages/ProjectDetail.jsx`

author: franklinbaldo
body:
## Summary

Audit of `src/components/NavMenu.svelte` surfaced several bugs and non-idiomatic Svelte patterns; this rewrites the component.

### Issues found
- **Duplicate `id="main-nav-list"`**: the `{#if open} ... {:else} ...` block rendered two separate `<ul>` elements with the same id, producing invalid HTML and breaking the hamburger's `aria-controls` reference.
- **Whole menu unmounted/remounted on every toggle**, fighting Svelte's reactivity.
- **Resize bug**: `.drawer` styles were scoped to `@media (max-width: 768px)`, so opening the drawer on mobile and resizing to desktop left an unstyled open `<ul>` floating in the page.
- **Open state never reset across the breakpoint** — drawer state could resurface when shrinking back to mobile.
- **`astro:after-swap` stole focus** by re-focusing the hamburger on every page navigation.
- Focus-trap / outside-click handlers ran unconditionally, even on desktop where there is no drawer.
- JS-driven `transition:slide` was heavier than necessary.

### Fix
- Single `<ul id="main-nav-list">` rendered always; drawer state expressed via `class:drawer` / `class:open` plus `inert` for the closed-on-mobile case.
- Viewport tracked with `matchMedia('(max-width: 768px)')`; crossing into desktop forces `open = false`.
- All mobile-only behavior (escape, focus-trap, outside-click, focus first link on open) is gated on a `$derived` `drawerOpen`.
- `astro:after-swap` collapses the drawer without stealing focus.
- Slide replaced by CSS `transform`/`opacity` transition, with a `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback.
- `aria-current="page"` added for the active route; hamburger label flips between "Open navigation" / "Close navigation".

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run check` — 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- [x] `npm run test:unit` — 1023 tests pass.
- [ ] Manual: toggle drawer on mobile viewport, resize between mobile/desktop while open, verify focus trap with Tab/Shift+Tab, Escape closes and returns focus to hamburger, page navigation closes drawer without stealing focus.

author: laboef1900
body:
## Summary

User-visible payoff for the trial system shipped in `compendiq-ee#158` (CQEE1 parser + `/api/license/info`). A banner appears above the page chrome whenever the active license is a trial:

- **`> 7` days remaining** → subtle info: `Trial — N days remaining.`
- **1–7 days remaining** → warning: `Trial — only N day(s) left. Contact sales to keep enterprise features.`
- **`≤ 0` days remaining** → destructive: `Trial expired N day(s) ago — contact sales to upgrade.`

Negative-`daysRemaining` rendering depends on the EE-side change in `compendiq-ee#158` to *preserve* `expiresAt`/`daysRemaining` after a trial expires (rather than nulling them when `tier` downgrades to `community`). That coordination is intentional.

## Where it lives

- `frontend/src/shared/components/banners/TrialBanner.tsx`
- Mounted in `AppLayout.tsx` immediately after `<ServiceStatus />`, sharing the "between header and panels" slot. Same visual register, same horizontal padding.

## Graceful degradation

- `/api/license/info` 404 (CE deployment, no EE backend) → banner hidden silently.
- `type !== 'trial'` (paid or no key set) → banner hidden.
- Network error → banner hidden, no console noise.

## Why a separate fetch (vs reading from `EnterpriseProvider`)

`EnterpriseProvider` already fetches `/api/admin/license`, but that endpoint follows the canonical `LicenseInfoResponseSchema` from `@compendiq/contracts` — which doesn't expose `type` or `issuedAt`. Widening the contract for an EE-only concept would force a CE/contracts change with no CE-side benefit. Banner reads the EE-only `/api/license/info` instead and stays self-contained. Single-shot fetch on mount is correct because trial state changes at day granularity — a stale banner survives a page reload.

## Test plan

- [x] 10 new component tests in `TrialBanner.test.tsx`: 404, paid, community-no-key, > 7d active, 1≤n≤7 warning, 1-day singular, 0d expired, negative expired, 1-day-ago singular, network error.
- [x] `npm run typecheck` clean.
- [x] `npm run lint` clean (`--max-warnings=0`).
- [x] Full frontend suite still passes: **2078 / 2078 tests across 170 files**.

## Out of scope

- Showing the banner to non-admin users only — deliberately excluded. Trial expiration is a deployment-level fact every user benefits from seeing; gating it would surprise free-tier users on a trial deployment by hiding why their access changed.
- Internationalization. Strings are English only, matching the rest of the SPA.
- Dismiss/snooze. Trials are short-lived; any "x" button would be re-shown 24h later anyway.

body:
## Summary
First step on the v2.0 path. Today the admin preview iframe only refreshes on Save. After this:

- **postMessage protocol** with versioned envelope `{ kind: 'clear/preview/v1', op, ... }`. Handshake validates token + schema version + parent origin.
- **Hot-swap text** — every keystroke on text-typed fields (`text` / `textarea` / `string` widgets) propagates to the iframe via debounced (100ms) `op:'patch'`; consumer swaps `textContent`. No save required.
- **Click-to-edit** — clicking a wrapped node in the iframe sends `op:'focus'` to admin → editor scrolls + focuses the matching input.
- **Graceful fallback** — schema-version mismatch latches save-then-reload mode for the session; topbar dot turns amber.
- **Adopter opt-in** — `previewFieldAttrs(url)` helper in `@clearcms/astro` returns `{ data-clear-field }` attrs in preview mode, `{}` otherwise. Plus a `<script>import '@clearcms/astro/preview-client'</script>` line. Scaffolder template updated.

Out of scope (v1.1+): richtext live update, image swap, structured-field popovers, two-way bind.

## Test plan
- [x] +27 admin tests, +15 astro tests (537 total, 0 failures).
- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — 0 errors across 12 packages.
- [x] Protocol envelope guard rejects mismatched `kind`; debouncing verified; click round-trip verified.

## Notes
- Schema-version digest uses FNV-1a (32-bit, sync) instead of sha256 (async). Collisions are harmless (operator hits Save+reload).

author: extratoast
body:
## Summary

Two distinct bugs surfaced during the live install, both rooted in the `/api/*` routing.

### 1. Every anonymous `/api/*` call returned 401 (and `/api` itself returned 503 transiently)

The api IngressRoute's catch-all rule was deliberately set up *not* to strip `/api` (comment: "Plain REST /api/* without strip, priority 50"), but **every controller in the api is mapped at root paths** — `/health`, `/events`, `/csrf`, `/contributionPeriods`, etc. Only two outliers had `/api` in their `@RequestMapping`:

- `MainController` registered both `/health` AND `/api/health` as a defensive alias.
- `MyServicesController` lived at `/api/me/services`.

Result: `https://v2.esa-blueshell.nl/api/events` arrived at the api as `/api/events`, no controller matched, the `SecurityFilterChain` saw it didn't match any `requestMatchers().permitAll()` entry (which list root paths), `anyRequest().authenticated()` fired, **401 to every anonymous caller**. The 503 was Traefik returning empty-backend during the brief rollout window triggered by PR #172.

This PR makes the assumption uniform: strip `/api` everywhere, every controller stays at root paths.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/edge/ingressroutes/api.yaml` | Add `strip-api-prefix` middleware to the catch-all route. Comment rewritten. |
| `services/api/.../MyServicesController.kt` | `@RequestMapping("/api/me/services")` → `/me/services` |
| `services/api/.../MainController.kt` | `@GetMapping(["/health", "/api/health"])` → `/health` (alias no longer needed; k8s probes are tcpSocket, Gatus probe `/api/health` arrives as `/health` after strip) |
| `services/api/.../SecurityConfig.kt` | Drop the now-redundant `/api/me/services` from permitAll |

Externally everything still lives at `https://v2.esa-blueshell.nl/api/...` — the strip happens on the Traefik hop only.

### 2. Gatus's Traefik probe always failed

Probe target was `http://traefik.ingress-system.svc.cluster.local:9000/ping`. **Chart 39.x dropped the separate `:9000` named port** — the dashboard, API, and `--ping=true` healthcheck all share the `traefik` named port, exposed on the K8s Service as `8080`. Switch the probe URL + update the corresponding comments in the Traefik HelmRelease.

### Aside

`.cf_token` is now gitignored (operator-local Cloudflare token file from the seed-vault-from-env flow, same shape as `.ghcr_token`).

## Test plan
- [x] `kubectl kustomize` clean for every overlay
- [x] `./gradlew :services:api:compileKotlin` BUILD SUCCESSFUL
- [ ] CI green
- [ ] Live: after merge + image build + rollout
  - `curl https://v2.esa-blueshell.nl/api/health` → 200
  - `curl https://v2.esa-blueshell.nl/api/me/services` → 200 (anonymous, returns the public `MyApps` catalog)
  - Gatus "Blueshell API" → green
  - Gatus "Traefik Dashboard" → green

author: szhygulin
body:
Closes #100.

## Summary

Across-dispatch fail-fast for non-clean exits. When a coding-agent run finishes without a clean implement (no envelope, `decision="error"`, or SDK truncation), the orchestrator posts a structured `## vp-dev failure post-mortem` comment on the GitHub issue. The triage gate on the next `vp-dev run` reads that comment deterministically and marks the issue `ready: false` until a human posts a resolution signal (`retry`, `fix landed`, `scope changed`, `unblock`, `proceed`) or the operator passes `--include-non-ready`.

Issue #34 burned ~$8.30 across two re-dispatches of a 9-file plan before the user manually noticed and split it. This gate makes that loop deterministic-prevented.

## Files

- `src/orchestrator/failurePostMortem.ts` (new) — `composeFailurePostMortem()` (Markdown body) + `detectPendingPostMortem()` (sentinel + resolution-keyword scan). Sentinel is `^## vp-dev failure post-mortem` (case-insensitive, line-anchored — quoted text inside other comments cannot trigger).
- `src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts` — call site in `runOneIssue` after the run-state entry settles. Skipped in dry-run; failure to post logs `orchestrator.post_mortem_failed` but does not abort the run.
- `src/orchestrator/triage.ts` — deterministic pre-model gate in `triageOne`. Saves the LLM call when the post-mortem is pending.
- `src/github/gh.ts` — `postIssueComment(targetRepo, issueId, body)` helper (uses `--body-file` via tmp file for safe Markdown handling).
- `src/orchestrator/failurePostMortem.test.ts` (new) — 13 unit tests: sentinel anchoring, case-insensitive detection, resolution-keyword recognition (single + multi-word), second-post-mortem-doesn't-resolve-the-first, ambient-comment doesn't lift the gate, multi-paragraph post-mortem detection.

## Behavior change

**Before**: Agent fails on #N → state JSON records it, partial branch pushed → next run re-dispatches #N → fails again → repeat.

**After**: Agent fails on #N → state JSON records it → orchestrator posts post-mortem on the issue → next run's triage detects the comment, returns `ready: false` with reason `awaiting human review of prior failure post-mortem (run-XXX)`, surfaced in the preview's `triageSkipped` block. Human posts a resolution comment or passes `--include-non-ready` to override.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — clean.
- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- [x] `npm test` — 98/98 passing (13 new + 85 existing).
- [ ] End-to-end: a `vp-dev run` against an issue with a simulated `error_max_turns` failure posts the comment and the next run's preview lists the issue under `triageSkipped`.

author: ivaylodimitrov-cmyk
body:
## Summary
- Pin `postgres:latest` to `postgres:17` in `services/postgres/service.yml`
- Postgres 18+ changed the volume layout (mount must be `/var/lib/postgresql`, not `/var/lib/postgresql/data`), which breaks the existing `${POSTGRES_HOME}` data and causes the container to refuse to start
- Pinning keeps existing dev data working without a `pg_upgrade` migration

## Future migration to 18+
If we want to bump later, two changes are required together:
1. Change the mount in `services/postgres/service.yml` from `:/var/lib/postgresql/data` to `:/var/lib/postgresql`
2. Migrate the existing `${POSTGRES_HOME}` data via `pg_upgrade --link` (see https://github.com/docker-library/postgres/issues/37) — or wipe `${POSTGRES_HOME}` for a fresh init if dev data is disposable

## Test plan

author: szhygulin
body:
Closes #98.

## Summary

The coding agent's main pass (`runCodingAgent()` pass 1) had a hardcoded `maxTurns: 50` that indirectly bounded cost — it fired at a less-meaningful boundary than what we actually want to limit. Issue #34's 9-file plan twice hit `error_max_turns` mid-edit despite making forward progress, burning ~$8.30 total with no recovered work.

Now that [PR #93](https://github.com/szhygulin/vaultpilot-development-agents/pull/93) shipped `RunCostTracker` and the SDK exposes `maxBudgetUsd` on `query()`, replace the turn cap with a cost-shaped one.

## Changes

- **`src/agent/codingAgent.ts`**:
  - Drop `maxTurns: 50` from pass 1. The SDK now runs uncapped on turns and hard-stops on cost via `error_max_budget_usd`.
  - Plumb `maxBudgetUsd: input.costTracker?.remainingBudget()` to all three `runSdkPass()` calls (pass 1, recovery 2a, recovery 2b). Each pass reads the tracker at dispatch time so it sees the budget actually left after prior passes forwarded their cost.
  - Extend the truncation-recovery trigger from `errorSubtype === "error_max_turns"` to also fire on `error_max_budget_usd` — the recovery flow records a structured envelope regardless of which ceiling tripped it. Recovery passes' `maxTurns` (2a: 1, 2b: 4) stay; they're decision-bounded by design.

- **`src/util/costTracker.ts`**:
  - Add `budgetUsd` constructor argument (optional) and stash it as `readonly budgetUsd`. Defensive: NaN / Infinity / negative reduce to `undefined`.
  - Add `remainingBudget()` — returns `budgetUsd - accumulated` clamped to `>= 0`, or `undefined` when no budget was configured. The clamp matters because the SDK rejects negative budgets; returning 0 lets the SDK exit immediately on the next dispatch with `error_max_budget_usd`.

- **`src/cli.ts`**: Pass `budgetUsd` to the `RunCostTracker` constructor.

- **`src/util/costTracker.test.ts`**: 7 new tests covering `budgetUsd` accessor (undefined / value / malformed / zero), `remainingBudget()` behavior (no-budget / accumulating / exhausted / zero-budget).

## Behavior

- **No budget set** (`--max-cost-usd` absent, `VP_DEV_MAX_COST_USD` unset): `remainingBudget()` returns `undefined`, the SDK runs uncapped on cost — same shape as the pre-#98 main pass minus the turn ceiling.
- **Budget set, sufficient headroom**: agent runs to completion or natural envelope emit; turn count no longer matters.
- **Budget exhausted mid-pass-1**: SDK exits with `error_max_budget_usd`; truncation-recovery fires (same shape as `error_max_turns` recovery), pass 2a captures a structured `decision: "error"` envelope, pass 2b best-effort salvages in-flight work.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` clean
- [x] `npm test` — 93 tests pass (7 new in `costTracker.test.ts`)
- [ ] Smoke: `vp-dev run --max-cost-usd 5.0 --target-repo X --issues N` against an issue whose work would have hit `error_max_turns` under the old cap; agent runs to completion or until cost ceiling exhausts.
- [ ] Smoke: `vp-dev run` without `--max-cost-usd`; agent runs uncapped on both turns and cost.

— Cook (agent-fe90)

author: comtihon
body:
`workflows.py::_stream_graph` (used by /approve, /reject, start_run, retry) wired up `runner.graph.astream(...)` without setting `runner._current_run` and `runner._current_run_repository`. The node-body helpers `_wrap_with_status_running` and `_save_conv_id` read those attributes — so when the runner had been previously bound to a different `run` object (typically by `stream_graph_to_pause` during the post-restart recovery path), the helpers' saves wrote the *stale* run's state on top of the live one mid-stream.

Observable symptom: a run that hit ask_context, paused, was recovered on pod restart, then had its ask_context interrupt resolved by the user POSTing /approve. The status flipped back to waiting_approval mid-stream because the wrapper kept persisting the recovery's stale run object (which had status=waiting_approval / current_step= ask_context_step). The UI re-read step_outputs.__interrupt__ and showed the user the same questions again, even though gather_context was actually re-running with the new answers in the background.

Fix: set `runner._current_run = run` and `_current_run_repository = container.run_repository` at the top of `_stream_graph`, mirroring what `yaml_graph.py::stream_graph_to_pause` already does. This binds each invocation to its own run and prevents cross-invocation drift.

Test: `tests/test_graphs_api.py::test_stream_graph_rebinds_runner_to_ current_run` pre-pollutes the runner with a stale binding (mimicking recovery), invokes _stream_graph with a fresh run, and asserts the runner now points at the fresh run. Pins the contract so a future refactor can't quietly reintroduce the drift.
