## Summary

Finishes the v3.2 review-performance and hardening slice on top of the merged v3.1 baseline.

This PR tightens `pr-review` cleanup/cache safety, keeps Python and deployment-topology coverage in the temp-index review path, improves indexing hot paths, and normalizes checked-in diagnostics and fixtures so warnings, comments, and benchmark artifacts stay neutral.

## Context / Motivation

The v3.0 and v3.1 review found that the newer `pr-review` path could drift from the main indexer surface unless Python and deployment topology were explicitly covered end-to-end. The same pass also found cleanup/cache edge cases, grammar issues in diagnostics, and a few repo-wide fixtures that looked like local or sensitive-looking data.

## Key Decisions

- Keep `redb` as the graph-store backend.
- Add a checked-in root `gather-step.config.yaml` so this repo can self-review without a manual config override.
- Treat missing graph schema stamps as implicit v0 for the v3.1/v3.2 baseline, while still rejecting future stamped versions with typed schema errors.
- Move projection and git-classification regexes to module-level lazy statics instead of pursuing larger v3.3-only parser/storage refactors.
- Preserve full unmapped error chains in CLI fallback formatting; unmapped errors may now print their cause chain instead of only the top-level message.
- Rename the local benchmark convention from "private corpus" to "external corpus" and keep real paths/results gitignored.

## Files Changed

| Area | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| `crates/gather-step-cli/src/commands/pr_review.rs` | Added Python plus deployment temp-index regression coverage, config/default cache behavior fixes, marker access handling, and polished diagnostics. |

| `crates/gather-step-parser/src/projection.rs`, `crates/gather-step-git/src/classify.rs` | Promoted repeated regex construction into reusable lazy statics. |
| `crates/gather-step-analysis/src/projection_impact.rs` | Reduced repeated dotted-field string allocation in projection matching. |
| `crates/gather-step-storage/*` | Added graph schema policy tests, tightened watcher/indexer fixture text, and simplified a clippy-flagged search-store helper. |
| `benchmark/`, `gather-step.config.yaml`, docs fixtures | Added self-review config and normalized benchmark/test fixture strings away from local paths and sensitive-looking placeholders. Existing README, Cargo authors, MIT license, and JJ Adonis website credits are preserved. |

author: justinf555
body:
## Summary
Both \`PhotoViewer\` and \`VideoViewer\` live in an \`AdwNavigationView\` and are *popped*, not disposed, when the user backs out to the grid. The underlying widgets keep whatever they were last displaying alive — for the photo viewer that's the decoded RGBA full-res buffer (50–200 MB; RAW from a 50 MP sensor lands at the high end), plus the edit panel's preview image and render output if edit-mode was active. For the video viewer it's the GStreamer pipeline, including demuxer buffers.

This wires \`connect_hidden\` on each viewer to drop those resources after the pop animation completes:
- \`PhotoViewer\` clears \`imp.picture\`'s paintable, and calls \`EditPanel::end_session\` (which already cancels the debounced save and drops the \`EditSession\`).
- \`VideoViewer\` clears \`imp.video\`'s file, which tears the GStreamer pipeline down.

## Verification
Diagnosed via \`dhat-rs\` heap profiler. Before the fix: ~70 MB sat live the entire run after viewing one RAW; with the fix that buffer is freed within ~200 ms of pressing back. \`htop\` RSS visibly drops 100+ MB on viewer close.

## Test plan
- [ ] Open a large RAW in the viewer, back out to the grid. Confirm RSS in htop drops by the decoded-image size (≥ 50 MB for typical photos, 100–200 MB for RAW).
- [ ] Open a video, back out to the grid. Confirm playback stops and audio device is released (no continued sound from a torn-down pipeline).
- [ ] Open a photo, enter edit mode, back out without toggling edit off. Re-enter the same photo: edit mode should re-initialize cleanly with no stale state, and the previous session's debounced save (if any) should have flushed.
- [ ] Navigate prev/next within the viewer (existing path that replaces the paintable). Should be unaffected.

author: pjm17971
body:
_Posted by the gRPC experiment agent (Claude)_

Doc-only PR. Records the V6→V7 profile delta from PR #18 and turns
the perf regression into a concrete library ask.

## Why

PR #18 ($\text{V7 } \texttt{samples()}$ migration) shipped with a real perf gap vs V6
at the ceiling regime: −19% throughput, +17% heap at 87k/s. The
PR body posited three suspects but didn't profile-diff them. This
doc closes that loop.

## What it says (one paragraph)

The regression isn't `samples()`. It's the second
`LivePartitionedSyncRolling`. Every per-event pond hop roughly
doubled inclusive-time (`#routeEvent` 15.0% → 28.9%, `ingest` 11.5% →
25.0%, `_pushTrustedEvents` 13.1% → 27.4%). The reducer itself is
~2.3% self-time across all three of its source files — fine. User-
code self-time dropped 88% as expected (manual deque + slice trim
were real cost), but pond pays it all back and more on the doubled
ingest path.

## What falls out for the library agent

A **fused multi-window rolling** would close the doubled-ingest cost
and most of the heap delta:

```ts
byHost.rolling([
  { window: '1m',    output: { cpu_avg: 'avg', cpu_sd: 'stdev', cpu_n: 'count' } },
  { window: '200ms', output: { cpu_samples: 'samples' } },
], { trigger });
```

Two smaller side notes in the doc: `#evictPartition` is unexpectedly
hot at ceiling (8.8% self-time, new in the V7 top-25) and worth a
look; `samples()` itself is fine and doesn't need optimisation
pressure.

## Reproducer

In the doc — checkout `a030c6c` in a worktree, copy the generated
`grpc/events.ts` across (it's git-ignored), run `profile-agg.ts`
with `--profDir=/tmp/agg-prof-v6`. Then `pnpm perf` on `main` for
V7. Both at `--P=1000 --N=1000 --seconds=20` to match.

## Test plan

- [x] No code changes, no tests to run
- [x] Doc renders on GitHub

author: osamaadeel
body:
… CHAR/BYTE size specifiers

The Oracle exporter (and the OFSAA toolkit in particular) emits CREATE TABLE statements with everything double-quoted and PKs wrapped in a named CONSTRAINT clause. The previous parser failed three things:

1. The CREATE TABLE regex required a bare table name, so quoted forms like `CREATE TABLE "FCT_OPS_RISK_DATA"` weren't stripped — the entire body collapsed into one un-parseable line ("No columns parsed from this DDL").
2. `CONSTRAINT "PK_1881" PRIMARY KEY ("A", "B") USING INDEX ENABLE` was silently skipped, so composite PKs from real exports lost their PK marking even when the columns themselves parsed.
3. `VARCHAR2(3 CHAR)` / `VARCHAR2(120 BYTE)` size specifiers broke the column regex's size capture, dropping the length silently.

Adds a parser test file with 9 cases — including a reproduction of the full FCT_OPS_RISK_DATA DDL the user reported.

author: dalkia
body:
## Summary
- When a worker received `SIGTERM` mid-conversion (e.g. rolling deploy, autoscale-down), the SQS message stayed invisible for the full **3h visibility timeout** (`task-queue.ts:112,129`) before another worker could pick it up — the conversion was effectively lost for hours even with idle capacity available.
- The consumer-server had no signal handlers and `consumeAndProcessJob`'s `finally`-based delete never ran when the process was killed, so neither delete nor NACK happened.
- This PR adds `releaseInFlight()` on the task queue: it tracks the in-flight message and, on shutdown, calls `ChangeMessageVisibility(VisibilityTimeout: 0)` to return it to the queue immediately. `SIGTERM` and `SIGINT` handlers in `service.ts` invoke it (with a 5s timeout). Hard kills (SIGKILL/OOM) still fall back to the visibility timeout — unchanged.

## Changes
- `consumer-server/src/adapters/task-queue.ts` — interface gains `releaseInFlight()`. SQS adapter tracks `inFlight` via closure; `releaseInFlight()` calls `changeMessageVisibility(0)`. The `finally` skips `deleteMessage` if the message was already released so we don't ack a NACKed job. Memory adapter has a no-op. New `job_queue_releases_total` metric for observability.
- `consumer-server/src/service.ts` — `process.once('SIGTERM' | 'SIGINT')` handlers race the release against a 5s timeout. `SIGTERM` is also caught by Lifecycle's built-in handler (which stops components in parallel) — the two don't conflict.
- `consumer-server/test/unit/task-queue.spec.ts` — 5 new tests for the SQS adapter: release path skips delete, success path deletes, no-op when nothing in-flight, idempotent on repeated calls, tolerates AWS errors.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` passes
- [x] `npx eslint src/adapters/task-queue.ts src/service.ts` passes
- [x] `npx jest --forceExit` — 7/7 tests pass (5 new + 2 existing)
- [ ] Manual: send `SIGTERM` to a staging worker mid-conversion; confirm `job_queue_releases_total` increments and the message is picked up by another worker within seconds (not hours)
- [ ] Manual: confirm successful conversions still delete normally (no spurious release on the success path)

author: jiahui-gu
body:
## Summary

Wave 1 / 3 dev — renderer side. Replaces the legacy preload-installed
`window.ccsm` IPC bridge with a renderer-resident compatibility shim
that POSTs every call to the local daemon over loopback HTTP. **None
of the 28 existing `window.ccsm.X(...)` call sites are touched** —
they keep using the same surface, the underlying transport changes
out from under them.

Task #567

## Files

| file | role |
| --- | --- |
| `src/lib/daemon-port.ts` | NEW — caches the daemon port from `window.__getDaemonPort()` (preload bridge owned by wave-1 dev-B). |
| `src/lib/daemon-client.ts` | NEW — thin POST wrapper, uniform `{args}` / `{result}` envelope, single `'daemon offline: ...'` failure mode. |
| `src/lib/window-ccsm-shim.ts` | NEW — implements the legacy `CcsmApi`. Pre-fetches sync property `window.platform` at install time. Event subscriptions are no-op stubs (see follow-up). |
| `src/index.tsx` | MODIFY — `await installCcsmShim()` before `root.render()` so `<DragRegion>` reads of `window.ccsm?.window.platform` are safe on first render. |
| `src/global.d.ts` | MODIFY — drops the inline `window.ccsm` typing in favour of `CcsmApi` re-exported from the shim; adds `__getDaemonPort`. |
| `src/pty.d.ts`, `src/session.d.ts` | MODIFY — minor commentary; `ccsmSession` flipped to optional for symmetry. `ccsmPty` stays non-optional to avoid touching `src/terminal/*` (out of scope). |
| `eslint.config.js` | MODIFY — adds `fetch`/`Response`/`Request`/`Headers` to renderer globals. |

## Mapping rule (channel → endpoint)

```
window.ccsm.X(arg1, arg2, ...)         → POST /api/X
window.ccsm.window.minimize()           → POST /api/window/minimize
window.ccsm.userCwds.get()              → POST /api/userCwds/get
window.ccsm.i18n.setLanguage(l)         → POST /api/i18n/setLanguage  (event-style)
window.ccsm.i18n.getSystemLocale()      → POST /api/i18n/getSystemLocale

Body:    { args: [arg1, arg2, ...] }
Resp:    { result: <T> }   (HTTP 200)
         OR { error: '...' }  (HTTP non-2xx → throw new Error(error))
         OR HTTP 204 No Content (events) → resolves undefined

Event channels (from spec — no .send() callers exist in src today,
but the convention is wired so wave 2 can plug them in):
   '<channel>'  → POST /api/event/<channel>   body { args: [...] }
   e.g. 'set-language' → POST /api/event/set-language
```

The `set-language` event path is already exercised by the shim's
`i18n.setLanguage` (matches the original ipcRenderer.send shape: a
one-way fire-and-forget). The other three event channels listed in
the spec (`session:setActive`, `notify:userInput`, `session:setName`)
have **no current `ipcRenderer.send` call sites in `src/`** — they're
either gone or never landed in this branch — so no shim wiring was
needed for them. `daemonEvent(channel, args)` is exported from
`daemon-client.ts` for any future caller.

## Shim API

`CcsmApi` (exported from `src/lib/window-ccsm-shim.ts`, re-typed into
`window.ccsm` via `src/global.d.ts`) is byte-for-byte the same surface
as the pre-refactor inline `window.ccsm` typing. Three categories:

1. **async methods** (most of them) — each translates to a single
   POST. Examples: `loadState`, `saveState`, `getVersion`,
   `scanImportable`, `pickCwd`, `pathsExist`, `updatesCheck`, etc.
2. **sync property** — `window.ccsm.window.platform`. Pre-fetched in
   `installCcsmShim()` so React render reads see a real string. If
   the daemon is offline at boot, falls back to a
   `navigator.userAgent`-derived guess (the only consumer branches on
   `=== 'darwin'`, so the worst-case is showing the Windows-style 8px
   drag strip until the user reloads with the daemon up).
3. **event subscriptions** — `onUpdateStatus`, `onUpdateDownloaded`,
   `onMaximizedChanged`, `onBeforeHide`, `onAfterShow`. v0.3 has no
   daemon→renderer push channel yet, so these install **no-op
   handlers and return a no-op unsubscribe**. The renderer keeps
   working: Updates pane shows the last polled status, the maximize
   button just doesn't auto-flip until the user clicks again.
   **Wave-2 follow-up**: wire SSE / WebSocket from daemon and replace
   the stubs.

## Failure mode

`installCcsmShim()` is wrapped in try/catch internally:
- `__getDaemonPort()` missing → fallback platform, all methods throw
  `'daemon offline: window.__getDaemonPort preload bridge missing'`.
- `__getDaemonPort()` rejects / returns junk → fallback platform,
  methods throw `'daemon offline: invalid port ...'`.
- Daemon up but `/api/window/platform` unreachable → fallback
  platform, async methods that the user actually triggers throw
  `'daemon offline: <fetch error>'`.

Acceptance: **never silent fail**. Every renderer-visible failure
from the shim surfaces as a thrown Error whose message starts with
`daemon offline:` (single recognizable prefix for telemetry).

## Call-site audit

```
$ grep -rn 'window\.ccsm[\?\.]' src | grep -v 'window\.ccsm\(Pty\|Session\)' | wc -l
37   # incl comments and chained reads (window.ccsm.window.platform counts twice)

$ grep -rn 'window\.ccsm\?\?\.\|window\.ccsm\.' src | grep -v ccsmPty | grep -v ccsmSession
   # 28 unique runtime call sites across stores/, components/, app-effects/, agent/, App.tsx
```

**Zero** of those 28 call sites are modified by this PR. Spot-check
files: `src/stores/persist.ts`, `src/stores/drafts.ts`,
`src/stores/store.ts`, `src/components/settings/UpdatesPane.tsx`,
`src/components/settings/AppearancePane.tsx`,
`src/components/settings/NotificationsPane.tsx`,
`src/components/Sidebar.tsx`, `src/components/AppSkeleton.tsx`,
`src/components/WindowControls.tsx`, `src/components/ImportDialog.tsx`,
`src/app-effects/useExitAnimation.ts`,
`src/app-effects/useHydrateSystemLocale.ts`,
`src/app-effects/useUpdateDownloadedBridge.ts`,
`src/stores/slices/sessionCrudSlice.ts` — none of these appear in the diff.

## Out-of-scope (per spec)

Untouched: `src/components/*`, `src/agent/*`, `src/app-effects/*`
(beyond consuming the shim transparently), `src/stores/*`,
`src/terminal/*`, `daemon/*`, `electron/*`. The wave-1 dev-B preload
that installs `window.__getDaemonPort` is also out of scope and
expected to land in parallel.

## Local checks (host: Windows 11, mode: fast)

- lint: ✓ (exit 0, 91 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors)
- typecheck: ✓ (exit 0, both `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.electron.json`)
- build: ✓ (exit 0, webpack production + tsc electron)
- unit tests: skipped — no existing spec touches `window.ccsm` /
  `installCcsmShim` / `daemon-port` / `daemon-client` (verified via
  `grep -l` across `src` and `tests`). New shim code is exercised
  end-to-end by the renderer at boot; CI three-platform matrix will
  cover the integration path once wave-1 dev-B's preload lands.
- e2e: skipped, mode rationale — current e2e harnesses run Electron
  without the v0.3 daemon up, so post-refactor they would see the
  intentional `daemon offline` failure mode for every persisted
  state read. e2e validation is gated on the wave-2 daemon being
  reachable from the harness; the wave-2 PR will revive e2e.

## Reverse-verify

N/A — not a bug fix.

### Changes
- Add `#include <lemon/network_simplex.h>` to the bundled wrapper  
- Expose `NetworkSimplex<ListDigraph, int, int>` as `NetworkSimplexListDigraphIntInt`  
- Bind the following methods:
  - Constructor from `ListDigraph`
  - `lowerMap`
  - `upperMap`
  - `costMap`
  - `supplyMap`
  - `stSupply`
  - `reset`
  - `resetParams`
  - `run`
  - `totalCost`
  - `flow`
  - `potential`
- Expose integer helpers for `NetworkSimplex` problem types:
  - `INFEASIBLE`
  - `OPTIMAL`
  - `UNBOUNDED`
- Bump LEMON JLL recipe version from `1.3.4` to `1.3.5`

### Why
LEMONGraphs.jl already uses the bundled `liblemoncxxwrap` artifact for:
- Maximum-weight perfect matching  
- Dijkstra shortest paths  

`NetworkSimplex` is also available in upstream LEMON and is a natural next binding to expose. This keeps the wrapper incremental and directly supports a real downstream JuliaGraphs integration rather than adding unused surface area.

AI Disclosure: Used Codex 5.3, asked it to add Simplex methods and follow the structure of file. then manually verified methods by mapping them.

body:
## Summary
Re-add filter entry for `SocketApiTest.SocketTCPExtension` that was lost during a Chromium version update.

**Note: This is a Chromium test** (located in `src/chrome/browser/extensions/api/socket/socket_apitest.cc`, not `src/brave/`).

## Root Cause
The test intermittently fails in `testPendingCallback` because TCP `read()` returns only the HTTP response headers without the body when the response arrives in multiple TCP segments. The test incorrectly assumes a single `read()` returns the complete response.

- **Chromium upstream status**: Known upstream flake with **5.8% flake rate** (83,121 verdicts over 30-day lookback in LUCI Analysis). Already disabled on Windows by Chromium (crbug.com/1319604).
- **Brave modifications**: Brave has no `chromium_src` overrides in the socket API path. The Brave socket overrides are for SOCKS5 and SSL client sockets, unrelated to the extension TCP socket API.

## Fix
Re-added `SocketApiTest.SocketTCPExtension` to `test/filters/browser_tests.filter` with an inline comment documenting the upstream flake rate and issue link. This entry was previously added in PR #33980 but was removed during a Chromium version update.

## Test Plan
- [x] Ran npm run format - passed
- [x] Ran npm run presubmit - passed
- [ ] CI passes cleanly

Resolves https://github.com/brave/brave-browser/issues/54922

## Summary

Follow-up to PR #4 addressing the eight issues called out in Killer's latest review.

**Desktop**
- **Removed the duplicate scene labels in every scene.** The bottom-left `SCENE NN` and bottom-right scene-tag (`AWARENESS`, `CONNECTION`, …) were echoing the persistent top brand mark and read as a second floating copy. Both DOM elements, their CSS, and their per-frame JS updates are gone. Only the top-center brand mark remains as the scene label.
- **Scene 4 silhouette now reads as a full body.** The particle silhouette generator was running with `fit = 1.0` on desktop, which produced a figure ~6.7 world units tall. The camera dollies to z ≈ 5.4 during scene 4, where the visible vertical view is only ~5.6 units, so head and feet were being clipped — exactly the "only head visible" issue. Desktop now uses `fit = 0.78` and reallocates the leg share from 20% → 28% of the points so the legs read as legs instead of thin streamers.
- Scene 5 grid background image opacity stays capped at `0.12` (already correct).
- Scene 4 silhouette **image** stays at `heightFactor: 0.65` with `contain` fit so the full PNG figure (head → feet) fits inside any viewport.

**Mobile (now `max-width: 768px`)**
- **Bumped the `IS_MOBILE` breakpoint from 640px → 768px.** PR #4's disjoint fade was correct, but the breakpoint missed phablets / iPad mini portrait / phone-landscape, so those viewports still got the desktop cross-fade and showed both headlines simultaneously during the 0→1 transition. They now use the disjoint window too.
- **Scene 0 → Scene 1 fade is strictly disjoint.** Verified by JS probe at the boundary: at `t = 0.094` both scene 0 and scene 1 sit at `0`, and only at `t ≈ 0.106` does scene 1 begin fading in. Zero overlap.
- **Scene 2 neural background image stays at `0.12` peak on mobile** (was already correct), and the duplicate `CONNECTION` label is gone alongside every other scene's bottom-corner labels.
- **Scene 4 particle silhouette uses `fit = 0.55` on mobile** so the full body — head, torso, arms, legs, feet — fits inside a portrait phone frame instead of collapsing to a head-only blob.
- **Scene 6 orb image dropped to `heightFactor 0.25` (50% of the previous 0.50)** with `yOffsetFactor 0.30`. The orb now floats well above the centred headline rather than sitting behind it; opacity peak stays at `0.25` on mobile.

**Verification screenshots** (local Playwright + python http.server):

author: mike-majic
body:
### Motivation
- Improve readability of table cells that contain long text or multi-line item lists by showing truncated lines with a hover tooltip for the full content.
- Make diary rows and excerpts more compact and consistent by truncating long titles/excerpts and tags/names while preserving access to full content.
- Refactor the inventory edit modal to better separate item categories (Armi/Droga/Oggetti) and simplify adding/removing items.
- Preserve UI state when changing user role by avoiding an unconditional navigation to the dashboard.

### Description
- Added new CSS classes for one-line truncation and a styled floating tooltip (`.itemsTooltip`, `.itemsOneLine`, `.cellOneLine`) and adjusted diary/truncation styles including `-webkit-line-clamp` for excerpts.
- Implemented `buildCellTooltipHtml`, `buildItemsCellHtml` and `initItemsTooltip` to wrap values in `data-tooltip-full` spans and initialize a single global tooltip element, and call `initItemsTooltip` during `boot`.
- Replaced inline HTML for many table cells with calls to `buildCellTooltipHtml`/`buildItemsCellHtml` in various renderers including diary, actions log, and inventory tables so full content is available on hover while keeping rows compact.
- Reworked the inventory edit modal to provide three separate selects and quantity inputs (`invEditItemSelectArmi`, `invEditItemSelectDroga`, `invEditItemSelectVarie` and corresponding qty fields), added `fillInvEditSelect` and a category-aware `invEditAddItem(cat)` handler, and updated item serialization and rendering to use the new structure.
- Adjusted `invSaveRecord` to correctly handle inline item+quantity validation and selection when no draft items are present, and updated the edit modal markup and buttons styling.
- Changed `diaryInvestigationTable` layout to `table-layout: fixed` and reduced widths for `Titolo/Nomi/Tag` columns to improve compactness, and switched `diaryTitleMain`, names and tags to truncated single-line displays with tooltip support.
- Updated `initAfterLogin` signature to `initAfterLogin(keepCurrentSection = false)` and callers to allow keeping the current section when user role changes, and ensured `renderUsersTable()` is called after role changes.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

author: mistrox43
body:
## Summary
This PR enhances the file parser worker with request tracking capabilities and implements several performance optimizations including memory caching, batch size tuning, and progress reporting improvements.

## Key Changes

### Request Tracking
- Added `requestId` parameter to all worker message types to enable tracking of concurrent operations
- Implemented request ID management in `useFileParser` hook with separate tracking for ingest and filter operations
- Added validation to ignore stale responses from previous requests

### Performance Optimizations
- **Memory Caching**: Introduced in-memory row caching (up to 2MB) to avoid redundant database reads for filtered queries
- **Batch Size Tuning**: Increased append batch size from 10,000 to 50,000 rows for better I/O efficiency
- **Progress Reporting**: Throttled progress updates to 1MB intervals during CSV streaming to reduce message overhead
- **Synchronous File I/O**: Migrated OPFS writes from async writable streams to synchronous `SyncAccessHandle` for better performance

### Storage Layer Improvements
- Added `finalizeAppend()` method to `RowStore` interface for proper resource cleanup
- Implemented OPFS sync write handle management with proper flush/close lifecycle
- Optimized IDB operations with better cursor handling and batch operations
- Improved OPFS detection with proper feature checking for `createSyncAccessHandle`

### New Features
- Added `parse-tabular` worker message type for parsing Excel/tabular files without streaming
- Created new `useTabularParser` hook for independent tabular file parsing (sites, listings, users)
- Implemented filter optimization that returns cached base analytics when no filters are applied

### Code Quality
- Improved TypeScript type safety with proper type casting for navigator APIs
- Optimized string parsing in CSV streaming (manual newline detection vs split)
- Better memory management with cache size limits and cleanup logic
- Enhanced error handling with proper resource cleanup in finally blocks

## Notable Implementation Details
- The worker now maintains cached rows and base analytics to serve repeated filter queries without database access
- Progress messages are only sent when meaningful progress occurs (1MB+ processed) to reduce overhead
- The OPFS implementation uses synchronous writes within a single handle to improve throughput
- Request IDs allow the UI to safely ignore responses from cancelled operations

Order is preserved in `localStorage`, in the share-URL payload, and submitted to the order API in the order the user arranged — so the printed kit comes out in that order. ### What changed - Each item card in the customizer now carries: - **⠿ drag handle** (top-start) — primary path for desktop / mouse / trackpad. - **Numbered order badge** (top-end) — at-a-glance "this will be page N". - **▲▼ reorder buttons** — keyboard / touch-friendly fallback so users on small screens or with assistive tech aren't locked out of reordering. - HTML5 drag-and-drop wiring on the cards: dragstart fades the source card, dragover paints a seraj-colored drop-target ring + slight scale on the hovered card, drop swaps positions. - Reorder mutates the existing `coloringCart` array in place, calls `saveColoringCart()`, then `renderColoringBook()` so all derived totals (price, progress strip) stay in sync. No new state. - Reorder hint line ("اسحب الرسومة من المقبض ⠿ — أو استخدم ▲▼ — لتغيير ترتيب الصفحات في الكشكول.") only shows when there are 2+ items. ### Also fixes a Devin Review finding from PR #21 - `/api/coloring/categories` was building its cache key with `parentSlug ?? ""`, which collapsed two distinct queries onto the same key: - "param absent" (`parent` not in querystring) → loads all categories - "param present but empty" (`?parent=`) → only matches categories with empty `parentSlug` - Switched to a sentinel (`__none__`) so the two queries get distinct cache entries and never serve each other's data. No DB migrations, no API contract changes, no schema changes. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human This PR is **low-medium risk** — touches one customizer view + one cache key. CI passing is necessary but not sufficient — please exercise the customizer end-to-end on the preview before merging. - [ ] Open `/#/coloring-book` with 3+ items in the cart. Drag any card by the ⠿ handle onto another — confirm the order badge numbers update, the dragged card briefly fades, and the drop target shows the orange ring while hovered. - [ ] Use ▲▼ on a card in the middle and at the ends — confirm the corresponding button is disabled at the boundaries and clicks reorder correctly. - [ ] Refresh the page after reordering — confirm the new order is preserved (it persists via `localStorage`). - [ ] Click "🔗 شارك كشكولك" after reordering, open the share URL in another tab — confirm items appear in the new order. - [ ] On mobile / a touch device, confirm the ▲▼ buttons work even if drag itself is awkward (HTML5 DnD on touch is hit-or-miss by design). - [ ] Submit a test order from the customizer and confirm the order's `coloringItems[]` field arrives in the expected order on the admin Orders view. - [ ] Cache fix: hit `/api/coloring/categories` (no `parent`) and `/api/coloring/categories?parent=` from a non-admin client; confirm both work and don't leak each other's results. ### Notes - Touch DnD: HTML5 DnD on phones is unreliable across browsers, which is why the ▲▼ fallback exists. If touch DnD ever becomes important we can layer a small touch shim, but the buttons cover the same use case without the bloat. - The order badge uses `toArabicNum(idx + 1)` so it respects the existing Arabic numerals convention used elsewhere in the customizer. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/cfce49646d754016af6250f0a7e7cf64 Requested by: @Omarhussien2 ---

author: kylecarbs
body:
Adds a `diff_url:` term to the `q` search parameter on `GET /api/experimental/chats` so callers can look up the chat associated with a particular pull request, merge request, or any other URL persisted on the chat's diff status.

```
q=diff_url:"https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/123"
```

Match is case-insensitive. When the URL lives on a delegated sub-agent's diff status, the parent chat is returned so the relationship surfaces from a single lookup.

<details>
<summary>Design notes</summary>

- **Forge-agnostic.** Reuses the existing `chat_diff_statuses.url` column rather than introducing a `pr:` vocabulary, since the SDK already documents the URL as "may point to a pull request or a branch page depending on whether a PR has been opened." Works for GitHub PRs, GitLab MRs, branch pages, etc.
- **Composes with `archived:`.** The two terms can be combined: `q=archived:true diff_url:"..."`.
- **Case handling.** The parser used to lowercase the entire `q` string up front, which would mangle URL path segments. Switched to lowercasing only the field key inside `searchTerms` (already happens there) and keeping the value as the caller typed it. The SQL comparison lowercases on both sides.
- **Validation.** `diff_url` must be a syntactically valid HTTP(S) URL with a non-empty host. No forge-specific validation.
- **Index.** Adds `idx_chat_diff_statuses_url_lower` on `LOWER(url)` so the lookup is cheap even on large datasets.
- **Sub-agent fan-in.** `EXISTS` clause matches when the URL lives on the chat itself or any chat with `root_chat_id` equal to the chat's id, so a delegated sub-agent's PR pulls in its parent.
- **Deferred.** Sentinels like `pr:any` / `pr:none` and a forge-agnostic state filter (`diff_state:open|merged|closed`) were intentionally left out of this change. They couple cleanly to a second forge or a clearer product call, and shipping them now would lock in vocabulary we may want to revisit.

</details>

## Tests

- `coderd/searchquery`: parser tests for valid URLs, case handling (key insensitive, value preserved), composition with `archived:`, and validation errors (non-HTTP scheme, missing host, malformed URL).
- `coderd/exp_chats_test.go`: end-to-end coverage hitting `ListChats`. Verifies a root chat matches its own URL, a parent chat surfaces when only a sub-agent has the URL, lookups are case-insensitive, non-matching URLs return empty, and invalid URLs return `400`.

---

_This PR was authored by a Coder Agent on behalf of @kylecarbs._

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
💡 **What**:
Refactored the `tui.ts` configuration loader to perform all filesystem I/O operations concurrently before merging the results sequentially.

🎯 **Why**:
The configuration was loading sequentially in blocks (global config -> custom config -> project config -> directory configs -> managed configs). If any of those configs took time to read and parse from disk, it delayed the start of the next read. Since all config file paths are known upfront, they can be read concurrently.

📊 **Impact**:
Eliminates blocking N+1 I/O delays during TUI configuration initialization, improving application startup times.

🔬 **Measurement**:
The test suite passes, ensuring the sequential deep merging is strictly preserved in correct precedence. All config overrides work identically as before, just faster.

author: aorumbayev
body:
## Summary
- remove the serial full non-snapshot suite from the Windows job on main
- keep Windows CI focused on the explicit windows_ci compatibility marker
- add subprocess resolution and runtime-env tests to that marker so the Windows gate still covers the platform-specific bugs we actually care about
- lower the Windows job timeout from 30m to 10m

## Why
The main CI Windows job was still running after every other job had completed, then failed after ~20 minutes. Ubuntu/macOS already run the full Python suite; Windows should validate Windows compatibility, not duplicate the full suite serially.

## Verification
- uv run pytest tests/ --collect-only -q -m windows_ci
- uv run pytest tests/ -m windows_ci -n 0 -q
- uv run poe lint

author: fw-bot
body:
### Issue:
When changing the delivery date (used as the Hungarian exchange rate date), some journal lines could be recomputed incorrectly, leading to unbalanced entries

### Cause:
`expected_currency_rate` was recomputed when `delivery_date` changed, but the new value was never automatically applied

In addition, after https://github.com/odoo/odoo/pull/225407, `_sync_tax_lines` partially updated the lines:
https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/f5501e5c8dcf60444077912db4c87e7a3f2654a6/addons/account/models/account_move.py#L3029-L3031
https://github.com/odoo/odoo/blob/f5501e5c8dcf60444077912db4c87e7a3f2654a6/addons/account/models/account_move.py#L1633-L1637
These methods reapply the previous tax rate, causing base and tax lines to be updated inconsistently
As a result, when the base amount increases, the tax amount decreases, and vice versa

### Steps to reproduce:
- Install `l10n_hu_edi` and `accountant` with demo data, then switch to the `HU company`
- Go to Currencies → USD and add two rates:
April 5: HUF per Unit = 100
April 6: HUF per Unit = 150

author: chrisns
body:
## Summary
- Renames the Customer Profiles domain from `ndx-try-aicc-<account>` to `amazon-connect-ndx-aicc-<account>` so the Connect SLR (`AmazonConnectServiceLinkedRolePolicy`) can actually read it on behalf of the agent workspace.
- Adds a Delete handler to `CustomerProfilesPutIntegration` in the bootstrap Lambda so a domain replacement (this rename, or any future one) isn't blocked by an orphan `customer-profiles:PutIntegration`.
- Replaces the misleading "no explicit association required" comment with the real story.

## Why
The agent workspace's Customer Profile tab was showing _"Please contact your administrator to review your Amazon Connect Role Policy"_ on every fresh AICC lease.

Verified live (account `252552941771`):

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Connect instance active | ✅ |
| `customer-profiles:PutIntegration` (CTR ingestion) wired up | ✅ |
| Customer Profile widget loads | ❌ before this PR / ✅ after |

`AmazonConnectServiceLinkedRolePolicy` (the SLR Connect uses for the agent UI) scopes every `profile:*` action to:

```
"Resource": "arn:aws:profile:*:*:domains/amazon-connect-*"
```

Our domain didn't match the prefix, so every SLR call (`profile:GetDomain`, `profile:SearchProfiles`, etc.) was an IAM AccessDenied and Connect surfaced its generic "role policy" error. Renaming with the required `amazon-connect-` prefix fixes the widget; the rest of the wiring (PutIntegration, security profile permissions, KMS key policy, etc.) was already correct.

There is no `CUSTOMER_PROFILES`/`CUSTOMER_PROFILES_DOMAIN` `IntegrationType` on `connect:CreateIntegrationAssociation` (verified via boto3 enum introspection — valid values: EVENT, VOICE_ID, PINPOINT_APP, WISDOM_*, CASES_DOMAIN, APPLICATION, FILE_SCANNER, SES_IDENTITY, ANALYTICS_*, COGNITO_USER_POOL, MESSAGE_PROCESSOR, CALL_TRANSFER_CONNECTOR, Q_MESSAGE_TEMPLATES). Connect auto-discovers the CP domain via the SLR once the name matches the policy scope.

## Test plan
- [x] Local: `aws cloudformation validate-template` against the modified template.
- [x] Live: `sam package` + upload to the blueprints bucket + `update-stack-set` against account `252552941771` only — succeeded in ~1 minute.
- [x] Verified the new domain `amazon-connect-ndx-aicc-252552941771` was created with the integration and `CTRNoInferred` object type rebuilt cleanly.
- [ ] Reload the Connect agent workspace Customer Profile tab — confirm the error banner is gone and the searchable profile UI renders.
- [ ] Domain rename for any **existing** lease requires manually deleting the old `ndx-try-aicc-*` domain (and its integration / object types) before the StackSet update; the new Delete handler on the bootstrap Lambda makes future replacements automatic.

## Related
- `co-cddo/ndx-try-aws-scp#44` was opened as a defensive SCP relaxation based on the original (incorrect) hypothesis that `connect:CreateIntegrationAssociation` was the missing call. With the real fix in this PR, that SCP is no longer required for AICC. May still be worth merging on its own merits (lets users wire up Wisdom/Cases integrations themselves), or close as no-longer-needed — caller's choice.

body:
The automod torment action (ghost/delayed messages + silent disconnect) had no manual moderator equivalent — it could only be triggered automatically by the word filter.

## Changes

- **`/lag <uid>`** — adds the target's IPID to the torment list; starts a silent random disconnect timer (5 s–4 min) for all current sessions under that IPID. Ghost/delayed IC and OOC delivery kicks in immediately via the existing `isIPIDTormented` checks. Requires `MUTE`.
- **`/unlag <uid>`** — removes the IPID from the torment list. Requires `MUTE`.
- **Cancellable disconnect timers** — `startTormentDisconnect` now re-checks `isIPIDTormented` before closing the connection, so `/unlag` (and `/untorment`) can race the timer and win. This also improves existing automod behaviour.
- **Registry** — `/lag` usage updated to `<uid>` (was a no-op punishment; now IPID-based). `/unlag` added as a new entry.
- **Help grouping** — `/lag` stays in "Timing & throughput"; `/unlag` appears in "Removal & control".

author: iamcxa
body:
Adopts the spacedock-ui canonical pr-merge.md 0.11.0 (carlove-derived two-track review pattern) into kc-claude-plugins's docs/ship-flow/_mods/.

## What changed

Replaces the old confidence-tier ≥90 threshold gate with a two-track review pattern battle-tested in carlove (n>100 PRs as of 2026-05):

1. **Step 1** — Request Copilot reviewer-request via `gh pr edit` / API fallback, then **wait 360s (6 min)** before evaluating. Optional 120s extension to 8 min total.
2. **Step 2** — In parallel with the wait, dispatch local pr-reviewer teammate (sonnet, fresh context) running the **skill-resolution chain**:
   1. `Skill: kc-pr-flow:kc-pr-review` (preferred)
   2. `Skill: pr-review-toolkit:review-pr` (fallback)
   3. Fresh-context external code-review agent (last resort)
   With **ALWAYS-POST-ADVISORY** rule: review is posted to PR with both inline CODE comments AND advisory DOC/NEW items, even when verdict = APPROVE.
3. **Step 3** — After both reviews land, dispatch `Skill: kc-pr-flow:kc-pr-review-resolve` to triage combined findings as a single pass. VETO loop cap = 2 rounds.
4-7. Mark Ready → arm auto-merge → assign + tag final reviewer → schedule review-resolve continuation.

Self-PR caveat documented: GitHub blocks self-APPROVE; review posts as comment with explicit "would-be-APPROVE" note when PR author == reviewer.

## Why

The old confidence-tier gate was informational at best (n=4 in this workspace's PRs; never triggered a useful block). The two-track pattern catches structural bugs the verify-stage runtime DCs miss when deferred to bet observation window — exactly what happened on PR #8 (Copilot caught Cand 1 design choice was structurally wrong, leading to Cand 2 course correction in 3 fixup commits).

## Source

`spacedock-ui:docs/ship-flow/_mods/pr-merge.md` — committed in spacedock-ui repo concurrently. The skill-resolution fallback chain (kc-pr-flow → pr-review-toolkit → external agent) is the generalization for adopters that don't have kc-pr-flow installed.

## Sequencing

This PR is independent of #8. Either PR can merge first.

## Summary

### Bug fix (urgent — Step 1)

The save button on `/admin/sms/*` was disabled whenever a "recommended" variable was missing, with the old red error copy *"Skabelonen mangler påkrævede variabler: …"*.

**Root cause:** PR #9 (cursor-position insertion + recommended-not-mandatory + Inter font) was opened but **never merged into main**. So production has been running the PR #8-era validation, which treats the variable list as mandatory and blocks save. PR #11 didn't regress anything — the regression already existed; PR #11 was just unrelated.

This PR applies the recommended-not-mandatory pattern directly to current main:

- `REQUIRED_VARIABLES` → `RECOMMENDED_VARIABLES`. Same grouped structure (`[customer_first_name, customer_name]` is one "name greeting" group; either alternative satisfies it).
- New `RECOMMENDED_REASONS` map with the Danish "why this matters" lines from the original PR #9 spec.
- Red error block replaced with a yellow warning panel: `border-l-4 border-warning bg-warning-bg p-3 rounded-r-lg`, header *"Anbefalede variabler mangler"*, bullets `• {var} — explanation`. Inline lucide-style `AlertTriangle` SVG (no new dep).
- `canSave` is now just `isSuperAdmin && isDirty && !saving`. **Never blocked by missing variables.**
- Save tooltip simplified — no more *"Tilføj de påkrævede variabler først"*; only *"Ingen ændringer at gemme."* when there's nothing dirty.

### Feature: customer favourite barber

New SQL view `public.customers_enriched` joins `customers` with computed favourites:

- `favourite_barber_id` / `favourite_barber_name` — most-frequent barber across `status='completed'` bookings (tiebreak: barber_id asc).
- `favourite_service_id` / `favourite_service_name` — same for services.
- `last_visit_at` — `max(starts_at) where status='completed'`.
- `activity_status` — `'active'` if last completed visit < 60 days, `'inactive'` if older, `'never'` if no completed bookings.

Customer detail page gains a new card *"BLIVER KLIPPET AF"* (Cormorant SC eyebrow + Inter 500 14 px name) in the same grid as *FÅR SOM REGEL* / *SIDST HER* / *KUNDE SIDEN*. Hidden when null (customer has no completed bookings yet).

### Feature: Kunder list filters

Filter row below the search input. Five composable dropdowns + a Nulstil link:

| Filter | Options |
|---|---|
| **Frisør** | Alle / per active barber (filters by `favourite_barber_id`) |
| **Ydelse** | Alle / per service (filters by `favourite_service_id`) |
| **Besøg** | Alle / 1-2 / 3-5 / 6-10 / 10+ (visit-count tier) |
| **Udeblivelser** | Alle / 0 / 1 / 2+ (`no_show_count`) |
| **Aktivitet** | Alle / Aktiv (60 d) / Inaktiv / Aldrig (`activity_status`) |

- Pill-shaped white selects, gold border `#B08A3E` 1 px. Active selects get a `#FAF6EC` gold-tinted bg so a glance over the row tells you which dimensions are filtering.
- All filters compose with AND; search is additive (ILIKE on `full_name` + phone substring match).
- "Nulstil filtre" link appears on the right when any filter is non-default; clears all five.
- All filtering is client-side — for ~200 customers the round trip would be more expensive than re-running an Array.filter on every keystroke.

## Schema additions (applied via Supabase MCP)

- `public.customers_enriched` view (SECURITY INVOKER → inherits the existing `customers` RLS: admin write + barber read).
- Verified: customer with completed bookings shows favourite_barber_name = 'Hamada', favourite_service_name = 'Herreklip', activity_status = 'active'. Customers with no completed bookings show NULL favourites + activity_status = 'never'.

## Note on PR #9

PR #9 is still open and now overlaps with this PR on `SmsTemplateEditor.tsx`. PR #9 has unique content this PR doesn't: cursor-position variable insertion (forwardRef + Selection/Range API) and the explicit `font-sans` Tailwind class on the editor body. **Whichever PR merges second will need a rebase.** I recommend merging this one first since it ships the urgent bug fix; PR #9 can then rebase to keep just the cursor-insertion + font-sans pieces.

- [ ] **Manual**: customer detail for Oliver Pouret-Frydendahl shows "BLIVER KLIPPET AF Hamada" in the card grid
- [ ] **Manual**: Kunder list — set Frisør = Hamada, narrows; add Udeblivelser = 2+, narrows further; click Nulstil — full list returns
- [ ] **Manual (375 px)**: filter row stacks cleanly on mobile

Do not merge — leaving for Oliver to spot-check the SMS editor fix in browser and merge.

author: estmcmxci
body:
## Summary

Fixes the identity layer's silent failure mode for any caller who doesn't already know the agent ID. Closes #43.

## Before / after

`emilemarcelagustin.eth` is a registered agent (ERC-8004 #24994 on Base). Trust resolution today:

```
$ ensemble trust emilemarcelagustin.eth
  ✓ Personhood: World ID, ...
  ✗ Identity: no ENSIP-25 registration found        ← bug
  ✓ Context: ENSIP-26, SKILL.md at ...
  ...
  Trust Tier: none
```

After this PR:

```
$ ensemble trust emilemarcelagustin.eth
  ✓ Personhood: World ID, ...
  ✓ Identity: ERC-8004 #24994, eip155:8453          ← fixed
  ✓ Context: ENSIP-26, SKILL.md at ...
  ✓ Manifest: AIP v1, signature valid
  ✓ Skill: domain-verified
  Trust Tier: full
```

## Root cause

`packages/resolver/src/layers/identity.ts:87`:

```ts
const agentIds = knownAgentIds ?? [];
```

If the caller passed no IDs (the common case), the inner scan loop iterated over an empty array and the function fell through to `verified: false`. A code comment promised "fall back to scanning a reasonable range" — that fallback never existed.

## Fix

Read the canonical `agent-ids` ENS text record (a JSON array of agent-ID strings, e.g. `["24994"]`) and merge it with caller-supplied IDs before scanning. This is the same record `ensemble agent link` already writes when publishing an ENSIP-25 record (see #40), so for any name linked through Ensemble, identity now resolves automatically.

```ts
const indexed: string[] = [];
const indexRaw = await readText(ensName, "agent-ids");
if (indexRaw) {
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(indexRaw);
    if (Array.isArray(parsed)) {
      for (const id of parsed) {
        if (typeof id === "string" && id.length > 0) indexed.push(id);
      }
    }
  } catch { /* malformed → degrade, don't throw */ }
}
const merged = Array.from(new Set([...indexed, ...(knownAgentIds ?? [])]));
```

Best-effort: a malformed value or RPC error degrades to using only the caller-supplied IDs rather than failing the whole layer.

## Naming choice — `agent-ids` (plural) vs the issue's `agent-id`

The issue (#43) proposed `agent-id` as a comma-separated string. author: nathanflurry
body:
## Stack Context

This stack hardens Rivet Actor SQLite storage against lifecycle overlap, where multiple actor instances can observe or write the same Depot-backed SQLite database concurrently.

## What?

- Add Depot head-fence checks for SQLite reads and commits.
- Preserve structured `depot.head_fence_mismatch` errors through pegboard-envoy and envoy protocol v5.
- Mark native SQLite VFS instances fatal on head-fence mismatch and surface that at the worker boundary.
- Stop the actor generation on fatal SQLite storage errors for both local native SQLite and remote SQLite.

## Why?

SQLite corruption symptoms around actor lifecycle churn point to overlapping actor instances accessing the same database. Depot is the authority for the current SQLite head, so this PR checks expected vs actual head inside Depot transactions and treats mismatches as a fatal lifecycle invariant violation instead of allowing continued reads or writes.

## Validation

- `cargo check -p depot-client -p rivetkit-core`
- `cargo check -p depot-client-embedded -p pegboard-envoy -p rivetkit-core`
- `cargo check -p rivetkit-core`

author: noahgift
body:
## Summary

aprender-core's dev-deps create a publish-time cycle:
- \`renacer\` (= aprender-profile) workspace-pinned at 0.32.0
- \`entrenar\` (= aprender-train) workspace-pinned at 0.32.0

Both depend on aprender-core at runtime → publishing aprender-core requires their 0.32.0 to exist on crates.io, which they can't because they require aprender-core 0.32.0 first. Cycle.

## Fix

Override dev-dep entries to path-only (no version key). cargo strips path-only-no-version dev-deps from the published manifest.

\`\`\`toml
renacer = { path = "../aprender-profile", package = "aprender-profile" }
entrenar = { path = "../aprender-train", package = "aprender-train" }
\`\`\`

Local tests still resolve via the path; downstream consumers of the published crate don't see these deps at all.

## Verification

- \`cargo publish -p aprender-core --dry-run --allow-dirty\` ✓ clean (was failing)
- \`cargo test -p aprender-core --lib --no-run\` ✓ compiles

## Why this is the canonical fix

Per Cargo's published-manifest semantics, path-only-no-version dev-deps are stripped at publish time. Same pattern used by wasmtime, swc, and other monorepo projects.

The alternative (separate quantization crate per \`qwen2.5-coder-showcase-demo.md §E.7\`) is multi-PR architectural work; this 2-line change unblocks v0.32.0 cascade publish today.

## Refs #1514

This is step 1 of the v0.32.0 cascade publish project. Subsequent steps:
- Clean-room green on intel
- Topological cargo publish (~13-19 user-facing crates)
- Post-publish QA per \`feedback_post_publish_qa_required.md\`
- CHANGELOG entry

author: kdeyarmin
body:
## Summary

Phase G.4 — surfaces the patient-side smart-trigger data (leak rising, usage dropping, cushion wear, tubing/humidifier drop — Phase E.2) to the signed-in customer on `/account`. Same detections + data window the admin email dispatcher already uses; just made visible whenever the customer is in their account.

### New endpoint

`GET /shop/me/insights` (auth-gated by `requireSignedIn`). Returns:

```ts
{ insights: CustomerInsight[] }   // empty when no patient match
```

Each insight carries:

```
id, kind, detectedAt, windowStartDate, windowEndDate, notified,
headline, body, cta: { label, url }
```

Static copy + per-kind CTA URLs are rendered server-side so we can A/B test conversion language without re-deploying the SPA bundle.

### Match strategy: email-only

Linking `shop_customers.customer_id` ↔ `patients.id` requires a separate consent flow we haven't built yet (HIPAA — accidental cross-account exposure if a patient's email gets re-used by a different account). Email-match is conservative: signed-in customer's `email_lower` vs patient `lower(email)`, and an unmatched email returns an empty list rather than 404, so the SPA component can hide cleanly.

### PHI posture

Response carries trigger kind + dates only. No therapy values (leak rate, AHI, usage minutes) — those live in `patient_therapy_nights` and never appear in the customer-facing projection. Audit-friendly: log emits `customerId + count` only.

### SPA wiring

- `InsightsSection` mounts above the existing reorder-suggestions on `/account`.
- Hides entirely when the list is empty — most patients won't have a detection on any given day, and an "all good" empty card would just be noise.
- "Notified" pill appears on insights whose `sent_at` is non-null so a customer who's already heard from us via email/SMS sees the badge instead of the same insight as fresh.

## Summary

Right-click on the file tree to create, rename, and delete files and folders — operations that previously had to be done in a separate terminal/Finder.

- **New File / New Folder** (directories only): prompts for a name; supports nested paths like `foo/bar.ts` to create intermediate directories.
- **Rename** (files and directories): prompts for a new name with the basename pre-selected (extension excluded for files).

### Backend
`src/main/file-watcher.ts` gains `createFile`, `createDirectory`, `renamePath`, `deletePath`. ### Tests

author: phil-browne
body:
## Summary

When a Port/MCR/MVE attached to a VXC is replaced — for example when an MCR's ASN is changed (ESD-1094), or when a Port's `port_speed` (a `RequiresReplace` attribute) is bumped — the upstream resource's `product_uid` is unknown at plan time. That unknown propagates into the dependent VXC's `a_end` / `b_end` `types.Object`, and decoding an unknown object into `vxcEndConfigurationModel` blows up with:

> Value Conversion Error / Target Type: provider.vxcEndConfigurationModel / Suggested Type: basetypes.ObjectValue

This made any plan that touched an attached upstream resource crash before reaching apply, even when the user's intended change was perfectly reasonable.

## Fix

In `vxc_resource.go` `ModifyPlan`:

- Short-circuit the partner-config / `requested_product_uid` reconciliation block when any of the four end-config objects (`state.AEndConfiguration`, `state.BEndConfiguration`, `plan.AEndConfiguration`, `plan.BEndConfiguration`) is `IsUnknown()`. There is nothing meaningful to reconcile until the upstream apply has produced concrete values.
- Guard the `plan.AEndPartnerConfig.As(...)` and `plan.BEndPartnerConfig.As(...)` calls against unknown values for the same reason.

The reconciliation that *was* skipped is purely a plan-time cosmetic — Create/Update still run and produce the correct state.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go vet ./...`
- [x] `go test ./internal/provider/` (unit mode)
- [x] `golangci-lint run --timeout=10m` — 0 issues
- [x] `go generate ./...` — no doc drift
- [ ] Acceptance: `TestAccMegaportVXC_AttachedProductReplace` — forces a Port replacement (`port_speed` 1000 → 10000) and asserts the dependent VXC plans cleanly. Pre-fix this step fails with the Value Conversion Error.

## Related

- ESD-1094 (separate PR): MCR ASN should not force replacement. That fix is blocked on a megaportgo SDK change to expose `asn` on `ModifyMCRRequest`. This PR fixes the user-visible cascade error independently, since the same crash can be triggered by any RequiresReplace change on an attached Port/MCR/MVE.

Addresses https://github.com/megaport/terraform-provider-megaport/issues/369

## Summary

Closes #283.

Replaces the hard-coded calendar transition durations with a user-configurable speed setting (`off | fast | normal | slow`). The four speeds map to 0/150/300/600 ms; `normal` matches the previously hard-coded 300 ms `SimpleCalendar` slide, so existing users see no behavioural change after migration. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` continues to short-circuit animations inside `AnimatedSwap` itself — this setting layers on top.

## Phasing

- **Phase 1** — `UserSettings.calendarTransitionSpeed` column + migration `0006_add_calendar_transition_speed`; typed `CalendarTransitionSpeed` enum and `TRANSITION_SPEED_TO_MS` mapping in `src/lib/calendar/transition-speed.ts` with unit tests.
- **Phase 2** — `PUT /api/settings` validation; `useUserSettings` exposes the new field with default fallback for unknown / missing values.
- **Phase 3** — `ICalendarContext.transitionDurationMs` flows from the user setting; the three production `AnimatedSwap` callsites (`/calendar` page fade, `SimpleCalendar` month slide, `/test/calendar` fade) read from context. Selecting "Off" produces `transitionDurationMs=0`, which uses the same instant-swap path as `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- **Phase 4** — `CalendarTransitionSection` (Radix `ToggleGroup`, `Off / Fast / Normal / Slow`) wired into the settings page + the test settings page; component tests cover the picker; Playwright `e2e/calendar-transition-speed.spec.ts` (video on) covers the off-path swap and the slow-path mid-animation snapshot via the new `?transitionMs=N` URL param on `/test/calendar`.

## Notes

- The setting is stored as a `TEXT` column (not a Postgres enum) so we can extend the choice list without a schema migration. Validation lives in `src/lib/calendar/transition-speed.ts` and is shared between the API route and the UI.
- Deferred / out of scope: per-callsite override (the page-level fade and the month slide currently share one speed; a follow-up could split them if anyone asks).
- Day/Week/Year intra-view slides (PR #299) will pick up the same context value once they merge — no further wiring needed there.

## Test plan

- [x] **CI green.**
- [x] `pnpm test:run` — **1917 tests pass** (was 1908; +9 new — 8 transition-speed unit, 5 API validation, 3 hook, 9 settings-section, 1 SimpleCalendar wiring; existing context-mock factories updated to include the new field).
- [x] `pnpm lint:fix && pnpm format:fix && pnpm check-types` — clean (only pre-existing warnings).
- [x] Local `prisma migrate diff --from-empty --to-schema --script` produces the same SQL as the migration.
- [ ] Playwright `calendar-transition-speed.spec.ts` (video on) — needs runtime browser; not run in this CI path. Spec is structured to verify both the off and slow speed paths against the test page.

body:
## Summary

Add `@select-skip-when-head-ref-prefix:` — a spec-header directive
that lets `e2e/select-specs.js` drop a rule-matched spec when the PR's
head ref starts with one of the listed prefixes. ALWAYS_RUN baseline
is exempt; the directive only filters rule-matched specs.

Annotated specs (all carry `cms/`):

- `e2e/cms-publish-loop.spec.js`
- `e2e/cms-delete-published.spec.js`
- `e2e/cms-publish-loop-preview.spec.js`
- `e2e/cms-publish-loop-prod-mutate.spec.js`

These four specs already self-skip at runtime on `cms/*` PRs
(`RUN_HOST_REPO_PUBLISH_LOOP` / `RUN_PROD_MUTATE_PLAYGROUND` /
`PR_NUMBER` are unset), but the selector was still picking them up,
forcing the full e2e bring-up — Ruby + Node + Playwright browser
install — only to no-op. Eliminating that on `cms/*` PRs (e.g. the
PR-137-style edits) should save the lion's share of those runs'
wall-clock and queue time, especially when `_e2e/canary-post.md` is
the only changed file (selection collapses to scope=skip after
filtering, so a single baseline shard runs instead of a 4-way matrix).

When `GITHUB_HEAD_REF` is empty (cron / `workflow_dispatch` / push)
the selector skips directive filtering entirely — annotated specs
stay selected so scheduled runs still get full coverage.

The workflow's `select` job now passes `GITHUB_HEAD_REF: ${{ github.head_ref }}`
into the step env (GHA does not auto-populate it on `step.env`).

Independent of Layer 2 (dynamic shard count); only the directive plumbing
changes here.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx playwright test e2e/select-specs.test.js` (34 tests, all pass)
- [x] Manual CLI sanity: `GITHUB_HEAD_REF=cms/foo node e2e/select-specs.js --base origin/main` against a contrived `_e2e/canary-post.md` diff collapses to scope=skip; without the env var the same diff yields 7 specs including the publish-loop ones.

author: wangyuyan-agent
body:
## Summary

Adds thread participation tracking to the Feishu adapter. Once the bot replies in a thread (topic), subsequent messages in that thread no longer require @mention — matching Discord's default `allow_user_messages: "involved"` behavior.

```
                    Incoming message (group chat)
                              │
                              ▼
                     Has thread_id (root_id)?
                      /                \
                    No                  Yes
                    │                    │
                    ▼                    ▼
            Require @mention     Bot participated in
                    │            this thread?
                    │             /          \
                    │           No           Yes
                    │            │             │
                    │            ▼             ▼
                    │     Require @mention   BYPASS ─── respond
                    │            │                     without @
                    ▼            ▼
              Bot @mentioned?  Bot @mentioned?
               /       \        /       \
             No        Yes    No        Yes
              │         │      │         │
              ▼         ▼      ▼         ▼
           (drop)   respond  (drop)   respond
                                      + record
                                      participation
```

## Prior Art

| Project | Approach | Key Difference |
|---------|----------|----------------|
| **Discord (OAB)** | In-memory cache + API history rebuild on miss | Discord threads are channels → one API call rebuilds state seamlessly after restart |
| **OpenClaw** | Bot creates threads (topic-spawn) → always owner | No participation tracking needed |
| **Hermes Agent** | No tracking — strict @mention always | Different philosophy |

## Feishu API Fact-Check

Feishu's `GET /im/v1/messages` returns **all messages in a chat** with no per-thread filter (`root_id` must be matched client-side). Rebuilding participation state after restart would require scanning entire chat histories — impractical for active groups. This is why we use pure in-memory cache (same as Discord's data structure, minus the API rebuild path).

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `gateway/src/adapters/feishu.rs` | Add `session_ttl_secs` config, `participated_threads` cache, participation check in mention gating, `record_participation` on reply |
| `docs/feishu.md` | Add `FEISHU_SESSION_TTL_HOURS` env var + Thread Participation docs |

## Testing

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| @bot in thread → then message without @ | ✅ bot responds |
| Message without @ in main channel | ✅ bot silent |
| Restart → message without @ in same thread | ✅ bot silent (cache cleared) |
| Re-@bot → then message without @ | ✅ bot responds again |
| @bot2 in thread where bot1 participated | ⚠️ bot1 also responds (known, see below) |
| `cargo test` — 99 passed, 0 failed | ✅ |

## Known Limitations

1. **Multi-bot threads:** All participated bots respond to every message (matches Discord `involved` default). Follow-up: `multibot-mentions` mode.
2. **No persistence:** Restart clears cache. Users re-@ once to re-engage. Feishu API doesn't support efficient per-thread history queries.
3. **No `/leave`:** Bot stays involved until TTL expires.

## Follow-up Plan

| Priority | Item |
|----------|------|
| Next | `multibot-mentions` mode — require @mention when multiple bots are in a thread |
| Later | `/leave` command |
| Later | Persistence to PV (JSON file) |

## New Environment Variable

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `FEISHU_SESSION_TTL_HOURS` | `24` | Thread participation cache TTL. Set `0` to disable. |

author: buckz1lla
body:
## Trace: why $201.50?

`_rule_out_of_network` calculates: `estimated_savings = total_patient_responsibility * 0.5`
→ **$403.00 × 0.5 = $201.50**

Confidence was LOW because `_apply_data_confidence_guard(0.7, 4 missing data points)` reduces the base score below the medium threshold.

## Root cause: two rules firing on the same claim

Both `_rule_out_of_network` and `_rule_oon_referred_ancillary` were running for Ashley's WakeMed lab claim, producing two separate signals:

| Rule | Amount | Confidence | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_rule_out_of_network` | $201.50 | LOW | Generic: "Contact facility to negotiate..." |
| `_rule_oon_referred_ancillary` | $261.95 | LOW-MEDIUM | "Call insurer for in-network exception, get ordering provider letter..." |

Neither rule knew the other had already handled the same claim.

## Fix

Added a keyword check in `_rule_out_of_network`: if the service matches any `_REFERRED_ANCILLARY_KEYWORDS` (laboratory, imaging, pathology, radiology, anesthesia, etc.), skip the claim. The more specific `_rule_oon_referred_ancillary` handles it with:
- More accurate savings estimate (65% vs 50%)
- Targeted action steps (in-network exception request, contract termination inquiry, ordering provider letter, state insurance complaint)

## After this fix, Ashley's WakeMed EOB will show:
- **~$261.95** potential review value
- **One** signal (not two), from the referred-ancillary rule with specific guidance

## Test Coverage
- Harness: **39/39 — 100% PASS**

author: djwmobley
body:
## Summary

Round-1 review (commit eeece73, 2026-05-05) closed all bypass findings from initial review. See full body in detailed sections below.

## Round-1 findings addressed

| # | Severity | Bypass shape | Code site fixed | Probe(s) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | MAJOR | pwsh -File ok.ps1; pwsh -Command "(bad)" | hooks/pretool-lint-bash.js (dropped FILE_INVOCATION_RE early-return) | [file-then-inline-bad], [file-then-inline-clean] | exit 0 -> exit 2 |
| 2 | MAJOR | pwsh -EncodedCommand (b64) (UTF-16LE per MS contract) | hooks/pretool-lint-bash.js (added ENCODED_COMMAND_RE + decoder; aliases -EncodedCommand/-encodedcommand/-EnC/-enc) | [encoded-command-bad], [encoded-command-clean], [encoded-command-shortform-enc] | exit 0 -> exit 2 |
| 3 | MINOR | Heredoc pipe-on-opening-line (cat << 'EOF' \| pwsh ...) | hooks/pretool-lint-bash.js (added PIPED_HEREDOC_OPENING_RE alongside the existing closing-line variant) | [heredoc-pipe-opening-bad], [heredoc-pipe-opening-clean] | exit 0 -> exit 2 |
| 4 | MINOR | Inline-prose lead-in fence in chat ("Run this: " before fence) | hooks/stop-lint-chat.js (leading anchor relaxed `^` -> `(?:^\|\n\|\s)`) | [inline-colon-fence-bad], [inline-colon-fence-clean] | exit 0 -> exit 2 |
| 5 | flagged-OOS-now-IN | pwsh -Command '(bad)' (single-quoted body) | hooks/pretool-lint-bash.js (INLINE_COMMAND_RE extended with single-quote alternative) | [single-quoted-bad], [single-quoted-clean] | exit 0 -> exit 2 |
| 6 | flagged-OOS-now-IN | sh -c "$(...)" / bash -c "$(...)" (subshell substitution) | hooks/pretool-lint-bash.js (added SUBSHELL_RE; recursive scan with depth cap 3 via SUBSHELL_MAX_DEPTH; collectMatches() helper avoids stateful-RegExp.lastIndex pitfall) | [subshell-substitution-bad], [subshell-substitution-bash-bad], [subshell-substitution-clean] | exit 0 -> exit 2 |
| 7 | flagged-OOS-now-IN | echo "(lit)" \| pwsh (literal lifted) AND cat (file) \| pwsh (refuse + block) | hooks/pretool-lint-bash.js (STDIN_ECHO_RE lifts the literal; STDIN_CAT_RE detects file-source pipes and emits stderr "Refusing pipe-to-pwsh from external file source -- cannot lint <file>" with exit 2) | [stdin-pipe-echo-bad], [stdin-pipe-echo-clean], [stdin-pipe-cat-warn-and-block] | exit 0 -> exit 2 |
| 8 | flagged-OOS-now-IN | Capital / synonym fence variants (PowerShell, PWSH, POSH) | hooks/stop-lint-chat.js (regex `i` flag + tag set widened to `(powershell\|pwsh\|ps1\|posh)`; generic `shell` and no-label intentionally excluded) | [case-insensitive-fence-bad-PowerShell], [-PWSH], [-POSH], [-mixed-posh], [-clean-PowerShell], [fence-shell-not-matched] | exit 0 -> exit 2 |

### EncodedCommand substrate citation

URL: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_powershell_exe (verified 2026-05-05)

Verbatim quote (under -EncodedCommand parameter section): "Accepts a base-64-encoded string version of a command. Use this parameter to submit commands to PowerShell that require complex quotation marks or curly braces. The string must be formatted using UTF-16LE character encoding."

Decoder implementation: Buffer.from(b64, 'base64').toString('utf16le'). Round-trip verified 2026-05-05:
- PS encode: [Convert]::ToBase64String([System.Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes("Get-Date")) -> RwBlAHQALQBEAGEAdABlAA==
- Node decode: Buffer.from("RwBlAHQALQBEAGEAdABlAA==", "base64").toString("utf16le") -> Get-Date
- Equality: exact match.

Decoder rejects malformed base64 (non-alphabet chars, odd-length buffer) by emitting a refusal warning and blocking with exit 2.

### Subshell recursion contract surprise

The initial implementation used the existing module-level RegExp instances with `while (re.exec(s))` loops. The subshell extractor's recursive call extractInlinePsBlocks(inner, depth+1) ran its own scan, including SUBSHELL_RE.lastIndex = 0 on entry. On return, the parent's outer `while (SUBSHELL_RE.exec(command))` restarted from index 0, re-matching the same outer subshell -> infinite loop, OOM after ~120 seconds.

Fixed via collectMatches(regex, str) helper: builds a fresh RegExp instance from regex.source / regex.flags per call, returns concrete match results before any recursion. The recursion contract is now stateless across stack frames. Same helper applied to all eight extractor patterns for consistency.

## Adversarial probe counts

| Hook | Pre-PR | v0.4 R1 (initial PR) | Round-1 closures (eeece73) | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stop hook (test-stop-hook.js) | 0 | 8 probes / 12 assertions | +9 probes | 21 probes |
| PreToolUse-Bash hook (test-pretool-bash-hook.js) | 0 | 8 probes / 12 assertions | +22 probes | 34 probes |
| File-based adversarial probes | 49 | 0 | 0 | 50 |

`node tests/run-battery.js` final output: All batteries, probes, and unit tests passed! (Stop hook probes: 21 passed, 0 failed. PreToolUse-Bash hook probes: 34 passed, 0 failed.)

## Known design decisions and limitations

- cat (file) \| pwsh is not lintable -- the hook cannot read arbitrary file contents at hook time. Detect-and-block-with-warning is the chosen handling. Author should inline the body via pwsh -Command "..." (catches at PreToolUse) or write the file via Write/Edit (catches at PostToolUse).
- Subshell recursion is capped at depth 3 via SUBSHELL_MAX_DEPTH. Pathological multi-level nesting beyond that is rejected (returns no extracted blocks). In practice, depth 3 covers all realistic shapes.
- Generic shell and no-label fences are intentionally excluded from the Stop hook tag set to avoid over-matching legitimate non-PS code blocks.
- R28 on short snippets: pwsh -Command "Get-Date" alone triggers R28 (regex-inverse: no `if ($null -eq` guard). R28 was designed for complete scripts. Clean probes use conformant snippets that satisfy R28. Pre-existing limitation, not introduced by this PR.

## Versioning

## Summary

Adds `GET /api/system/health/probes` returning the canonical sorted list of registered probe names. Lets frontend callers validate at startup that an expected probe exists before reading `probes[name=…]` from `/api/system/health`.

## Why

#6917 documented that probe names are hardcoded twice (backend `@register_health_probe('batch_jobs')` + frontend `probes.find(p => p.name === 'batch_jobs')`). Typo on either side breaks silently — frontend gets undefined, falls back to 'unavailable'.

This is **phase 1**: enables runtime validation. Phase 2 (codegen/enum-based SSOT) tracked separately as #6917 stays open.

## Implementation

`list_registered_probes()` already existed at `api/system_health.py:137`. This PR is a single new `@router.get` endpoint in `api/system.py` that wraps it. Public, cheap, auth-matches `/api/system/health`.

author: pepperinsalt
body:
🎯 **What:** This PR fixes a vulnerability where an unbounded JSON payload could crash the Node.js server.
⚠️ **Risk:** Due to a lack of file-size checking, a large data payload could overwhelm process memory via String concatenation on HTTP streams combined with `JSON.parse` exhaustation, leading to out of memory failures/DoS.
🛡️ **Solution:** Limits the parsed `bodySize` in `vite.config.ts` server middleware handler to a sensible default maximum of 5MB. Any payload larger than this boundary forces the server to destroy the connection explicitly and return `413 Payload Too Large`. Headers have sent checks added to avoid runtime errors on HTTP stream destruction.

body: ## Summary - Rotate stale Whitenoise app database keyring entries when creating a fresh encrypted database or encrypting a plaintext database. - Preserve existing keyring entries during interrupted migration recovery sidecar handling. - Delete app and per-account MDK database keyring entries during app wipe, and delete per-account MDK storage/keyring entries on logout. - Pin MDK to merged master commit `634085a919ffac725323f7085291d945979af507`, which includes marmot-protocol/mdk#275 for fresh per-account MLS database key rotation. ## Root Cause If a database file was removed while its keyring entry remained, fresh database creation could reuse stale SQLCipher key material. author: cagatay-y
body:
The Windows and Linux documentations for the same feature were used as references. It was more difficult to find information on how devices support the feature, so the interface is mostly based on how virtio-net devices expect to be driven. The code was [tested](https://github.com/hermit-os/kernel/pull/2308) on the Hermit kernel with a virtio-net device, but only with IPv4, as Hermit does not support IPv6.

## Design rationale
- The segmentation capabilities are specified separately for TCP on IPv4 and IPv6. This follows the example of [Linux](https://docs.kernel.org/networking/netdev-features.html#:~:text=TCPv4%20%28when%20NETIF%5FF%5FTSO%20is%20enabled%29%20or%20TCPv6%20%28NETIF%5FF%5FTSO6%29%2E) and [Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/network/offloading-the-segmentation-of-large-tcp-packets#:~:text=Support%20IPv4%20or%20IPv6%2C%20or%20both%20IPv4%20and%20IPv6.). This should provide flexibility for devices that support only one of the IP versions and should not be a problem for devices that support both as a single feature.
- As it is necessary to communicate to the device what the target segment size is, a field is added to [PacketMeta](https://docs.rs/smoltcp/latest/smoltcp/phy/struct.PacketMeta.html). To keep the compiler able to optimise out the structure if the features associated with the fields, the segmentation offload feature is optional, following the example of  [`packetmeta-id`](https://docs.rs/smoltcp/latest/smoltcp/phy/struct.PacketMeta.html#:~:text=If%20no%20field%20is%20enabled%2C%20this%20struct%20becomes%20zero%2Dsized%2C%20which%20allows%20the%20compiler%20to%20optimize%20it%20out%20as%20if%20the%20packet%20metadata%20mechanism%20didn%E2%80%99t%20exist%20at%20all.).
- For pre-segmentation IP packets whose size exceeds the maximum that is allowed by the length field of the IP header, we fall back to zero. An alternative would be to set the field to zero unconditionally, and this [seems](https://www.intel.com/content/dam/doc/manual/pci-pci-x-family-gbe-controllers-software-dev-manual.pdf#page=73) to be a "should" level expectation for at least for some Intel cards. The fallback approach has the advantage of keeping code that uses the IP header field (for example for [constructing `TcpPacket`s](https://docs.rs/smoltcp/latest/smoltcp/wire/struct.TcpPacket.html#method.new_checked) to set the partial checksum in our case) functional for sufficiently small unsegmented packets. On the other hand, it can also be argued that causing a failure even for smaller packets can help uncover the error case with the larger packets earlier in the development of the device drivers.

## Comparison to  #830
- The segmentation capabilities struct in the older PR follows the structure of [`ChecksumCapabilities`](https://docs.rs/smoltcp/latest/smoltcp/phy/struct.ChecksumCapabilities.html). This PR does not do so for the following reasons:
  - The segmentation capability for a given protocol is not binary. Different devices may support large (i.e. unsegmented) packets of different maximum sizes ([references for various devices](https://github.com/hermit-os/kernel/issues/1861#:~:text=Different,10%5D%2E))
  - On the receive side the related feature seems to be called "coalescing." It may be somewhat confusing to represent information for the receive side in a structure whose name refers to "segmentation."
- The capability structure is named `SegmentationCapabilities` rather than the TCP specific name `TsoCapabilities`. I believe the current structure can be expanded to support UDP, though I currently do not have a prototype for that.
- The current PR has support for communicating the target segment size to the device.
- This PR is missing an equivalent to [this line](https://github.com/smoltcp-rs/smoltcp/pull/830/changes#diff-9797218dceaf8c0bdfeddfab917f17b8d1028fd1e817a5b3de18bc4814fd894eR1742). The addition of the `set_meta` calls seems correct to me but because it is not segmentation offload specific and I was not able to test its necessity because of the lack of IPv6 support on our test platform, I did not include it in this PR.

body:
### Motivation
- Reduce repetition in the notifications controller schema module by making function name, schema builder, and handler registration a single source of truth. 
- Prove a data-first pattern that preserves existing JSON-RPC names and registry behavior while making future schema maintenance simpler. 

### Description
- Introduced a `NotificationControllerDef` type and a `NOTIFICATION_CONTROLLER_DEFS` declaration table that pairs `function` strings with schema builder functions and handler wrappers. 
- Rewrote `all_controller_schemas()`, `all_registered_controllers()`, and `schemas(function)` to derive their outputs from the declaration table. 
- Factored each controller schema into a dedicated `schema_*` builder function and preserved the `schema_unknown()` fallback. 
- Added a bidirectional parity unit test asserting declared schema functions and registered handlers remain exactly in sync. 

### Testing
- Ran the hard preflight checks to ensure required files exist and they passed. 
- Ran `cargo fmt --all` which succeeded. 
- Attempted `cargo test --manifest-path Cargo.toml notifications::schemas` but the run was blocked during crate compilation due to a missing system dependency (`alsa`/`pkg-config`) in the environment, so tests could not complete.
