## Summary

- Flue's `composeSystemPrompt` was using `payload.system_prompt` (the `agents.system_prompt` DB column — just a short persona blurb) verbatim and **never reading `/tmp/workspace/*.md`**. So Marco answered "I don't know your name" through the Flue runtime even though USER.md was correctly synced to disk by `bootstrapWorkspace`.
- Strands' `_build_system_prompt` reads SOUL/IDENTITY/USER/AGENTS/CONTEXT/TOOLS plus PLATFORM/CAPABILITIES/GUARDRAILS/MEMORY_GUIDE and concatenates them. This PR ports that to Flue.

## What changed

- `composeSystemPrompt` now takes `{ payload, workspaceDir, workspaceSkillsBlock?, now?, fileReader? }` and is `async`. Reads system files first, then user files, joins with `\n\n---\n\n`. Falls back to `payload.system_prompt` (or a short Flue default) only when no workspace files exist — keeps tests that synthesize a payload without a populated workspace working.
- `server.ts` `await`s the new signature and passes `env.workspaceDir`.
- `system-prompt.test.ts` rewritten with a virtual-file `fileReader` fixture; covers workspace inlining, system-before-user ordering, date prefix, skills block, and both fallback paths.

## Verification

- 272 vitest specs + 5 todo green; typecheck clean; prettier-check clean on changed files
- After deploy: invoke Marco with "What is your name?" through the admin chat — should answer "Eric" (not "I don't know")

## Out of scope

- The `mcp_admin-ops_me` tool attached to Marco is a separate config issue; with USER.md actually in the prompt it should no longer be the answer-of-last-resort. Tracking as a follow-up audit.

## Summary

ADR-style addition to `docs/api/health.md` recording why `/api/monitoring/services/health` deliberately stays as a parallel surface alongside the canonical `/api/system/health` aggregator (#3333).

## TL;DR — they answer different questions

| Endpoint | Question | Caller |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/system/health` | "Is the AutoBot backend itself healthy?" | Frontend health monitor |
| `GET /api/monitoring/services/health` | "What's the constellation of remote services?" | Ops dashboard scraping |

## Three reasons to keep parallel

1. **Shape mismatch** — `ServicesSummaryResponse.services[]` is typed; `ComponentHealth.data` is opaque dict.
2. **Different SLA** — 2s probe budget vs 5-10s ops scraping window.
3. **Auth posture** — different audit profiles even though both unauthenticated.

Doc also captures the migration path if fold-in is ever needed.

## Summary

Adds 14 LLM-UX features that make jira-agent significantly more useful for tool-calling LLMs (Claude, GPT, etc.) by reducing round-trips, enabling self-discovery, and providing structured recovery paths.

## Features

**Self-discovery and routing**
- `jira-agent schema`: machine-readable JSON of the full command tree (no auth required)

**Composite workflows** (multi-step operations in one call)
- `issue start-work`: assign + transition to In Progress
- `issue close`: transition to Done with optional resolution/comment
- `issue create-and-link`: create issue + link to parent in one call

- `issue mine`: issues assigned to current user with semantic filters (`--status`, `--type`, `--priority`)

**Token efficiency**
- `--compact` flag: strips nulls/empties, flattens single-key objects, JSON Lines for arrays
- `--fields-preset`: named field sets (`minimal`, `detailed`, `triage`)

**Agent recovery**
- `--dry-run` on composite commands: preview field diffs without mutating
- Pagination `has_more` + `next_command` in metadata
- Error responses include `next_command` and `available_actions` for structured recovery

author: phuetz
body:
## What this enables

Drop the produced \`D:\CascadeProjects\gitnexus-kit-v0\` directory onto a USB stick, plug it in at a client site, double-click \`launch.bat\`, get a working chat against the pre-indexed graph at http://localhost:3000 — **zero install footprint** on the host machine. Built for the agile-up.com on-site intervention use case.

## Three small Rust changes do all the work

### \`gitnexus-core/storage/repo_manager.rs::dirs_or_home\`
\`GITNEXUS_HOME\` env var checked first, fallback to \`USERPROFILE\` / \`HOME\`. Single point of patch — every \`~/.gitnexus/\` path in the workspace already routes through this helper. Setting \`GITNEXUS_HOME=D:\kit\data\` rewires the registry, chat-config, models cache, and every CLI subcommand at once.

### \`gitnexus-cli/commands/serve.rs\`
New \`<binary_dir>/web/\` static fallback that takes precedence over \`<cwd>/.gitnexus/docs/\`. The kit packager copies \`chat-ui/dist/\` here, so gitnexus.exe serves the React UI itself — no separate Vite dev server, no proxy, no CORS dance.

### \`chat-ui/.env.production\`
\`VITE_MCP_URL=""\` → same-origin requests in the production build. The chat-ui talks directly to the \`gitnexus.exe\` it was loaded from.

## Packaging — \`scripts/build-kit.ps1\`

\`\`\`powershell
pwsh scripts\build-kit.ps1 -SeedRepo "D:\taf\Alise_v2"
\`\`\`

Runs \`cargo build --release -p gitnexus-cli\` + \`npm run build\` and assembles:

\`\`\`
D:\CascadeProjects\gitnexus-kit-v0\
├── gitnexus.exe          # Rust release, statically linked
├── launch.bat            # sets GITNEXUS_HOME + opens browser + runs server
├── README.md
├── web/                  # chat-ui dist (same-origin)
└── data/
    ├── .gitnexus/
    │   ├── chat-config.json    # api_key empty by design — operator fills
    │   ├── registry.json       # auto-managed
    │   └── models/             # ONNX (optional)
    └── repos/
        └── <seed>/.gitnexus/   # pre-indexed graph + embeddings + docs
\`\`\`

\`-SeedRepo\` parameter copies a pre-indexed \`.gitnexus/\` from any host repo (e.g. Alise_v2) into the kit.

## Smoke test (executed)

1. Built the kit to D:\CascadeProjects\gitnexus-kit-v0\ (64.5 MB total without seed repo).
2. \`cd D:\CascadeProjects\gitnexus-kit-v0; GITNEXUS_HOME=$PWD\data ./gitnexus.exe serve --port 3001\`.
3. Endpoint checks:
   - \`GET /health\` → \`200 {"service":"gitnexus","status":"ok","version":"0.1.0"}\` ✅
   - \`GET /api/repos\` → \`200 {"repos":[]}\` ✅ (empty because GITNEXUS_HOME points at the **kit** registry, not the operator's — proves the override works)
   - \`GET /\` → \`200 552 bytes\` of chat-ui index.html ✅ (proves \`web/\` static serving)

## Security posture

- The sample \`chat-config.json\` ships with **\`api_key: ""\`** on purpose. Operator fills it on the kit just before the visit (env var \`GITNEXUS_API_KEY\` or edit the JSON). Lost USB doesn't leak credentials.
- For 100% offline use later, the same kit layout will accept a bundled Ollama runtime + local model. Kept as V1 (24 GB+ for a quality coding model — too big for V0).

## Validation

- \`cargo check -p gitnexus-cli -p gitnexus-core\` — exit 0
- \`cargo build --release\` (kit packager) — exit 0
- Live HTTP smoke test against running kit — 3 endpoints OK

body:
## Summary

Lands the schema-only first half of the cross-cluster atomic-visibility wave: two purely additive `[Id]` slots on `LatticeMutation` and `ReplogEntry` (`AtomicBatchSize`, `AtomicBatchIndex`) that let a future producer-side stamping pass and a future receiver-side staging buffer recognise the sibling membership of an in-flight atomic transaction. The slots are wire-compatible (default `0` decodes legacy persisted state as "not part of an atomic batch") and zero-cost on every non-atomic write path. No producer-side capture and no receiver-side buffering yet — those land in R-095 / R-097 respectively. This change is the on-the-wire contract that everything downstream of it pins against.

## Changes

### New public API

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `LatticeMutation.AtomicBatchSize` (`[Id(14)]`, `int`) | Total entry count of the enclosing atomic transaction; `0` when the mutation is not part of one. |
| `LatticeMutation.AtomicBatchIndex` (`[Id(15)]`, `int`) | Zero-based position of this entry within the atomic transaction; `0` for non-atomic writes. |
| `ReplogEntry.AtomicBatchSize` (`[Id(14)]`, `int`) | Mirror slot on the WAL entry; populated end-to-end from the producing mutation. |
| `ReplogEntry.AtomicBatchIndex` (`[Id(15)]`, `int`) | Mirror slot on the WAL entry. |

### Modified API

| Type | Change |
|------|--------|

author: flo4604
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes WebSocket upgrade support in the frontline proxy. Two bugs were causing WebSocket connections to fail:

1. **`ModifyResponse` was wrapping `resp.Body` in `io.NopCloser(io.TeeReader(...))` for all responses**, including `101 Switching Protocols`. This destroyed the `io.ReadWriteCloser` interface that `httputil.ReverseProxy.handleUpgradeResponse` requires when hijacking the upstream connection for bidirectional copy, resulting in `"internal error: 101 switching protocols response with non-writable body"` and a 502 to the client. The fix skips the body wrap for `101` responses.

2. **`WithTimeout` middleware was attaching a deadline context to WebSocket connections**, which would cancel the context mid-session and tear down the bidirectional tunnel. The fix detects protocol upgrade requests (via `Connection: Upgrade` + `Upgrade` headers per RFC 7230 §6.7) and bypasses the timeout middleware entirely, passing the parent context through unchanged.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How should this be tested?

- `TestWebSocketUpgrade_HTTP1_Succeeds`: Starts a real echo WebSocket backend and a frontline proxy, performs a full RFC 6455 handshake through the proxy, sends a masked client frame, and asserts the echoed payload is returned correctly.
- `TestWebSocketUpgrade_BackendDown_DoesNotHang`: Verifies that when the upstream is unreachable, the proxy returns a `503` promptly rather than hanging or incorrectly upgrading the connection.
- `TestWithTimeout` (protocol upgrade case): Confirms that a request with `Connection: Upgrade` + `Upgrade: websocket` headers runs with the parent context and no deadline is attached, even when sleeping well past the configured timeout.

Fork https://github.com/Flo4604/ws deploy it locally 

`NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 bun run src/client.ts wss://ws-local.unkey.local/ws` replace the url with whatever project url you get. and then write 

`{"type":"ping"}` should give you a nice response.

author: nlrdev
body:
## Problems

1. **`TSCLI_BASE_URL` accepts any absolute URL.** `validateBaseURL` only enforced "absolute URL with scheme and host". An attacker who can set the env var (or get a wrapping AI agent to set it via prompt injection) would have the OAuth bearer token / API key sent to a host they control.
2. **`.tscli.yaml` is auto-loaded from cwd before `\$HOME`.** Combined with `encryption.age.private-key-command` shelling out via `exec.Command("sh", "-c", cmd)`, a malicious project repo can ship a `.tscli.yaml` that runs arbitrary code the first time `tscli` is invoked in that directory.

## Changes

### 1. Base URL allowlist
`validateBaseURL` now requires `https://` and a host of `api.tailscale.com` or `*.tailscale.com`. New env override `TSCLI_ALLOW_INSECURE_BASE=1` exists for local mock-server testing — never set in production.

### 2. Cwd-loaded `private-key-command` is rejected
Init() now classifies the loaded config's source. When the config came from cwd, `encryption.age.private-key-command` is silently zeroed with a stderr warning:

```
⚠️  ignoring encryption.age.private-key-command from cwd-loaded config (./.tscli.yaml) — this field shells out and is only honoured from \$HOME for security reasons. Move it to ~/.tscli.yaml if you trust it.
```

Every other field from cwd (tailnet selection, output preferences, etc.) is still honoured — the goal is to allow project-local config without permitting RCE.

### 3. `.tscli.yaml` / `.tscli.yml` added to `.gitignore`
Defensive — keeps an accidentally-checked-in profile from leaking secrets through git history.

## Test plan

- `go test ./pkg/safety/... ./pkg/tscli/... ./pkg/config/...` all pass.
- New `pkg/tscli/baseurl_test.go` covers the allowlist (default, subdomain, case-insensitive, attacker-host reject, http reject, override env).
- New `pkg/config/cwd_guard_test.go` covers cwd-loaded private-key-command stripping (with stderr warning) and home-loaded private-key-command being honoured.
- Pre-existing `do_contract_test.go` and `client_test.go` tests updated to set `TSCLI_ALLOW_INSECURE_BASE=1` since they wire fake `http://localhost` servers as the base URL.

## Compatibility

- `TSCLI_BASE_URL` pointing at any non-tailscale.com host now fails at startup. Any test/dev workflow that pointed at a mock server will need `TSCLI_ALLOW_INSECURE_BASE=1`.
- `.tscli.yaml` in cwd carrying `encryption.age.private-key-command` now silently drops that field. Configurations that legitimately wanted that field from cwd should move it to `~/.tscli.yaml`. (The other private-key sources — `private-key-path`, inline `private-key`, env `TSCLI_AGE_PRIVATE_KEY` — are unchanged.)

## Upstream

The base URL allowlist is broadly useful — happy to forward this part to `jaxxstorm/tscli`. The cwd-config restriction is more opinionated; depending on upstream feedback it could be made opt-in via a new flag.

author: snissn
body:
## Summary

- Enable the existing parallel internal merge path for sparse many-leaf applies by lowering the normal-pressure operation gate.
- Keep the change in the zipper apply layer only: no publish, root ownership, prepared-output, value-log, or collection visibility changes.
- Keep allocations bounded when the parallel path becomes active by storing per-child metrics and retired pages directly in `childWork`, and preserving small retired buffers through the child-work pool.

This PR is stacked on #1371 and uses its warm sparse many-leaf apply benchmark as the acceptance baseline.

## Local validation

```text
PASS go test ./TreeDB/zipper -count=1
PASS go test -race ./TreeDB/zipper -count=1
PASS go test ./TreeDB/zipper -run '^$' -bench 'Zipper(Apply|PrepareReadOnlyWarmSparse)' -benchmem -benchtime=100x -count=5
```

Focused benchstat against #1371 head on Apple M3:

```text
name                              old time/op   new time/op   delta
ZipperApplyWarmSparseManyLeaf-8    443.3us ±3%   301.2us ±4%  -32.04% (p=0.000 n=8)

name                              old alloc/op  new alloc/op  delta
ZipperApplyWarmSparseManyLeaf-8    8.143Ki ±0%   9.346Ki ±5%  +14.78% (p=0.000 n=8)

name                              old allocs/op new allocs/op delta
ZipperApplyWarmSparseManyLeaf-8     12.00 ±0%     20.00 ±5%  +66.67% (p=0.000 n=8)
```

Shape metrics stayed identical: `304 leaf_merges/op`, `3 internal_merges/op`, `2048 ops/op`, `307 pending_retired_pages/op`, and `1257472 index_write_bytes/op`.

The first naive version hit ~398-400 allocs/op. This version keeps the overhead to roughly eight extra allocs/op, mostly the worker goroutine path, while preserving the measured speedup.

body:
## Summary

PR 3 of 5 in the production-hardening sweep. Independent of [#51](https://github.com/Sheesha-Labs/indus-hydraulics/pull/51) and [#52](https://github.com/Sheesha-Labs/indus-hydraulics/pull/52) — no schema or runtime dependency.

The UAE-vs-export VAT rule was hardcoded inline in `apps/admin/src/lib/build-estimate-input.ts` (lines 69-74) and the total-money math (`computeTotals`) lived in `packages/pdf/src/types.ts`. Both are quote-pricing concerns that need to agree across the admin Send-Quote composer (live preview) and the PDF renderer. Drift between the two is a real bug pattern — the moment one half is updated and the other isn't, the customer's PDF disagrees with the admin total.

## What changed

Lift both into `@indus/domain`:

- **`packages/domain/src/vat.ts`** — `computeVatRate({ shipToCountryCode, override, defaultRate })`. Mirrors the existing rule (UAE → default 5%, non-UAE → zero-rated export, engineer override wins). 11 unit tests including UAE 5%, UAE 0% override, Oman zero-rated (matches the customer's manual Q26386 precedent), case-insensitive country code, null/missing ship-to, and engineer manual rates.
- **`packages/domain/src/quote-totals.ts`** — `computeQuoteTotals({ lines, vatRatePct, discountTotal, shipping })`. Same VAT-on-post-discount semantics, same 2-dp rounding. 7 unit tests covering subtotal sums, VAT base, shipping placement, zero-rated export, rounding, combined scenarios, and empty lines.

**Call-site updates** (public API preserved — no caller rewrites):
- `apps/admin/src/lib/build-estimate-input.ts`: VAT block becomes a single call to `computeVatRate(...)`.
- `packages/pdf/src/types.ts`: `computeTotals` now delegates to `computeQuoteTotals` from domain. Both existing call-sites (admin actions, `EstimatePDF.tsx`) keep importing the same symbol from `@indus/pdf`.
- `EstimateTotals` becomes a type alias of `QuoteTotals`.

Plus the same one-line `as const` → `Prisma.SentEmailWhereInput` fix on `customers/[id]/page.tsx` (separate commit; no-op once #51 merges).

## Deployment

No schema or data migration. After merge, normal Vercel deploy. The change is purely internal — all customer-visible behaviour is identical.

PR2 가 도입한 PENDING TTL 만료 → EXPIRED 자동 전환 후, KIS 가 실제 체결 결과를 콜백으로 보내도 \`Trade.executed()\` 의 가드가 \`TradeStateConflictException\` 던져 409 응답 → **백엔드 장부와 Terminal 실잔고 정합성이 깨지던** 문제 해결.

## 정책 결정 (옵션 A)
- **EXPIRED → EXECUTED 정정 전이 허용** (백엔드 추정 폐기 후 KIS 실거래 도착 시 장부 회복)
- **FAILED → EXECUTED 는 그대로 차단** (KIS 명시 거부 후 체결은 모순)

근거: FAILED 는 KIS 명시 응답(진실), EXPIRED 는 백엔드 추정. 추정이 틀린 케이스는 정정 가능해야 자본시장법 측면 정합성 회복.

## 변경
- \`Trade.executed()\`: 가드 한 줄 완화 — PENDING + EXPIRED 둘 다 EXECUTED 전이 허용
- \`TradeService.processCallback\`: \`before == EXPIRED\` 분기 추가 + WARN 로그 (\`"late EXECUTED 정정 — 만료 후 KIS 체결 도착"\`)
- \`failed()\` 변경 X — FAILED → EXECUTED 차단 정책 그대로

## 시나리오 매트릭스

| 콜백 status | 현재 status | 결과 |
|------------|------------|------|
| EXECUTED | PENDING | 정상 전이 → INFO 로그 |
| EXECUTED | EXECUTED (같은 입력) | 멱등 no-op |
| EXECUTED | EXECUTED (다른 입력) | 409 |
| EXECUTED | EXPIRED | **정정 전이 → WARN 로그** (신규) |
| EXECUTED | FAILED | 409 (그대로) |
| FAILED | PENDING | 정상 전이 |
| FAILED | EXECUTED | 409 (그대로) |
| FAILED | EXPIRED | 409 (그대로) |

## Test plan
- [x] TradeTest: EXPIRED → EXECUTED 정정 시나리오 3건 + FAILED 차단 회귀 그대로
- [x] TradeServiceTest: callback EXPIRED 상태 → 정정 전이 검증 1건
- [x] \`./gradlew test\` 396 tests 통과

## 별도 PR 로 미룸
- SignalHistory degradedReason 같은 가시성 컬럼
- Renderer 알림 / 사용자 거래내역 UI 에 "late 정정" 흔적 표시

- fix(perps): support unified account funding flows without any token withdraw flow cp-13.30.0 (#42410)

## **Description**

Follow-up to #42316. The original unified-account PR accumulated
significant
integration for the "any token" withdraw flow (confirmations-backed path
via
`TransactionPayController` post-quote mode). That flow is not shipping
in
this release, so this PR strips it out to reduce scope and review
surface.

**Removed (~1,200 lines):**
- `usePerpsWithdrawConfirmation` hook + tests (confirmations entrypoint)
- `useInsufficientPerpsBalanceAlert` hook + tests
- Post-quote feature flag selectors
(`selectIsPerpsWithdrawPostQuoteEnabled`)
- Perps-specific logic in `useAutomaticTransactionPayToken`,
`useTransactionPayAvailableTokens`,
`useInsufficientPayTokenBalanceAlert`,
  `useNoPayTokenQuotesAlert`, `useTransactionPayPostQuote`, and
  `transactionPayController` selectors
- Routing logic in `PerpsView` that conditionally chose between the
  confirmations path and the standalone withdraw page

**Preserved:**
- USDC-only withdraw page (`perps-withdraw-page.tsx`)
- Unified account `availableToTradeBalance` improvements (withdraw
balance,
  perps-withdraw-info, perps-withdraw-balance)
- `perps-controller` 5.0.0 upgrade and LavaMoat policy updates

## LavaMoat Policy Review

@MetaMask/policy-reviewers

Everything looks in order. The policy changes are from bumping `@metamask/perps-controller` from v4 to v5, and the net effect is narrow WebSocket event API updates plus removal of an unused signing dependency subtree.

What changed:
- All 8 affected policies update `@metamask/perps-controller>@nktkas/hyperliquid>@nktkas/rews`.
- New globals: `CloseEvent`, `Event`, `EventTarget`, `MessageEvent`.
- Removed globals: `AbortSignal.timeout`, `DOMException`.
- Browserify policies also remove the transitive `micro-eth-signer` subtree and its crypto-related dependencies (`@noble/curves`, `@noble/hashes`, `micro-packed`, `@scure/base`).

Assessment:
`@nktkas/rews` is the reconnecting WebSocket client used by HyperLiquid streaming. The new globals are standard browser event APIs for WebSocket lifecycle/message handling. No new package entries, filesystem, `child_process`, crypto, or new network primitives were introduced; `WebSocket` access already existed. The `micro-eth-signer` removal is a reduction in  policy surface.

## **Changelog**

CHANGELOG entry: null

## **Related issues**

Follows: #42316

author: dubaiincairo
body:
## Summary

- **eZee total revenue showing SAR 0.00** — eZee CSV exports start with a title/metadata row before the real column headers. The parser was treating that title row as headers, so `C.folio` / `C.total` were never found, `ezFolioMap` stayed empty, and all eZee sums (gross, VAT, municipality) came out 0. Fix: scan the first 5 lines and start parsing from the first one containing "Folio".

- **Odoo refund SAR 313 not counted** — The `fc2` fuzzy-match second pass matched empty/blank column headers (because `'type'.includes('') === true`), causing `PC.payType` to silently point to a garbage column. The outbound-payment flip never fired, so positive-amount refunds were counted as income instead of outbound. Fix: guard the fuzzy-match with `hl && ...` to skip empty headers; also added value-based auto-detection of the Payment Type column and extended the outbound value check.

body:
## Summary

REFACTOR-PLAN 의 leaf-up 다음 단계 (lmtune#CS) 의 **doc 전용** PR. ariadne A1/A2 머지와 병렬 진행 가능 (self-contained).

사용자 질문 "GPU/NPU 자세한 성능 정보는 어떻게 얻고 보관할 계획인가" 에 대한 본 프로젝트의 답을 contract 설계로 영속화.

## GPU/NPU 성능 정보 — 3-tier 구조

```
Tier 1: DeviceCatalog (벤더 datasheet 정본)        ← lmtune git-managed YAML
   ↓ link by pci_id (vendor:device)
Tier 2: Cluster Snapshot (ariadne 발견)            ← ariadne master
   ↓ host+bdf+sample_id 로 join
Tier 3: Performance Probes (lmtune device-bench)   ← DuckDB device_perf_samples
```

- **Tier 1** — `src/lmtune/devices/catalog/{b200,h100,h200,gb200,a100,mi300x,rbln-*}.yaml`. 필드: `peak_flops_dict (fp64/fp32_tf32/fp16/fp8/fp4)`, `mem_bw_tbps`, `nvlink_per_gpu_gbps`, `pcie_gen/lanes`. `sources[].url` + `accessed` 필수 (출처 정확성 의무화).
- **Tier 2** — ariadne 가 PCIe topology + NUMA + IOMMU 발견 (이미 보유) + A2 PR 에서 `GPUDeviceInfo` (nvidia-smi: serial, driver, NVLink topo, ECC, MIG mode), `NPUDeviceInfo` (rbln-smi: SDK ver, fw, link) 추가.
- **Tier 3** — 신규 `lmtune device-bench --probes nccl_all_reduce,mem_bw,flops,gpu_direct` 명령. R0 contract 머지 후 진입. `device_perf_samples` 테이블에 `cluster_fingerprint` 로 trial 결과와 join.

## ClusterProvider ABC + 4 입력 방법

| Provider | 의도 | 의존 |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `LiteralClusterProvider(yaml)` | BYO | 없음 |
| `AriadneClusterProvider(inventory)` | Discover | `[cluster]` extra (`ariadne`) |
| (entry_points) `KubernetesClusterProvider` | k8s Node API + DaemonSet | 외부 패키지 |
| (entry_points) `PrometheusClusterProvider` | DCGM exporter reverse-engineer | 외부 패키지 |

→ WorkloadProvider 와 동형 패턴 (BYO + Discover 통합 ABC).

## CLI 표면

```bash
lmtune run --cluster-spec cluster.yaml ...                    # BYO
lmtune run --cluster-discover --inventory hosts.txt ...       # Discover
lmtune cluster discover --inventory hosts.txt --out c.yaml    # 단독 명령
lmtune cluster validate cluster.yaml
lmtune devices catalog {list, show, match}                    # Tier 1 조회
lmtune device-bench --cluster-spec c.yaml --probes ...        # Tier 3 (R0 후)
```

## 의존 그래프

```
ariadne#A1 (multi-host snapshot) ─┐
ariadne#A2 (GPU/NPU info) ────────┼─→ lmtune#CS (코드 PR, 본 PR 머지 후 별도)
                                  │
                                  ▼
                            (R0, OD, OUT 후속)
```

- 본 doc PR = ariadne 작업과 **병렬 진행 가능** (self-contained).
- 사용자가 ariadne 측에 multi-host 지원 요청 직접 완료.
- 본 doc 머지 = ariadne 측에 lmtune 의 contract 기대 명세 전달 (양 repo 정렬 가이드).
- A1/A2 머지 후 lmtune CS 코드 PR 진입 (Catalog 8 yaml + Provider 구현체 + CLI + tests).

## Test plan

- [x] doc-only — code/test 변경 0 (회귀 0 보장)
- [x] `docs/contracts/README.md` 의 ClusterSpec row 가 본 문서로 link
- [x] WorkloadSpec 문서 (PR #37) 와 동형 구조 (책임 분리표 + ABC + 구현체 + CLI + Acceptance + Trade-offs)

## Non-goals (본 PR)

- Catalog 8 yaml (`b200, h100, ...`) 작성 — CS 코드 PR 에서 ariadne A1 의 ClusterSpec schema 와 함께 작성.
- ClusterProvider 구현 코드 — CS 코드 PR.
- `device-bench` 명령 구현 — R0 / OD PR.
- ariadne 본체 변경 — 사용자 외부 트랙.

author: ngc-shj
body:
## Why

R35 (Production-deployed component merged without manual test plan) fired **105 times** across passwd-sso reviews and **59 times** in claude-code-config — the next-largest gap after R3 (now addressed by PR #61's `check-propagation`). R35 already specifies the deployment-artifact list mechanically, but enforcement has been manual: a reviewer under time pressure misses the artifact match, the diff merges without a manual-test.md, and the gap surfaces in a later round.

## What

`hooks/check-deployment-artifact.sh` reads `git diff --name-only [base-ref]...HEAD` and matches against the closed list of deployment shapes from R35:

- Container build / orchestration: `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose*.yml`, `compose.yml`, `.dockerignore`
- Kubernetes: `k8s/`, `kubernetes/`, `manifests/`, `*.deployment.yml`, `kustomization.yml`
- Helm: `Chart.yaml`, `charts/`, `values*.yml`, `templates/*.yml`
- IaC: Terraform `*.tf`, Pulumi, CloudFormation, CDK
- Config mgmt: Ansible playbooks, cloud-init, systemd unit files
- Identity / TLS: OAuth/OIDC config, SAML IdP metadata, IAM, mesh policy, webhook signing-key
- CI/CD pipelines: `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.circleci/`, `Jenkinsfile`

When the gate fires, the hook also checks `git diff --diff-filter=A` for newly-added `*-manual-test.md`:

- **Found** → gate satisfied. Output prints the required-sections checklist (Pre-conditions / Steps / Expected result / Rollback, plus Tier-2 Adversarial scenarios) for visual verification.
- **Missing** → warn with the required sections inline.

## Tier classification

Mirrors R35 verbatim. **Tier-2 (Critical)** when ANY changed file path matches: `auth / oauth / oidc / saml / sso / mfa / webauthn / otp / totp / jwt / crypto / cipher / encrypt / decrypt / key-rotation / kms / tls / ssl / cert / session / federation / idp / webhook / signing / signer`. **Tier-1 (Major)** otherwise.

Tier-2 output additionally includes the Adversarial-scenarios reminder (cross-tenant access, token replay, redirect-URI/state manipulation, scope elevation, session fixation).

## Empirical sanity check (passwd-sso `HEAD~10..HEAD`)

```
=== Deployment-Artifact Check ===
Base: HEAD~10
Changed files: 309

## Deployment artifacts present (R35 gate fires)

Tier: Tier-2 (Critical)

Changed deployment-artifact files:
  - .github/workflows/ci-integration.yml
  - .github/workflows/ci.yml

## Manual test plan present in diff — gate satisfied

  ✓ docs/archive/review/433-key-rotation-gaps-manual-test.md
  ✓ docs/archive/review/adversarial-crypto-tenant-tests-manual-test.md
  ✓ docs/archive/review/centralize-state-transitions-manual-test.md
  ✓ docs/archive/review/vault-attachment-rotation-phase-b-manual-test.md
```

passwd-sso has been doing R35 right — the hook confirms 4 manual-test.md artifacts were added across the 10-commit window matching the deployment activity.

## Lockstep invariant

R35's deployment-artifact list is a closed set; the hook's `DEPLOY_PATTERNS` array MUST stay in lockstep. Both `common-rules.md` R35 row and this hook reference each other so a future addition to one immediately exposes the gap in the other. The PR description states this as a meta-rule.

## Integration

- `common-rules.md` R35 row gains a "mechanical detection" sentence pointing at the hook.
- `phase-2-coding.md` Step 2-5 (self-R-check) gains a pre-step that runs the hook alongside `check-propagation.sh`, before the sub-agent pass.
- `settings.json` permission entries match the existing `fingerprint` / `propagation` hook style.

## Out of scope

- **Plan-name resolution**: the hook checks for ANY `*-manual-test.md` added in the diff, not the specific plan-name match. Strict plan-name resolution would need branch-name parsing or scanning the latest `*-plan.md` added in the diff. Reasonable to defer until a real false-positive emerges.
- **Tier-2 Adversarial-scenarios content validation**: the hook prints the required-sections checklist; it does NOT parse the manual-test.md to confirm the Tier-2-specific Adversarial section exists. Sub-agent pass picks that up.

## Test plan

- [ ] Synthetic Dockerfile change without `*-manual-test.md` → warn fires, Tier-1
- [ ] Synthetic Dockerfile + `*-manual-test.md` added → gate satisfied
- [ ] Synthetic K8s manifest + `auth/` path → Tier-2 with adversarial reminder
- [ ] Synthetic non-deployment change (just code) → gate silent
- [ ] Real passwd-sso PR → confirm 4 manual-test artifacts detected, output is scannable
- [ ] Verify migration files under `prisma/migrations/` are NOT flagged (those aren't deployment artifacts in R35's sense — append-only history)

author: haglerd
body:
## Summary

Hotfix release. Five items:

| # | Severity | Item |
|---|----------|------|
| 1 | MED (info-leak) | **Auth on log endpoints**: `/showlog`, `/showrebootlog`, `/crashlog`, SSE `?log` now go through `AUTHENTICATE()`. No-op when no password set. |
| 2 | **HIGH (user-visible OTA broken)** | **CORS / OTA fix**: `functions.js` device-side `serverStatus.downloadURL` reverts to GitHub Pages URL pattern. github.com 302-redirect to objects.githubusercontent.com doesn't carry CORS headers on the redirect itself, blocking device-UI `fetch()`. Pages serves with CORS directly. Manifest URLs stay at github.com (web installer uses different fetch semantics). Broken since v34. |
| 3 | LOW (display) | **`crashVersion[16] → [32]`**: AUTO_VERSION at v36 is 20 chars + NUL, was getting truncated to "3.4.4-forceclos" in the rendered crash log header. RTC layout shift discards v36-era crash logs on the v37 OTA boot (same as a power cycle). |
| 4 | LOW (display) | **Panic-snapshot uptime coherence**: `panicSnapshotDone` latch (static, atomic release/acquire ordering matching V3 discipline) prevents post-panic log writes from racing into the captured ring buffer after `crashUpTime` was sampled. Bounds the "header says 16228 ms but buffer last line says 20321 ms" mismatch. |
| 5 | LOW (display, user complaint) | **Steady-state crash logs no longer carry boot noise**: new `LOG::clearMessageBuffer()` invoked from `loop()`'s post-IP one-shot block immediately after `=== Initialization complete` (`ratgdo.cpp:351`). Clears HomeKit/WiFi/mDNS init lines so a steady-state crash captures only post-init context. Early-boot crashes still preserve full boot trace. |

Manifest: `v3.4.4-forceclose.36` → `v3.4.4-forceclose.37` (4 refs).

## Out of scope (deferred to v38)

- Boot-time heap exhaustion → `tiT` IllegalInstruction in mDNS receive (architectural, not a hotfix)
- W1-W7 audit findings from v36 post-closeout fresh-eye review (W1, W4, W7 important; W2/W3/W5/W6 nit)

## Verification

- ESP32 build expected clean (no public signature changes; one new private symbol `panicSnapshotDone`).
- Code-reviewed (auto-mode agent pass) — APPROVED. Four minor doc/style nits all fixed before merge.
- v37 install validated via local-file OTA path (the Pages-fetch path has not yet been exercised end-to-end — first real test is when v38 cuts a release and v37 devices try the device-UI "Update from GitHub" button).

## Test plan post-merge

- [ ] Workflow `release.yml` builds clean and uploads 5 firmware artifacts to the release
- [ ] `docs/firmware/` on `main` gets the 4 flash bins (NOT .elf — MH7-redux behavior)
- [ ] Manifest auto-updates to point at v37 release URLs
- [ ] User OTAs v36 → v37 via local-file path on at least one device
- [ ] User confirms `/crashlog` shows full version "v3.4.4-forceclose.37" (no truncation)
- [ ] User confirms a fresh crash log no longer shows HomeKit init noise (the user's specific complaint)
- [ ] On the next release after v37, exercise the device-UI "Update from GitHub" button to validate the Pages-fetch CORS fix end-to-end

### Motivation
- Provide a self-contained, beginner-friendly browser game that demonstrates Canvas drawing and simple 2D physics.
- Create a playable carrom board with striker/coins, pocket detection, and a visible HUD for score and status.
- Use a single static file so the example can be opened directly in a browser without dependencies.

### Description
- Added a new `index.html` implementing a square carrom board with four corner pockets and a 3D-style look using Canvas and CSS. 
- Implemented game pieces: a draggable mouse-controlled striker and multiple coins with initial placement and radial shading for depth. 
- Implemented core physics including friction-based slowdown, wall/cushion bounce, elastic-style collision resolution between striker/coins and coin/coin, and pocket detection that removes coins. 
- Added gameplay features including mouse drag-to-aim-and-shoot controls, an aiming guide, a scoring system (`+10` per coin, `-5` if striker is pocketed), and a smooth animation loop using `requestAnimationFrame`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change. 
- The change is a single static `index.html` file intended for manual playtesting by opening `index.html` in a browser.

- **New 4-section menu** in `./setup.sh` for existing deployments: **Monitor / Deploy / Catalog / Auto update**, each with its own submenu. CLI flags continue to work as direct shortcuts and the first-run flow is unchanged.
- **`Reset verified catalog`** — wipes catalog metadata (collections, verified item metadata, verified library items, verified library container) and re-seeds from the current catalog version. Underlying `Workflow` / `SearchSet` / `KnowledgeBase` rows and user library bookmarks are preserved. Implemented as a `--reset` flag on `scripts/seed_catalog.py`; the `setup.sh` wrapper takes a Mongo backup first and requires typing `RESET` (not y/n) to confirm.

The cache file is also added to `.gitignore`.

| Section | Items |
|---|---|
| **Monitor** | System status (`./status.sh`), Tail logs (per-service), Check for updates, Run diagnostics |
| **Deploy** | Repair, Redeploy, Upgrade, Full setup, Reconfigure email |
| **Catalog** | Update verified catalog, **Reset verified catalog** (destructive), Re-ingest knowledge bases |
| **Auto update** | Schedule (cron), Remove schedule, Run auto-update now, View auto-update log |

- [ ] All previous CLI flags (`--repair`, `--upgrade`, `--redeploy`, `--seed`, `--reingest`, `--reset-email`, `--cron-setup`, `--cron-remove`, `--auto-update`) still work as direct shortcuts

author: pranjalssh
body:
## Summary

Adds two opt-in env flags that flip DeepSeek-V4 inference onto a fused FP4 MoE
path through DeepGEMM:

- `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS` → exports `DG_USE_FP4_ACTS=1`,
  flipping the mega-MoE \`x\` symm-buffer slot from FP8 (E4M3) to packed FP4
  (E2M1) and halving the per-rank symm buffer footprint.
- `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_MXF4_KIND` → exports `DG_USE_MXF4_KIND=1`,
  switching the L1+L2 mainloops from `kind::mxf8f6f4` (K=32 with-padding)
  to `kind::mxf4` (K=64 dense, 2× MMA throughput).

Also routes the existing pre-dispatch kernel through DeepGEMM's new
`deep_gemm.mega_moe_pre_dispatch` (instead of the sgl-kernel JIT'd
`mega_moe_pre_dispatch.cuh`), unifying the FP4/UE8M0 contract behind the
same library that owns the symm buffer layout.

The bundled DeepGEMM wheel under `python/sglang/srt/_vendor/` carries:
- The FP4 acts + MXF4 kind code paths
- The new fused `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` kernel
- A heuristic fix bumping `block_m=16 → 32` when `kind::mxf4` is on,
  avoiding the 1024-byte smem alignment static_assert at small batches
- Cherry-pick of upstream sgl-project/DeepGEMM
  [`003ed71`](https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/commit/003ed71b9cf9bca6a9edef85fa32bdb757cc13e2)
  (relax NVLink barrier timeout 30s → 180s)

No sgl-kernel changes; the existing 0.3.21+cu130 wheel works.

## Measurements (DeepSeek-V4-Pro on B300 ×8)

### GSM8K accuracy (1319q, 8-shot, parallel=256, 3 warm reps each)

| Config       | accuracy           | output tok/s | wall (s)     |
|--------------|---------------------|--------------|--------------|
| FP4+MXF4     | 95.60% ± 0.53      | 4587 ± 102   | 26.70 ± 0.64 |
| FP8 baseline | 95.80% ± 0.30      | 4404 ± 123   | 28.00 ± 0.79 |
| Δ (FP4-FP8)  | **−0.20 pp** (< noise) | **+4.2%** | **−4.6%** |

Accuracy gap is well within run-to-run variance (max stdev 0.53 pp).
**FP4+MXF4 does not measurably hurt GSM8K reasoning.**

### bench_serving sweep, 8192-input × 256-output (single warm run each)

| conc | FP8 TTFT | FP4 TTFT | Δ      | FP8 total tok/s | FP4 total tok/s | Δ     |
|------|----------|----------|--------|-----------------|------------------|-------|
| 64   | 983 ms   | 921 ms   | −6.3%  | 29110           | 31411            | +7.9% |
| 128  | 971 ms   | 919 ms   | −5.4%  | 39412           | 42648            | +8.2% |
| 256  | 1080 ms  | 974 ms   | −9.8%  | 47422           | 51333            | +8.2% |
| 512  | 1342 ms  | 1313 ms  | −2.2%  | 52113           | 56240            | +7.9% |

**FP4 wins on every metric at production prefill length** — TTFT down
2-10%, total throughput up ~8% across the conc range.

### bench_serving 1024-input × 256-output, conc=128 (5 reps FP4)

| Metric | FP4 mean ± stdev | FP8 (single) |
|--------|------------------|---------------|
| Output throughput | 2598 ± 74 tok/s | 2365 tok/s (+10%) |
| Median TTFT | 516 ± 67 ms (range 438-620) | 512 ms (≈0%) |

The single-rep "+41% TTFT regression" reported earlier was a one-run outlier;
across 5 reps mean TTFT ≈ FP8 baseline.

## InferenceX CI integration

The benchmark script
[`benchmarks/single_node/dsv4_fp4_b300_sglang.sh`](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/main/benchmarks/single_node/dsv4_fp4_b300_sglang.sh)
already sets `SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE=1` for high-concurrency
configs (CONC ∈ {2048, 4096, 8192}). To enable the FP4+MXF4 path, two
extra envs are needed alongside the existing config:

\`\`\`bash
export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS=1
export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_MXF4_KIND=1
\`\`\`

Image-build steps:
1. Use `pranjalssh/sglang@fp4-acts-pre-dispatch` as the sglang source
   (instead of upstream `sgl-project/sglang@deepseek_v4`).
2. After `pip install -e python/`, run
   \`bash python/sglang/srt/_vendor/install.sh\` to install the bundled
   DeepGEMM wheel — replaces whatever was installed at base-image time.

The included `docker/deepseek_v4_b300_fp4.Dockerfile` is a drop-in
replacement that demonstrates this; either reference it directly or
copy the relevant install steps into the existing
`deepseek_v4_b300.Dockerfile`.

## Test plan

- [x] Bytewise unit test for `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` (FP8 + FP4 paths) at
  production shape (M=8192 H=7168 K=6 G=32, num_experts=384). Passes
  bytewise vs `deep_gemm.utils.per_token_cast_to_fp4` /
  `per_token_cast_to_fp8` reference.
- [x] sglang server boots end-to-end on DeepSeek-V4-Pro B300 ×8 with
  FP4+MXF4 envs set. Health = 200, generation works.
- [x] GSM8K 1319q accuracy = 95.6% (3 warm reps), within noise of FP8 95.8%.
- [x] bench_serving 8192/256 sweep at conc {64,128,256,512}: FP4 better
  than FP8 on every metric.
- [ ] InferenceX CI sweep (delegated to follow-up; this PR adds the
  wiring needed for it).

## Risk / Rollback

- Both new envs default to **off**. If left unset, behavior is identical
  to the existing `deepseek_v4` branch (modulo the swap from sgl-kernel's
  `mega_moe_pre_dispatch` to `deep_gemm.mega_moe_pre_dispatch`, which is
  bytewise-identical for the FP8 path).
- Rollback: revert this PR or set both envs to 0.
- The bundled DeepGEMM wheel only takes effect after explicit
  `python/sglang/srt/_vendor/install.sh`. Without that step, the
  base-image's DeepGEMM is used and the new symbols
  (`mega_moe_pre_dispatch`, `transform_weights_for_mega_moe` re-exports)
  may be missing — server will fail to import in `forward_mega_moe`.

author: ashfrancis
body:
Companion to #690. The route-label fix exposed a previously-masked truth: the slow-request-ratio recording rule was using a deny-list that folded catalogue lookups (`/v1/assets`, `/v1/markets`) and historical scans (`/v1/history`, `/v1/ohlc`) into the 99.9% budget. The Freighter RFP only commits **/v1/price + /v1/oracle/*** to ≤ 200 ms p95 — even slo.yml's own doc-string says so — but the implementation didn't match.

Replace the deny-list with an explicit allow-list across the five relevant endpoints. `/v1/price/tip` intentionally excluded (different consistency contract per ADR-0018, no SLO target).

The remaining real perf signal — /v1/price at ~215 ms and /v1/oracle/latest at ~440 ms — is a separate optimization effort on top of this scope fix.

## Test plan
- [x] `promtool check rules /etc/prometheus/rules.d/slo.yml` — 16 rules pass

author: dhruvkelawala
body:
## Summary

Closes #216.

Adds the **Obsidian** theme (sacred-tech, deep obsidian altar with bronze body / electrum gold / lapis cyan accents) and restores the theme-aware working indicator above the editor.

## Implementation

### Obsidian theme (`src/themes/obsidian.ts`)

13-token palette mapped from `docs/ui/stitch/obsidian-temple/DESIGN.md`. Tuned for visibly distinct read against Cathedral on dark terminal calibrations:

| Token | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `background` | `#050308` | deep obsidian, near-black violet undertone |
| `surface` | `#15082A` | violet polished granite — sidebar pops away from main |
| `surfaceRecess` | `#020104` | input prompt void |
| `surfaceLifted` | `#1F0F2E` | saturated violet stone for modals/overlays |
| `foreground` | `#D4B896` | aged papyrus / warm bronze |
| `foregroundDim` | `#8B7355` | oxidized bronze |
| `divider` | `#3A2750` | brighter violet so frames register on obsidian ground |
| `accent` | `#FFD700` | sacred gold (cartouche, accents) |
| `states.idle` | `#00C896` | malachite life |
| `states.thinking` | `#00E5FF` | neon cyan — thinking ignition |
| `states.tool` | `#F0B400` | electrum gold |
| `states.approval` | `#B91C1C` | carnelian |
| `states.learning` | `#FF00AA` | neon magenta — sacred memory writes |

### Working indicator widget (`src/working-indicator.ts`)

- Theme-aware retained widget mounted above editor in `SUMO_TUI=1` mode.
- Cycles with the active theme: Cathedral `◌ ✦ ❖ ✺ ❋ ❉` @ 150ms, Obsidian `▫ ◇ ◈ ◉ ⊛ ⊚` @ 180ms (slower ritual cadence).
- Subscribes to `onThemeChanged` so frame glyphs and accent color swap immediately on theme cycle.
- Driven from `agent_start` / `agent_end` events (busy when streaming, idle otherwise).

### Theme-change repaint (the hard part)

Switching themes had a subtle bug: SumoInteractiveMode and the extension code each got a **separate copy** of the theme registry because the retained `sumo-interactive-mode.js` jiti loader uses `moduleCache: false`. `setActiveTheme` fired listeners on copy B; SumoInteractiveMode subscribed on copy A → never invoked → no repaint.

Fix:

1. **Pinned the registry state** (`registry`, `listeners`, `activeThemeName`, `themeVersion`) on `globalThis[Symbol.for("sumocode.themeRegistry")]`. Same pattern as `ACTIVE_SUMO_RUNTIME_KEY` and the diagnostics singleton.
2. **SumoInteractiveMode now subscribes to `onThemeChanged`** and on each theme switch:
   - invalidates `OwnedShellRenderer.previousFrame` (busts cell-diff so all cells re-emit ANSI)
   - calls `retainedRuntime.requestRender()` (busts chat frame cache)
   - calls upstream `ui.requestRender(true)` (full pi-tui clear+repaint)
   - schedules an immediate `ownedShell.render()` on next tick

### `applyKnownTheme` decoupled from Pi theme system

SumoCode registry is the authoritative source of truth for SumoCode chrome. Pi `setTheme` is opportunistic — its rejection (Pi only knows its own built-in themes) is a soft side-channel warning, not a block.

## Verification

Node-pty test at 160 cols (sidebar visible) after `/sumo:theme obsidian`:

| Token | Cells emitted |
|---|---|
| bg `#050308` | 173 |
| surface `#15082A` (sidebar) | 115 |
| surfaceRecess `#020104` (input) | 9 |
| accent `#FFD700` sacred gold | 8 |
| foreground `#D4B896` bronze | 171 |
| divider `#3A2750` violet | 38 |
| thinking `#00E5FF` cyan | 4 |
| Cathedral bg leftovers | **0** |

- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` ✅
- `pnpm build` ✅
- `pnpm test` ✅ — 101 files / 737 tests
- `pnpm test:integration` ✅ — 16 files / 22 tests
- Manual end-to-end via `bin/sumocode.sh` confirmed by user

## Out of scope

- CRT scanlines, chromatic aberration, neon text-shadow glows are HTML-only effects from the Stitch spec; intentionally absent in the terminal port.
- Pi `setTheme` returns `Theme not found: obsidian` because Pi only knows its built-in themes — this is the documented opportunistic-only behavior. Surfaced as a non-fatal `(Pi theme not found: …)` line in the result card.

author: cicalese
body:
## Summary

Fixes #507 — the K8s gitops path was end-to-end broken. `canasta gitops init` succeeded, the repo got pushed, but Argo CD couldn't parse `rendered-values.yaml` (`error converting YAML to JSON: yaml: control characters are not allowed`) because the file was git-crypt-encrypted and Argo CD has no git-crypt awareness.

Root cause: a redundant secret duplication. The Helm chart's `deployment-web.yaml` and `deployment-jobrunner.yaml` already pull `MYSQL_PASSWORD` and `MW_SECRET_KEY` from the canonical K8s Secrets (`<id>-db-credentials`, `<id>-mw-secrets`) via `secretKeyRef`. But `k8s_sync_config.yml` *also* embedded the raw `.env` file (containing those same passwords) into `configData.web` — duplicating secrets in plaintext inside the cluster ConfigMap, AND forcing the gitops repo to encrypt `rendered-values.yaml`. The `/mediawiki/config/.env` file in the running pod is never read by anything.

## Changes

1. **`roles/orchestrator/tasks/k8s_sync_config.yml`** — strip `MYSQL_PASSWORD=` / `MW_SECRET_KEY=` lines from `.env` before embedding it in `_web_config_data`. The `cp /configmap-flat/.env /config/.env || true` in the assemble-config init container gracefully handles the absent keys.

2. **`roles/gitops/tasks/init_kubernetes.yml`** — write an empty `.gitattributes` for the K8s path. The canonical `gitattributes.default` registers `hosts/** filter=git-crypt` which encrypted `rendered-values.yaml`; with secrets out of the values file, nothing in the K8s repo carries secrets, so no encryption rule applies.

3. **`tests/unit/test_kubernetes_structure.py`** — four structural guards in two new test classes (`TestK8sSyncConfigSecretsStripped`, `TestK8sGitopsNoEncryption`).

## Scope

K8s only. The Compose path (`init_compose.yml`) is untouched — Compose creates `hosts/<host>/vars.yaml` containing real secrets (admin passwords, host-specific values), so its `gitattributes.default` encryption is doing real work.

The git-crypt init/export scaffolding in `init_kubernetes.yml` (the `git-crypt init`, key export, `--key` argument plumbing) stays in place — dead but harmless. Removing it, plus updating the related help text and docs, is a separate cleanup PR.

## Validation

End-to-end on the same 2-node AWS cluster used for #504 and #506. After `canasta gitops init --reinit --force`:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `rendered-values.yaml` cleartext in repo | yes |
| `MYSQL_PASSWORD=` / `MW_SECRET_KEY=` in `rendered-values.yaml` | absent |
| `.gitattributes` in repo | empty |
| Argo CD sync | `Synced` |
| Argo CD health | `Healthy` |
| Argo CD actually reconciled | yes (rotated web pod via own ReplicaSet) |
| Wiki HTTP response | `200` |
| `MYSQL_PASSWORD` / `MW_SECRET_KEY` env vars in pod | set (via `secretKeyRef`) |
| `/mediawiki/config/.env` in pod | no longer contains those keys |

## Migration for affected installs

`canasta gitops init --reinit --force` after this lands. Re-renders without secrets, overwrites the repo, Argo CD picks up the cleartext file on next refresh.

## Test plan

- [x] `make test-unit` (732 tests pass, 4 new)
- [x] On-cluster: rendered-values.yaml is cleartext after init
- [x] On-cluster: secrets absent from rendered-values.yaml AND from `/mediawiki/config/.env`
- [x] On-cluster: Argo CD reconciles successfully (Synced + Healthy + ReplicaSet rotation)
- [x] On-cluster: wiki still returns HTTP 200 with secrets reaching pod env via secretKeyRef
- [ ] Reviewer sanity check on the `reject('match', '^(MYSQL_PASSWORD|MW_SECRET_KEY)=')` filter (any other secret-bearing keys in `.env` worth dropping?)

author: yanniedog
body:
## Summary
- Adds D1 write-through after cacheable report-plot live fallback.
- Adds D1 write-through after cacheable snapshot live fallback.
- Updates the integration contract so a cacheable public report-plot live fallback writes one D1 row and the next same-scope request uses D1.

## Why
Post-deploy Stage 1 verification showed TD `/analytics/series` was fixed (`X-AR-Cache: d1` for 5/5 requests), but TD report-plot and snapshot could still hit `live` when their D1 rows were missing or payload-version stale. KV warmed after the first request, but after KV expiry the same live compute could recur. This follow-up converts that expensive live fallback into a durable D1 cache row.

## D1 cost behavior
This adds at most one bounded D1 write after an already-expensive cacheable live compute. That is intentionally cheaper than recurring live recompute after KV expiry. Non-cacheable report-plot requests still do not write D1 because `scope` is null.

## Verification
- `npm run typecheck:api`
- `npm run test -w workers/api -- snapshot-cache.test.ts public-cache-freshness.test.ts`
- `npm run test:integration -w workers/api -- report-plot.integration.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`
- `npm run verify`

API/cache-only change; no `site/` edits, so no `npm run stamp:site-assets` required.

## Summary by Sourcery

Persist live-computed report-plot and snapshot responses into D1 when eligible so subsequent requests are served from the durable cache instead of recomputing from live data.

New Features:
- Add write-through D1 caching for cacheable public report-plot live fallbacks.
- Add write-through D1 caching for snapshot live fallbacks when D1 fallback is allowed.

Tests:
- Update report-plot integration coverage to assert a D1 cache row is written after a cacheable public live fallback and that the next same-scope request hits D1.

author: zyproth
body:
## Summary

Switch the QR/device onboarding timeout loops in Feishu, WeCom, and Weixin from `time.time()` to `time.monotonic()`.

These flows currently compute absolute deadlines from wall-clock time. If the system clock jumps backward or forward during polling (for example due to NTP sync, VM/container clock adjustments, or suspend/resume), the onboarding flow can wait much longer than intended or time out early.

This patch makes the timeout behavior stable by using a monotonic clock for elapsed-time measurement.

## What changed

- `gateway/platforms/feishu.py`
  - `_poll_registration()` now uses `time.monotonic()` for its deadline and loop condition.
- `gateway/platforms/wecom.py`
  - `qr_scan_for_bot_info()` now uses `time.monotonic()` for its polling deadline.
- `gateway/platforms/weixin.py`
  - `qr_login()` now uses `time.monotonic()` for its polling deadline.

## Tests

Added regression coverage for all three flows to ensure timeout behavior is based on monotonic time rather than wall-clock time:

- `tests/gateway/test_feishu_onboard.py`
- `tests/gateway/test_wecom.py`
- `tests/gateway/test_weixin.py`

These tests simulate wall-clock rollback while allowing monotonic time to advance, and verify that the polling loops still time out correctly.

## Why this matters

This is a small reliability fix, but it affects user-facing onboarding paths that can otherwise behave inconsistently in environments where system time is adjusted during runtime.

Using `time.monotonic()` here matches the intended semantics: these loops are measuring elapsed timeout duration, not civil time.

## Validation

Ran:

- `tests/gateway/test_feishu_onboard.py`
- `tests/gateway/test_wecom.py`
- `tests/gateway/test_weixin.py`

Result:

- `121 passed, 8 warnings`

body:
The repo lacked installable package structure and a visual entry point, making it hard for engineers to `pip install` and import modules or quickly see the framework in action.

## Package structure (`pip install -e .`)

- **`pyproject.toml`** — PEP 517/518 manifest: name `unitary-manifold`, Python ≥ 3.12, AGPL-3.0, deps from `requirements.txt`, optional extras `[dev]`, `[notebooks]`, `[all]`; consolidates `pytest.ini` under `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`
- **`setup.py`** — one-line legacy shim (`setup()`)
- **`unitary_manifold/__init__.py`** — namespace shim; redirects `__path__` to `src/` so sub-package imports resolve without moving any files:

```python
# after pip install -e .
from unitary_manifold.core import metric, evolution
from unitary_manifold.holography import boundary
```

Kotlin 2.x will promote KT-36770 nullability-mismatch-in-overrides from a warning to a hard compiler error. This fixes all six occurrences in the codebase where Kotlin override signatures declared parameters or type arguments as nullable when the graphql-java 26 parent declares them as non-null.

**Key Changes**

- `ViaductQueryTraverser.kt` — changed `visitField(env: QueryVisitorFieldEnvironment?)` to non-nullable `env` in both `reducePostOrder` and `reducePreOrder` (graphql-java's `QueryVisitorStub.visitField` takes non-null)
- `IViaductInstrumentation.kt` / `ViaductInstrumentationAdapter.kt` — changed `beginParse` return type from `InstrumentationContext<Document?>?` to `InstrumentationContext<Document>?` (graphql-java's `Instrumentation.beginParse` returns `InstrumentationContext<Document>`)
- `FieldWithMetadata.kt` — changed `transform(builderConsumer: Consumer<Builder>?)` to non-nullable parameter (graphql-java's `Field.transform` takes non-null `Consumer`)
- `ValueExtensionsTest.kt` — removed nullable `?` from `accept` and `withNewChildren` override parameters
- `StandardViaductTest.kt` — fixed `getData` type parameter bound from `<T : Any?>` to `<T : Any>` to match `ExecutionResult.getData`

## How was it tested?  What documentation was provided?

- `./gradlew :core:shared:graphql:compileKotlin :core:engine:api:compileKotlin :core:engine:runtime:compileKotlin :core:shared:graphql:compileTestKotlin :core:service:runtime:compileTestKotlin` — BUILD SUCCESSFUL, zero KT-36770 warnings remaining

No behavioral change — these parameters were never actually null at runtime; the nullable declarations were just overly conservative.

author: copilot
body:
Burst issue-labeling activity (e.g., Ralph triaging multiple issues) stacks concurrent heartbeat runs. With no concurrency limit, all queued jobs compete for `ubuntu-latest` runners simultaneously — jobs that don't get a runner within 15 minutes are silently cancelled by GitHub.

## Changes

- **Concurrency group** (`cancel-in-progress: true`) — replaces any queued/in-progress heartbeat with the newest trigger, keeping exactly one instance running at a time
- **`timeout-minutes: 10`** — explicit job-level timeout instead of relying on GitHub's implicit 15-min queue cancellation; healthy runs complete in ~9s so this is a no-op in practice
- Applied to both `.github/workflows/squad-heartbeat.yml` and `.squad/templates/workflows/squad-heartbeat.yml`

```yaml
concurrency:
  group: squad-heartbeat
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  heartbeat:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
```

```

scholar.archive.org        ok=1  fail=10 mr=0   flags=[AUTO]             ← already disabled
dn790009.ca.archive.org    ok=0  fail=0  mr=7   flags=[]   ⚠️ leaking!
```

الـ subdomains `dn79*.ca.archive.org` بترجّع PDFs بنجاح من ناحية الشكل، لكن المحتوى دايماً كتاب غلط (الـ search ranker بيختار subdomain غلط لـ archive.org item). الـ TRUST tier محتاج totalWithRejects ≥ 10 فالـ subdomain اللي عنده 5-9 rejects + 0 ok يعدّي بدون حجب.

|------|-------|--------|
| Manual | `src:off:domain` exists | 🚫 |
| Hard | `total ≥ 5 AND rate = 0%` | ⛔ |
| Trust | `totalWithRejects ≥ 10 AND mr > 0 AND trust ≤ 20%` | 🟣 |
| **Mistral-only (NEW)** | **`mr ≥ 5 AND mr ≥ ok × 2`** | **💛** |
| Regular | `total ≥ 8 AND rate ≤ 15%` | 🟠 |

التأثير على snapshot الحالي:

- ✅ dn790006.ca.archive.org (2/0/5) → disabled (5 ≥ 4)
- ✅ Hindawi (15/34/50) → كان disabled بالفعل (TRUST)، يتأكّد كذلك (Mistral-only)
- ✅ archive.org الأصل (37/0/0) → ساكت (مفيش false positive)
- ✅ noor-book.com (3/6/3) → ساكت (3 < MIN)

```bash
SOURCE_AUTO_DISABLE_MISTRAL_ONLY_MIN_REJECTS  = 5    # min rejects to trigger
SOURCE_AUTO_DISABLE_MISTRAL_ONLY_REJECT_RATIO = 2.0  # rejects ≥ ratio × ok
```

### الحماية

- env-tunable للسيطرة على العتبات بدون redeploy
- لا يلمس مصادر بدون mistralRejected (مفيش false positive للـ archive.org الأصل)
- `getAutoDisabledSourceDomains()` بيشمله تلقائياً عبر `s.autoDisabled = ... || mistralOnlyAutoDisabled`، فالـ `engine.searchAllSources` بيفلتره من النتائج الجديدة

author: heruan
body:
## Summary

Reproducer for a Blaze 1.6.18 + Hibernate 7.2.x query-rendering bug:
`PaginatedCriteriaBuilder.getCountQuery()` throws
`org.hibernate.query.SemanticException: Could not interpret path expression 'reversesMovement_1'`
when:

1. The projected `EntityView` declares a **self-reference subview**
   (here: `MovementView.getReversesMovement(): MovementReferenceView` — same
   `Movement` entity, different view type to avoid the recursive
   subview cycle Blaze rejects at boot).
2. The underlying CB filters on the **same association** via its name:
   `cb.where("m.reversesMovement").isNull()`.

The fetch-join Blaze emits for the subview gets a Hibernate-generated
alias (typically `reversesMovement_1`). The COUNT query emitted by
the paginated builder later resolves the WHERE-clause path against
that alias and fails.

## Tests

- `crashesOnDirectAssociationIsNull` — **expected to fail** while the
  bug is unfixed; passes once Blaze resolves the path correctly in
  the count emitter.
- `workaroundFkPathSucceeds` — regression guard for the workaround
  we use in production: walk the FK column directly via `.id`
  (`m.reversesMovement.id IS NULL`) instead of the association name.
  Bypasses the implicit-join codepath that collapses onto the
  fetch alias.

## Production trade-off

The closely-related correlated form
```java
cb.whereNotExists()
    .from(Movement.class, "rev")
    .where("rev.reversesMovement.id").eqExpression("m.id")
    .end();
```
also crashes in our production setup (large fetch tree, multiple
filters). We replace it with an explicit LEFT ANTI-JOIN:
```java
cb.leftJoinOn(Movement.class, "revAnti")
    .on("revAnti.reversesMovement.id").eqExpression("m.id").end();
cb.where("revAnti.id").isNull();
```
Trade-off: Postgres planner does not recognise `LEFT JOIN + IS NULL`
as a semantic anti-join (`Hash Right Join` + `Filter: IS NULL` rather
than `Hash Right Anti Join`), with rows-estimate=1 vs rows=N. Run-time
on small/medium volumes is within margin (+9% measured at ~400 rows);
the misestimate may degrade plans embedding this predicate at higher
cardinality. We'd revert to the idiomatic NOT EXISTS form once the
upstream bug is fixed. The minimal repro here covers only the
direct-association variant; the correlated NOT EXISTS does not
reproduce in this minimal setup, suggesting an additional factor is
needed (likely the full fetch tree of a real GraphQL projection).

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew test --tests 'to.lova.blaze.issues.paginated_count_self_subview.*'`
      reproduces locally on Blaze 1.6.18.
- [ ] Bump `blaze-persistence` once a fix lands; the failing test
      should turn green.

author: joedanz
body:
## Summary

Make cabinet moves resilient to filesystem destination collisions.

### What was broken

\`movePage\` (\`src/lib/storage/page-io.ts:157\`) called \`fs.rename\` blind. When the destination already existed:

- The raw errno surfaced verbatim. A user dragging a top-level cabinet into a parent that already contained an entry with the same name saw \`\"Failed to move page: ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rename '/.../cabinet/getting-started' -> '/.../cabinet/test-subcab/getting-started'\"\`. Useful for a developer reading the code; opaque for everyone else.
- A frequent cause was a \"hollow orphan\" — the destination contained only empty hidden cabinet scaffolding (\`.agents/.conversations/...\`) recreated at the old path by daemon-side processes after a previous cabinet move. Zero file content, but \`fs.rename\` correctly refused to clobber a non-empty directory. The user has no indication that the blocker is empty leftover state, and short of opening a terminal and running \`rm -rf\`, no in-app way to clear it.

### What this changes

Three commits, each refining the previous:

**1. Pre-check the destination with a friendly error.** Before \`fs.rename\`, check \`fileExists(toResolved)\`. If the destination exists, throw a message that names the item and the parent: \`\"An item named \\\"X\\\" already exists in \\\"Y\\\". Rename or remove it first.\"\` The user knows immediately which collision to resolve.

**2. Sweep hollow orphans automatically.** When the colliding destination contains only hidden cabinet scaffolding directories and zero files at any depth, \`fs.rm\` it before the rename. A new helper \`isHollowOrphanDir\` does the recursive walk. Any destination with real content still throws the friendly error from commit 1 — the sweep is conservative by default.

**3. Tighten the sweep, handle the post-sweep race.**
- \`isHollowOrphanDir\` initially treated *any* tree of empty subdirectories as an orphan, which would silently delete a user-created empty folder named the same as the moving item. Restrict to known scaffolding directory names (\`.agents\`, \`.jobs\`, \`.cabinet-state\`) at the top level — the canonical set scaffolded next to every cabinet (\`src/lib/storage/cabinet-scaffold.ts:80-97\`).
- The daemon-side process that recreated the scaffolding can do so again between sweep and rename. If \`fs.rename\` then fails with \`ENOTEMPTY\`/\`EEXIST\`, surface the friendly error from commit 1 instead of letting the raw errno through.

### Why hollow orphans exist (context, not changed here)

Every cabinet has hidden runtime-state siblings — \`.agents/\`, \`.jobs/\`, \`.cabinet-state/\` (\`src/lib/storage/cabinet-scaffold.ts:80-97\`). When a cabinet directory is renamed, \`fs.rename\` relocates the whole tree atomically. But:

- Open file handles held against the old path keep flushing — most visibly to \`.agents/.conversations/{id}/events.log\` (\`src/app/api/agents/conversations/[id]/events-log/route.ts:31\`) and the staging attachments tree (\`src/components/composer/use-composer-attachments.ts:45\`).
- Chokidar watchers registered on \`data/**/.agents/**\` (\`server/cabinet-daemon.ts:1841-1843\`) fire on the unlink half of the rename pair, and downstream handlers can re-touch the old path while updating internal state keyed by absolute path.

The result is an empty \`.agents/.conversations/\` skeleton at the original location after every cabinet move that had any agent activity.

The architecturally correct fix is to notify the daemon on cabinet renames so it can close streams keyed by the old path, rewrite watcher path keys, and seed a short-lived ignore set. That's a separate change targeting \`server/cabinet-daemon.ts\`, the API route, and a typed event channel — happy to follow up with a PR for it. The sweep here is the user-visible band-aid that unblocks moves now, including for users with pre-existing orphans on disk who'd otherwise need shell access to clean them up. Once the daemon-side change lands, the sweep stays useful as a one-time migration path for legacy data and as defense-in-depth (one \`readdir\` per move when the destination already exists; no cost in the common case).

## Test plan

- [ ] Drag a top-level item into a parent whose directory already contains an entry with the same name and real content. Toast: \`\"An item named ... already exists in ... Rename or remove it first.\"\`
- [ ] Drag into a parent where the destination is a hollow \`.agents/.conversations/\` orphan from a prior move. Drag succeeds; the orphan is gone.
- [ ] Drag into a parent where the destination is a user-created empty folder (no scaffolding, no files). Friendly error fires; the empty folder is *not* swept.
- [ ] Manually create \`<dest>/some-file.txt\` inside an otherwise-empty destination. Drag in. Friendly error fires (file present → not hollow → not swept).
- [ ] Cross-device move (linked external cabinet on another mount) still falls through to copy+delete via the existing \`EXDEV\` branch.

author: bravo1goingdark
body:
## Summary

\`Archiver::probe()\` was synchronous but called \`Handle::current().block_on()\` on an async S3 head request. The startup path that invokes it (\`Server::run_inner\`) is async — sitting inside the tokio runtime created in \`keplor-cli/main.rs:run_server\`. tokio explicitly disallows nested \`block_on\`, so anyone enabling \`--features s3\` and configuring \`[archive]\` hits this immediately on startup:

\`\`\`
thread 'main' panicked at crates/keplor-store/src/archive.rs:74:49:
Cannot start a runtime from within a runtime. This happens because a function (like \`block_on\`) attempted to block the current thread while the thread is being used to drive asynchronous tasks.
\`\`\`

This is the first time the s3 feature shipped live, so the bug had no production exposure before now.

## Fix

- \`Archiver::probe()\` → async fn, awaits \`self.client.head\` directly.
- Single caller in \`keplor-server/src/server.rs:304\` updated to \`.await\` it.

3-line change.

## Verified

End-to-end against a real Cloudflare R2 bucket — startup log:

\`\`\`
{"level":"INFO","message":"event archival configured — S3 connectivity verified","bucket":"keplor-log","archive_after_hours":720,"archive_threshold_mb":15000,"interval_secs":3600}
\`\`\`

\`/health\` 200, no panic.

## Test plan

- [x] cargo build --release -p keplor-cli --features s3
- [x] Live startup against R2 bucket with valid credentials → "S3 connectivity verified" message appears
- [x] Live startup against bogus credentials should now fail-and-disable archival cleanly (probe returns Err, archival disabled, server keeps running)

#### Relevant issue or PR

Follow up to https://github.com/pasteurlabs/tesseract-core/pull/555 ; in that pr, the schema emitted by the `InputPath` / `OutputPath` models didn't contain `"format": "path"`, making it difficult to distinguish them from plain strings from the schema alone.

This is done to improve consistency with schemas generated by pydantic for paths (which are not just marked as strings, but also contain `"format": "path"`; this consistency, in turn, makes it easier for applications orchestrating Tesseracts to distinguish paths from plain strings.

For more detail, have a look at the changed lines in the test, in particular `{"title": "Inp", "type": "string"}` (no format present).

#### Description of changes

Restored the format: path annotation Pydantic emits for plain pathlib.Path fields, lost when we override __get_pydantic_core_schema__

#### Testing done

Local pytest + hopefully CI passes

## Description
Fix `rotation_trig_lut port not found` error in cache rotation

`ModelRunner` was calling `set_tensor("rotation_trig_lut", ...)` but the OV model exposes the input parameter as "model_rotation_trig_lut" (named by `StateManagementPattern` in OpenVINO transformations). This name mismatch caused a `RuntimeError: Port for tensor name rotation_trig_lut was not found` whenever `CacheEvictionConfig.apply_rotation = True` was set.

**Root cause:** After PR https://github.com/openvinotoolkit/openvino/pull/35500 moved the `SDPAToPagedAttention` call to runtime in `pipeline_impl.cpp`, the discrepancy between the parameter name created by the transformation "model_rotation_trig_lut" and the name used in `model_runner.hpp`: "rotation_trig_lut" became a runtime failure.

**Fix:** Correct the tensor name in `model_runner.hpp` to match what `StateManagementPattern` actually registers as a named model input.

body:
## Summary

Closes the post-#57 audit punch list for track 1.1 (UI completeness round 2). Eight commits across backend pipeline, API, and frontend covering four GitHub issues plus two roborev findings caught during review.

- **#61 (bug-84db2d3c)** — `run_phase_iter` no longer swallows uncaught exceptions; emits a terminal `phase_failed` event with the exception class+message so SSE consumers see a clear error instead of a silent stream end.
- **#59 (feat-6e148975)** — application-detail phase tracker + header status badge now react to SSE `event: phase` frames, transitioning gather→draft→render and flipping running→failed/done. Was stuck at `queued/queued/queued` after the initial GET.
- **#60 (feat-092c5a2c)** — `useApplication` retries the detail GET on 404 (5× 200ms backoff) so the modal-launched flow no longer flashes the dashboard empty-state during the post-POST propagation window.
- **#56 follow-up (feat-bb81c3ce)** — `GET /api/applications/{slug}` now exposes `apply_url` from the latest run's jd-parsed artifact; the re-run-apply button stays enabled and POSTs `{apply_url, force: true}` instead of routing every completed slug to the CLI tooltip.
- **roborev job 947 (HIGH)** — `useApplication` resets `data`/`error`/`isLoading` at the start of every effect run, so navigating between slugs never renders the prior slug's URL under the new one.
- **roborev job 948 (MEDIUM)** — `setRunning(false)` on `phaseNum===3` done so the header badge transitions to `done` instead of staying stuck on `running` after a streamed render completion.

## Commits

```
619c677 fix(web): clear running flag on SSE render/done (roborev job 948)
c22cd42 fix(web): reset useApplication state on slug change (roborev job 947 HIGH)
ae0f194 chore: ruff import sort
f1d21af feat(web): use apply_url for re-run-apply (feat-bb81c3ce frontend)
ee1fef9 fix(web): retry GET after POST 201 (feat-092c5a2c, #60)
cb1a014 feat(api): expose apply_url on GET /applications/{slug} (feat-bb81c3ce)
f5b5425 feat(web): wire phase tracker + status badge to SSE (feat-6e148975, #59)
8e32a13 fix(pipeline): emit terminal phase_failed on apply errors (bug-84db2d3c, #61)
```

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest -x` — 130/130 targeted tests pass (apply pipeline + apply_url API)
- [x] `cd web && npm run typecheck && npm test -- --run` — 128/128 frontend tests pass (15 new)
- [x] roborev branch review (job 948) — closed, no further findings on the post-fix branch
- [x] Live UI validation against worktree code (vite + jobsmith api serve restarted from worktree):
  - apply_url null path → button disabled with CLI tooltip
  - apply_url present → button enabled, role/company surfaced, POST fires with `force=true`
  - SSE `<<PHASE>> render status=backfilled` flips badge running→done and PHASE 3 to "done · 12.1s"
  - Slug-change navigation clears stale data immediately (no flash)
  - No console errors

## Follow-up

Filed [#63](https://github.com/shakestzd/jobsmith/issues/63) (htmlgraph `bug-ac784d62`) for the deeper architectural concern surfaced during validation: the API reads only `specialist_outputs` for artifacts and apply_url, while pre-dual-write runs and failed-mid-gather runs leave the data on disk only. Track 0.8 landed dual-write but the API contract was never updated to fall back to `.apply-state/`. Out of scope for this PR — separate follow-up track.

author: klappy
body:
## tl;dr
#47 merged. It plugged 5 Bugbot findings with 3 worker-side patches but: **(a)** the structure (TransformStream + waitUntil pump + setTimeout callback all sharing one writer) is what's inviting the findings, and **(b)** the wrapper STILL emits zero bytes during the first 15s on an idle session — which is the exact iOS Safari "Load failed" failure mode #47 was supposed to fix.

Verified post-#47-merge against ams.truthkit.ai:
```
$ AMS_URL=https://ams.truthkit.ai bash scripts/check-sse-heartbeat.sh
  bytes received in 25s: 8
  first 200 bytes: : ping  ← first byte arrived at +15s, not immediately
VERDICT: PASS
```
The validator passes (its budget is 25s) but iOS Safari's streaming-fetch watchdog can fire shorter than 15s in real cellular conditions. That's why the iPhone may still show the red frame.

## What this PR does
Replaces `wrapWithSseHeartbeat` with a **single-loop ReadableStream**. ~30 lines of mechanism instead of ~70.

```
const SSE_LEADING_FLUSH = new TextEncoder().encode(":ok\n\n");
...
async start(controller) {
  controller.enqueue(SSE_LEADING_FLUSH);          // ← +0ms flush
  reader = upstream.getReader();
  try {
    while (true) {
      let timeoutId;
      const heartbeat = new Promise(r => { timeoutId = setTimeout(() => r({heartbeat:true}), 15_000); });
      const next = await Promise.race([
        reader.read().then(r => { clearTimeout(timeoutId); return r; }),
        heartbeat,
      ]);
      if ("heartbeat" in next) { controller.enqueue(SSE_HEARTBEAT_FRAME); continue; }
      if (next.done) break;
      if (next.value) controller.enqueue(next.value);
    }
  } catch {} finally { try { controller.close(); } catch {} }
},
cancel(reason) {
  // hoisted reader so we don't trip the locked-stream TypeError
  if (reader) reader.cancel(reason).catch(() => {});
  else upstream.cancel(reason).catch(() => {});
}
```

## Why every Bugbot finding becomes impossible by construction
| Finding | Old structure cause | This structure |
|---|---|---|
| #2 Heartbeat leaks on disconnect | pump blocked on read, setInterval keeps firing | `cancel()` calls `reader.cancel()` → propagates to upstream → loop's `read()` rejects → finally closes |
| #4 Mid-event heartbeat injection | setInterval + shared writer interleaves bytes | heartbeat only enqueues between full upstream chunks (one writer, sequential loop) |
| #5 Re-arm race orphans timeouts | `armHeartbeat` overwrites `heartbeat` from two paths | one timer per loop iteration, cleared the moment `read()` resolves |

No `setInterval`, no `armHeartbeat`, no `closed` flag, no `cleanup` function. Removed all the shared mutable state the Bugbot findings orbit around.

## Local proof
4/4 tests pass — see commit message. Bug found and fixed during testing: `upstream.cancel()` on a stream locked to a reader throws and silently swallows; needed `reader.cancel()` via hoisted reader. Caught BEFORE push. (Fresh-iteration discipline: the proof script flushed out the bug the simpler shape would have shipped with.)

## After merge
1. CF Workers Build deploys to both hostnames.
2. Re-run `bash scripts/check-sse-heartbeat.sh` against either host — should still PASS, but with first bytes containing `:ok\n\n` arriving immediately instead of `: ping\n\n` at +15s.
3. Open `ams.truthkit.ai/` on your iPhone, click Mint in §A TinCan. Red frame should be gone.
4. If iPhone STILL shows it, the necessary-cause hypothesis is wrong — fall back to plan B (drop SSE leg from homepage, use ams_recv long-poll, already shipped as the documented degradation path).

## Follow-ups
- Tighten `scripts/check-sse-heartbeat.sh` MAX_IDLE_S default 25s → 2s to catch a future leading-byte regression (small one-line change).
- Canon-only PR adding `fresh-iteration-over-steering` as a tier-2 constraint, citing this PR + `journal/2026-05-05-curl-claim-done-incident.tsv` as two co-occurring instances of the same structural failure pattern in 24 hours.
- Upstream issue/PR against `cloudflare/agents` for SDK-native keepalive at `dist/mcp/index.js` GET handler.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches the Worker’s long-lived SSE response path; while the new single-loop stream reduces concurrency hazards, mistakes here could break notification streaming or fail to tear down upstream connections on disconnect.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Improves SSE liveness on iOS Safari** by changing the GET `text/event-stream` wrapper to emit an immediate leading SSE comment (`:ok\n\n`) instead of waiting up to 15s for the first heartbeat.
> 
> **Replaces the prior TransformStream + `waitUntil` pump + shared-writer timeout design** with a single sequential `ReadableStream` loop that races `reader.read()` vs a per-iteration timeout, enqueues `:keepalive\n\n` only between upstream chunks, and propagates downstream `cancel()` to `reader.cancel()` to avoid leaks.
> 
> Adds a journal entry documenting the post-#47 idle-byte gap and the rationale for the fresh-iteration rewrite.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 787b8b6dddaa2c9d0dea9aa5bd7055da91bf78f9. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

### Motivation
- Align UI and accounting sign conventions so positive excesses are presented consistently and journal amounts match expected debit/credit signs.
- Fix incorrect positive display of `totalCalc` in the table when it represents an excess, and ensure `Monto USD` in SAP rows uses the correct sign for consumption.

### Description

- Kept existing debit/credit population logic for `Débito (ME)` and `Crédito (ME)` intact while ensuring the exported USD column matches the journal sign conventions.
