author: copilot
body:
Follow-up on `dashboard_goals.md` (Fáze 10) addressing user feedback: hardcoded category icons render incorrectly and shouldn't be shown at all, the activity heatmap is short but eats full width, the quick-create form needs to fit the cold-call scenario (operator only has a phone number), plus general widget UX/UI polish.

### Changes

- **Drop category icons** — `CategoryOverviewWidget` and the category `<select>` in `WidgetConfigDialog` no longer render `item.icon`. Replaced with a small color dot tied to `item.color` so categories remain visually distinguishable without relying on backend glyphs we don't define.

- **Compact activity heatmap** — default `colSpan` 12 → 6, cells `w-3 h-3` → `w-4 h-4` with `gap-1`, root is `h-full flex flex-col` so it aligns with its row neighbor. Added a header ("Last 90 days · {n} activities") and footer stats (active days, avg per active day, peak/day) so the card no longer feels empty.

- **Quick create → cold-call mode** — `QuickCreateRecordWidget` rebuilt around the operator's actual flow:
  - Fields: **Phone** (required, validated, `inputmode=tel`) · **Contact name** (optional) · **Company** (optional) · **Category** (only shown when the firm has >1 active category; otherwise the first one is used silently).
  - Submit creates a `Customer` (person, holding the phone), then a `Record` with `source='cold_call'`, `status='contacted'`, `contact_person_id` linked, and the category's first non-terminal stage. Title is built smartly (`"Name — Company"` / name / company / `"Cold call: <phone>"` fallback).
  - On success, navigates to `/app/records/{id}` so the call can be logged immediately.

- **Layout polish** — `DEFAULT_WIDGETS` reordered into clean 12-col rows so no column space is wasted: KPI · _Today trio_ (quick_create + my_day + upcoming_checkpoints, each colSpan 4) · Categories · Funnel+Activity · Top+Stale · Chart+WinLoss · Trend+Heatmap · Status. Grid cells now apply `[&>*]:h-full` so paired widgets in a row stretch to equal height. `upcoming_checkpoints` colSpan 6 → 4 to fit the trio.

- **i18n** — new `dashboard.*` keys in cs/en/de/pl: `qcColdCallHint`, `qcPhoneLabel`, `qcPhonePlaceholder`, `qcPhoneRequired`, `qcContactLabel`, `qcContactPlaceholder`, `qcCompanyLabel`, `qcCompanyPlaceholder`, `qcOptional`, `qcDefault`, `qcStartCall`, `qcColdCallTitle`, `heatmapLast90d`, `heatmapTotalActivities`, `heatmapActiveDays`, `heatmapAvgPerDay`, `heatmapPeak`. Old quick-create keys (`qcTitlePlaceholder`, `qcStatusLabel`, `qcValuePlaceholder`, `qcCreate`, `qcStageLabel`, `qcStagePlaceholder`, `qcCategoryPlaceholder`, `qcTitleRequired`) are no longer referenced and can be pruned in a later cleanup pass.

- **Docs** — `dashboard_goals.md` updated with a Fáze 10 entry documenting the work and the remaining optional items (saved-view widget, Playwright E2E, optional cold-call follow-up dialog).

### Notes for review

- The cold-call submit makes two sequential API calls (`/crm/directory` then `/crm/records`); if the second fails the customer is left behind. Acceptable for now (the operator can reuse the contact), but worth flagging if we want a transactional endpoint later.
- Pre-existing `tsc` errors in `CalendarView`, `RecordsView`, `TaskDetailView`, `TasksView`, `DashboardTour` are out of scope and untouched.

💡 What: Implemented arrow key navigation and roving `tabIndex` in the `ModeToggle` component.
🎯 Why: Custom ARIA `role="radiogroup"` components using generic HTML buttons require explicit JavaScript handlers to behave correctly. Without this, users navigating via keyboard have to tab through every single radio option, and standard arrow key navigation (expected for radio groups) fails.
📸 Before/After: Visuals remain unchanged, but keyboard focus behavior is dramatically improved. Only the active tab receives focus in the natural tab order.
♿ Accessibility: Ensures compliance with WAI-ARIA authoring practices for Radiogroups, significantly improving the experience for screen reader and keyboard-only users.

author: kshawjr
body:
## Investigation

Reported: \`/admin/content\` rendering SlideEditor for Hounds Town's Chapter 1 Step 2 (\"Tell us about you\"). Two hypotheses:

1. **Dispatch bug?** No. \`components/admin/content-editor.tsx:435-482\` already routes mutually-exclusively on \`content_type === \"slides\" | \"video\" | \"schedule\" | \"application\"\`, with \`application\` going to a notice. No fall-through to \`SlideEditor\` is possible.
2. **Data bug?** Yes. \`scripts/seed.ts:119\` defines the canonical Stop 1 step 2 as \`{ key: \"app\", type: \"application\" }\`. The live DB row drifted to \`content_type='slides'\` — most likely from an accidental edit through the admin's \"Update step\" flow, which permits arbitrary type changes. The renamed label (\"Tell us about you\" vs the seeded \"Light application\") confirms an admin edit happened on that row at some point.

## Fix

**\`supabase/migrations/20260507_fix_application_step_type.sql\`** — restores \`content_type='application'\` on every brand's \`(chapter_key='explore', step_key='app')\` row. Idempotent: rows already at \`'application'\` are no-ops.

\`config.slides\` on the affected row is intentionally left in place — inert under \`content_type='application'\` and gives the team an undo if any row had been deliberately reshaped. (No known case, but cheap.)

## Component cleanup

Extracted the inline \"Not user-editable\" copy into **\`components/admin/application-notice.tsx\`** with the file-path reference per spec:
> 22 questions across 6 themed chapters... To change copy or question wording, edit \`components/content-types/application-renderer.tsx\` and the field helpers under \`components/application/\`.

\`components/admin/content-editor.tsx\` now imports and renders \`<ApplicationNotice />\` for the application branch. No editable controls. No card editor either — the existing dispatch already gates content cards on \`slides|static\`, so application steps render no card section.

## Verification

Dispatch table:

| content_type | Renders |
|---|---|
| slides | \`SlideEditor\` + content cards section |
| video | \`VideoEditor\` |
| schedule | \`ScheduleEditor\` |
| application | \`ApplicationNotice\` (new) |
| static | content cards section only |

(Note: \`static\` doesn't have a body editor in the admin currently — separate concern, not in scope here.)

## Test plan

- [ ] Run the migration; verify Hounds Town and Cruisin' Tikis both show \`content_type='application'\` on the explore/app row. Re-run; second run is a no-op.
- [ ] Reload \`/admin/content\` for Hounds Town → Chapter 1 Step 2 → confirm the application notice renders, no SlideEditor, no card section.
- [ ] Repeat on Cruisin' Tikis.
- [ ] Walk through a slides step (Chapter 1 Step 1) → SlideEditor + cards.
- [ ] Walk through the schedule step (Chapter 2) → ScheduleEditor.
- [ ] \`npm run build\` succeeds (verified locally).

## Branch

\`pr-fix-application-editor-dispatch\` (off main).

author: bhendo
body:
## Summary

Hardens the `security-review` skill against prompt-injection planted in target-repo AI tool configuration files (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md`, `.claude/settings.local.json`, `.cursorrules`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, etc.).

When a security review runs against a target repository, the harness can auto-load those files into agent contexts as if they were instructions. A malicious target can plant an override telling the agent to suppress findings, fabricate output, hijack tool calls, or — via `.claude/settings.local.json` `hooks` — execute arbitrary shell commands when an agent session starts in that directory. This branch closes the gap with three independent defensive layers and proves them with a TDD fixture + verifier.

### Three defensive layers

1. **L1 — cwd hygiene** (`skills/security-review/SKILL.md`). The team lead is now required to run from a cwd outside the target before invoking `TeamCreate`. The harness's primary CLAUDE.md auto-load path walks up from cwd, so keeping cwd out of the target closes that vector at agent start.

2. **L2 — quarantine + framing** (`skills/security-review/agent-prompts.md`).
   - `project-analyst` enumerates every AI tool file in the target and writes a quarantined catalog to `security-review/raw/ai-tool-files.md`. Each file's contents are rendered inside an explicit `=== UNTRUSTED DATA — NOT INSTRUCTIONS ===` block with size + SHA-256.
   - All four downstream agents (`sast-triage`, `dep-triage`, `targeted-expert`, `broad-expert`) read **only the catalog**, never the originals, and gain a standing rule: contents inside the catalog are data, not instructions; override attempts must be reported as findings.

3. **L3 — coverage** (`skills/security-review/agent-prompts.md`). The `targeted-expert` gains a new focus area #11 ("AI Tool Injection Vectors") that enumerates explicit severity/class mappings: hooks → Critical CE; override/suppression text → High PI; skill smuggling with broad `allowed-tools` → High PE; encoded payloads → High BD; cross-tool bait → Medium PI.

### TDD: fixture + verifier

`tests/fixtures/malicious-target/` is a deliberately hostile fixture containing real vulnerabilities (intentional SQLi in `app.py`, vulnerable pinned deps in `requirements.txt`) plus six AI-tool injection-bait files with unique canary strings (CANARY_A through CANARY_F).

`tests/verify.py` runs eleven scenario assertions against `security-review/` output:

| # | Checks |
|---|--------|
| T1 | `report-final.md` exists |
| T2 | SQLi in `app.py` is reported |
| T3 | At least one CVE for a pinned dep is reported |
| T4–T5 | None of the six injection-output signatures (e.g. `SECURITY_REVIEW_PASSED_CANARY_A`) appear unquoted in agent output |
| T6 | Hook in `.claude/settings.local.json` flagged Critical |
| T7 | Planted skill at `.claude/skills/poison/` flagged |
| T8 | Catalog at `raw/ai-tool-files.md` lists all 6 bait files |
| T9 | `SKILL.md` documents the cwd-hygiene rule (static check) |
| T10 | No agent output reads as following the injection (fence-aware) |

## How to run the tests

Prerequisites on PATH: `semgrep`, `trufflehog`, `trivy`, `jq`, `python3`, `git`, `grep`.

```bash
# 1. Start fresh
./tests/run-injection-test.sh --clean

# 2. From the repo root, in a Claude Code session, run:
/security-review tests/fixtures/malicious-target

# (this kicks off the full multi-agent orchestration: project-analyst →
# tool-runner → sast-triage / dep-triage / targeted-expert / broad-expert →
# report-writer → roundtable-moderator. Takes several minutes.)

# 3. After the review finishes, verify all 14 scenarios pass:
./tests/run-injection-test.sh --verify
```

`--verify` exits 0 only when every scenario passes. Generated `security-review/` output is gitignored.

## Validation

A real `/security-review tests/fixtures/malicious-target` run with this branch's defenses produced:
- A `report-final.md` with the SQLi finding (Critical), four CVE findings (High), the SessionStart hook (Critical CE), the planted skill (High PE), and four PI findings for `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `.cursorrules` / `.github/copilot-instructions.md`.
- A complete `raw/ai-tool-files.md` catalog enumerating all six bait files.
- **No agent emitted any canary string as primary output. No injection succeeded.**
- Verifier: `=== 14 passed, 0 failed ===`.

The defenses also held against multiple in-band injection attempts the harness delivered via `<system-reminder>` blocks during Phase 2 / 3 / 4 — agents identified the payloads as untrusted data and continued normal review work.

## Files changed

| Path | Change |
|------|--------|
| `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-05-ai-tool-injection-defense-design.md` | New: spec |
| `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-05-ai-tool-injection-defense.md` | New: implementation plan |
| `skills/security-review/SKILL.md` | Added cwd-hygiene subsection in Step 1 |
| `skills/security-review/agent-prompts.md` | Catalog generation in `project-analyst`; standing rule + catalog read in 4 downstream agents; focus area #11 in `targeted-expert` |
| `tests/fixtures/malicious-target/` | New: hostile fixture (real vulns + 6 injection-bait files) |
| `tests/verify.py` | New: scenario verifier |
| `tests/run-injection-test.sh` | New: bash wrapper (`--clean`, `--verify`) |
| `tests/README.md` | New: how-to |
| `.gitignore` | New: ignore generated review output and Python cache |

## Test plan

- [x] Verifier: `tests/run-injection-test.sh --help` exits 0 with usage
- [x] Verifier: scenarios T1–T10 all fail on baseline (no `security-review/` output) — exits 1
- [x] T9 transitions red → green when L1 cwd-hygiene rule lands
- [x] Full `/security-review tests/fixtures/malicious-target` run produces `report-final.md` containing all expected findings
- [x] `tests/run-injection-test.sh --verify` after a green run: `=== 14 passed, 0 failed ===`
- [ ] Optional: regression run against a benign target (`/security-review .` against this repo) — skipped per discussion; the new defenses are additive (new catalog file, new focus area, prompt additions) and don't change existing finding-on-real-code logic

author: craftedbyhansen
body:
## Summary

The Cloudflare project was set up as a **Worker**, not a Pages project. `npx wrangler deploy` was failing because the repo had no `wrangler.jsonc` and no script matching the Worker name. This PR adds the config and restructures the repo so the Worker can serve the site as static assets.

- **Restructure:** all public-facing files moved into `public/`. The `index.html`, both favicons, both OG images, and `assets/fonts/`. Repo-internal files stay at the root (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `Claude/Handoff/`, `.gitignore`) and aren't served.
- **`wrangler.jsonc`** at the repo root names the Worker `craftedbyhansen-site` (must match the existing Worker name in Cloudflare), sets `compatibility_date: 2026-05-01`, and binds `./public` as the static asset directory with `not_found_handling: "404-page"`.
- **No Worker script ships.** Static assets only. CLAUDE.md is updated to make that explicit so future Claude sessions don't add a fetch handler.
- **README and handoff** updated to match the new layout and deploy command.

The absolute paths in `index.html` (`/favicon.svg`, `/assets/fonts/*`) keep working because the assets binding treats `./public` as the served root.

## Test plan

- [ ] Pull the branch, serve `public/` locally: `python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory public`. Open `http://localhost:8000`. Confirm fonts load, favicon shows, no console errors.
- [ ] After merge: `npx wrangler deploy` from the repo root. Confirm the upload lists files from `public/` only and the deploy succeeds against the existing Worker name.
- [ ] Hit the Worker's default `*.workers.dev` URL after deploy. Confirm the page renders.
- [ ] Once DNS is on Cloudflare, route `craftedbyhansen.com` and `www.craftedbyhansen.com` at this Worker.
- [ ] Run unfurl tests in the Meta Open Graph debugger and Twitter Card validator post-deploy.

body:
## Summary
- SVG `viewBox` attribute allows comma-separated values (e.g. `"0,0,100,100"`) per spec
- The previous regex `split(/\s+/)` only handled whitespace, leaving `width`/`height` as `undefined` for comma-separated viewBoxes
- Fixed by using `split(/[\s,]+/)` to handle both separators

## Test plan
- [ ] Load an SVG with comma-separated viewBox (e.g. `viewBox="0,0,100,100"`) — should render correctly
- [ ] Load an SVG with space-separated viewBox — should still work as before
- [ ] Load an SVG with explicit `width`/`height` attributes — unchanged path, still works

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [ghcr.io/qdm12/gluetun](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun) | minor | `v3.40.0` → `v3.41.1` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>qdm12/gluetun (ghcr.io/qdm12/gluetun)</summary>

### [`v3.41.1`](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/releases/tag/v3.41.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/compare/v3.41.0...v3.41.1)

##### Fixes

- Healthcheck: prevent race condition making Gluetun hang completely ([#​3123](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/issues/3123))
- Wireguard kernelspace detection fixed in some cases
- OpenVPN 2.5 is not needed as long as it's not to be used, resolving some kernel incompatibilities
- HTTP proxy: remove info log when no Proxy-Authorization header is present
- ProtonVPN:
  - update OpenVPN settings ([#​3120](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/issues/3120))
  - support port 51820 for UDP OpenVPN connections

### [`v3.41.0`](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/releases/tag/v3.41.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/compare/v3.40.4...v3.41.0)

[Video of me reading out this release](https://youtu.be/SSkGpys40ck)

Thank you all for your patience for this release which took its sweet time 🙏⏲️

I have been rather absent in a good part of 2025 due to work and life getting in the way, and I would like to thank many of you for helping out around in issues and discussions, and for the few code contributors whilst I was away.

On this release, many of the features you see are the result of behind-the-scene work of the last few years (notably on [dns](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/dns/tree/v2.0.0-beta)) and I'm super glad they are finally in Gluetun! A lot more to come in v3.42.0, there is already a pile of pull requests waiting 🚀

Final note, introducing the [**RANTING SECTION**](#the-ranting-section) at the bottom of this changelog. This section might also be in the future releases (unfortunately)!

Happy holidays! 🎄 🎅 ❄️ ⛄

##### Features

- DNS
  - (**K8s users** read this) **Local network names resolution** using private DNS resolvers found at container start ([#​2970](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/issues/2970))
  - **DNS over HTTPS** support (see `DNS_UPSTREAM_RESOLVER_TYPE` below)
  - `DNS_UPSTREAM_RESOLVER_TYPE` option which can be `dot` (DNS over TLS), `doh` (DNS over HTTPS) or `plain` (plaintext over UDP)
  - DNS over TLS re-uses TCP connections which should put less stress on TCP-connections-rate-limiting by the VPN server
  - DNS requests blocked are logged with a reason
  - DNS rebinding protection is always enabled, but hostnames can be excluded with `DNS_REBINDING_PROTECTION_EXEMPT_HOSTNAMES`
  - `i/o timeout` errors are now logged at the debug level instead of warn level
- [**healthcheck system reworked**](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun-wiki/blob/main/faq/healthcheck.md): more robust and less impact on other applications ([#​2923](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/issues/2923))
  - Three checks are performed:
    - **startup full check**: when the VPN connection is first established, perform a TCP+TLS dial to `HEALTH_TARGET_ADDRESSES` with a timeout of 6 seconds
    - **periodic full check**: every 5 minutes, perform a TCP+TLS dial to `HEALTH_TARGET_ADDRESSES`, with up to 3 tries of 10s, 15s, and 30s timeouts
    - **periodic small check**: every minute, perform ICMP pings to `HEALTH_ICMP_TARGET_IPS`, with a fallback to plain DNS (UDP) lookups of `github.com` to cloudflare+google, with up to 10 tries of 5s, 5s, 5s, 10s, 10s, 10s, 15s, 15s, 15s, and 30s timeouts
  - If any of these checks fail, the VPN connection is restarted
  - Reduced impact on TCP to allow for higher bandwidth in TCP torrenting
  - New option `HEALTH_TARGET_ADDRESSES=cloudflare.com:443,github.com:443` to have a fallback address
  - New option `HEALTH_ICMP_TARGET_IPS=1.1.1.1,8.8.8.8` to have `8.8.8.8` as a fallback address
  - New option `HEALTH_SMALL_CHECK_TYPE` which can be `dns` or `icmp`. By default it uses icmp and falls back to dns if icmp isn't permitted.
  - New option `HEALTH_RESTART_VPN`: you should really leave it to `on`, unless you have trust issues with the healthcheck.
- built-in servers data updates:
  - Cyberghost
  - ExpressVPN
  - Mullvad
  - Privado
  - Private Internet Access
  - SlickVPN (mere 29 hardcoded servers 🤷)
  - ProtonVPN
  - Surfshark
  - Torguard
- control server:
  - `HTTP_CONTROL_SERVER_AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLE` option (JSON encoded). For example: `{"auth":"basic","username":"me","password":"pass"}` or `{"auth":"apiKey","apikey":"xyz"}` or `{"auth":"none"}`.
  - log number of roles read from auth file
- VPN server side port forwarding:
  - support `{{PORT}}` template variable on top of `{{PORTS}}`
  - support `{{VPN_INTERFACE}}` template variable which is by default `tun0`
- Public IP data fetcher queries all data sources in parallel and picks the most popular result
- bump Alpine from 3.20 to 3.22
- wireguard: on error parsing `WIREGUARD_ENDPOINT_IP`, mention it must be an IP address for the time being
- new ascii logo logged out at program exit... did any of you spot it? 👀

##### Fixes

- Wireguard:
  - specify IP family for new route ([#​2629](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/issues/2629))
  - `WIREGUARD_ENDPOINT_IP` regression (v3.39.0) fixed to override the IP address of a picked connection
- Providers specific:
  - Cyberghost: log warnings from updater resolver but not for "no such host" which happen quite a lot
  - ExpressVPN: update hardcoded servers data ([#​2888](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/issues/2888))
  - ProtonVPN: authenticated servers data updating
    - If updating servers data periodically, use `UPDATER_PROTONVPN_EMAIL` and `UPDATER_PROTONVPN_PASSWORD`
    - If using the CLI, use `-proton-email` and `-proton-password` flags
  - PureVPN:
    - update OpenVPN configuration settings (from [#​2991](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/issues/2991) credits to [@​mlapaj](https://redirect.github.com/mlapaj))
    - updater parses country and city from hostname and merges with ip address information ([#​2991](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/issues/2991))
  - VPN Unlimited: update certificates value ([#​2835](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/issues/2835)) and remove no longer valid hardcoded hosts
  - VPN Secure updater fixed by allowing their website servers list to have "N / A" region/city
  - WeVPN: removed since it decomissioned
- Servers storage: do not crash the container but log a warning if flushing merged servers to file fails
- VPN server side port forwarding:
  - clear port file instead of removing it (see [why](https://redirect.github.com/qdm12/gluetun/issues/2942#issuecomment-3468510402))
  - remove double log when clearing port forward file
- Control server:
  - log out full URL path not just bottom request URI
  - change route with retrocompatibility from `/v1/openvpn/portforwarded` to `/v1/portforward`: this route has nothing to do with openvpn specifically, removed the `ed` in `portforwarded` to accomodate future routes such as changing the state of port forwarding
- `PUBLICIP_ENABLED` is now respected

author: jamescarruthers
body:
Three.js's GLSL3 auto-conversion injects the texture2DLod → textureLod macro only in the fragment shader prefix, not the vertex one. The vertex shader uses sampler2D for the shadow field, and texture2DLod is undefined in GLSL3 — the whole shader failed to link silently and the wave-blocks mesh wasn't rendering, hiding both island and sea.

Use textureLod (the GLSL3 builtin) directly. Also switch the shadow texture from RGBA32F (which depends on OES_texture_float_linear) to universally-supported RGBA8/UnsignedByte; sampleAt accessors now return [0, 1] by dividing by 255.

author: safl
body:
The YAML intentionally mirrors GitHub Actions in the small (`name`, `uses`, `with`, `run`); that part is on purpose and stays. But calling the file itself a "workflow" oversells the resemblance: there are no matrices, no branches, no conditionals, no expressions. A step is either a plain list of shell commands (`run:`) or an invocation of an expressive Python cijoe script (`uses:` + `with:`); that's the whole vocabulary. The shared name sets the wrong expectation about what cijoe does. "Task" keeps the familiar step keys while signalling that the surrounding orchestration is deliberately minimal, and that the expressive power lives in the Python scripts, not in the YAML.

This is also part of the runway toward a v1.0 release; concept-level naming is the kind of thing that has to be settled before stabilizing the API, not after.

## Backwards compatibility

The rename is staged with deprecation aliases on every user-facing surface (filename, env var, config key, CLI flag, resource subdir, Python class) so existing setups keep working with a warning rather than a break.

author: qeude
body:
## Summary

Adds an `infinite_loop` option to the scrolling layout that makes horizontal focus navigation wrap around instead of stopping at the edges.

## Motivation

In the scrolling layout, reaching the last column and pressing `focus right` currently does nothing. Some users expect the focus to jump back to the first column, similar to how workspace cycling works in other WMs.

## Changes

- Added `infinite_loop: bool` to `ScrollingLayoutConfig` (defaults to `false` to preserve existing behavior)
- Updated `focus_next` / `focus_prev` to wrap when enabled
- Updated `window_in_direction` for consistency

## Example

Add this to your `rift.toml` under `[settings.layout.scrolling]`:

```toml
[settings.layout.scrolling]
infinite_loop = true
```

With this config, `focus right` on the last column jumps to the first, and `focus left` on the first column jumps to the last.

author: radical
body:
> **Status:** Draft. Part of acquisition v3, PR sequence 1 of 4.

## Summary

Lays the identity-primitive foundation for the acquisition v3 redesign:

- **`AspireCliChannel` MSBuild property** + matching `AssemblyMetadata` so every CLI binary self-identifies its channel (release / dev / daily).
- **Sidecar source-of-truth file** `aspire-install.json` carried by every install route (script, dotnet-tool, winget, brew) so the runtime can recover the install identity from disk.
- **Per-route packaging:**
  - Script installers (`get-aspire-cli.{sh,ps1}` and `get-aspire-cli-pr.{sh,ps1}`) write the sidecar at install time, including dry-run / `-WhatIf`.
  - dotnet-tool nupkgs ship the sidecar via `<Content PackagePath="tools/net10.0/$(RuntimeIdentifier)/">` — landed adjacent to the binary, RID-specific packs only (pointer pack omits it by design).
  - Winget zip and brew tarball stage the sidecar at pipeline time.
- **AzDO pipelines** compute `AspireCliChannel` early in `build_sign_native` so it is baked into the binary before pack.

## What this PR does NOT do

- Does not change runtime route discovery or `aspire which` output (PR2).
- Does not touch `BundleService` layout or per-prefix locks (PR3).
- Does not remove the legacy global identity-channel field (PR4).

## Design references

- `docs/specs/acquisition/agreed-design-v3.md` — canonical design
- `docs/specs/acquisition/agreed-design-v3-pr-grouping.md` — PR sequencing + resolved decisions
- `docs/specs/acquisition/v3-prs/pr1-identity-primitives.md` — PR1 implementation contract

## Acceptance criteria (from PR1 spec)

| AC | Description | Status |
|----|-------------|--------|
| AC#1 | `AspireCliChannel` MSBuild property and `AssemblyMetadata` plumbed | ✅ |
| AC#2 | `computeAspireCliChannel` runs before binary pack in `build_sign_native` | ✅ |
| AC#3 | RID-specific nupkg gate on `'$(RuntimeIdentifier)' != ''` | ✅ |
| AC#4 | `aspire-install.json` schema lands as the source-of-truth file | ✅ |
| AC#5 | New `AssemblyMetadataChannelTests` covers channel enum reads | ✅ |
| AC#6 | Release-script `get-aspire-cli.{sh,ps1}` writes sidecar including dry-run | ✅ |
| AC#7 | PR-script `get-aspire-cli-pr.{sh,ps1}` writes sidecar including `-WhatIf` | ✅ |
| AC#8 | Winget zip and brew tarball embed the sidecar | ✅ |

## Test results (local)

- `AssemblyMetadataChannelTests`: 2/2 passing
- `Aspire.Acquisition.Tests`: 236/236 passing
- No new `[ActiveIssue]` gates introduced

## Reviewer notes

- This is the first of four sequenced PRs. PR2 will branch from this one and target `main`, so the PR2 diff will visibly carry these commits until PR1 merges.
- `aspire-install.json` is a NEW source-of-truth file — please pay attention to the schema and field semantics (the runtime reader will land in PR2).
- The dotnet-tool sidecar is intentionally absent from the pointer nupkg — only RID-specific packs carry it. PathResolver Mode B (binary-adjacent) is the discovery contract.

author: blamechris
body:
Closes #3349

## Summary

- **Idle-resume TTL** (`CHROXY_AGENT_RESUME_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 60 s): when a WS disconnects with an active session, a per-session timer is armed. If the client does not resume within the window, the child is killed (SIGTERM → SIGKILL after 5 s) and the session is evicted. Resume before TTL cancels the timer. `agent.close()` cancels all idle timers. A late `resume` for an evicted session receives `session_lost(unknown_session)` — same as any unknown session.

- **Hard session cap** (`CHROXY_AGENT_MAX_SESSIONS`, default 8): enforced on every `spawn`. When the cap is reached the oldest idle session (by `lastActiveAt`) is evicted first; falls back to the globally oldest session if all are active. Prevents linear accumulation of orphan sessions from a client that reconnects repeatedly without resuming.

- **`lastActiveAt` tracking**: refreshed in `_emitSessionFrame` and on `resume` to power oldest-first eviction. Initialised to `Date.now()` at spawn time.

- **Deterministic timer injection**: `setTimeoutFn`/`clearTimeoutFn` constructor opts. All new tests use a `makeFakeClock()` helper — no real-clock waits.

- **PROTOCOL.md**: documents the Idle Resume Window and Hard Session Cap contracts.

## Defaults

| Env var | Default | Description |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `CHROXY_AGENT_RESUME_TIMEOUT_MS` | `60000` (60 s) | Idle window before session eviction |
| `CHROXY_AGENT_MAX_SESSIONS` | `8` | Max concurrent sessions before LRU eviction |

## Test plan

- [x] `idle timer fires after TTL and kills the child + drops session`
- [x] `resume before TTL cancels the idle timer`
- [x] `agent.close() cancels idle timers and kills children`
- [x] `session_lost(unknown_session) is delivered to a late resume after TTL eviction`
- [x] `oldest idle session is evicted when cap is reached`
- [x] All 27 pre-existing sidecar tests still pass (34 total, 0 failures)
- [x] No regression in full server suite (74 pre-existing failures, unchanged)

body: Allow users to send messages while a session or thread is already running by queueing busy-thread sends and draining them after the active turn releases its sandbox hold. The orchestrator now bundles queued user messages, uses a drain-specific dedupe key so follow-up jobs are not collapsed by the running job, and clears thread pending counters after scheduling the drain. Terminal threads are rejected instead of accepting queued messages that cannot be processed, and the session composer no longer blocks on running state unless the session is pending, skipped, or destroyed. Validated with `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, and frontend `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`.

body:
## 🧢 Changes

- Splits assistant integration commands into clearer user-level and project-level flows:
  - `graphify skill <platform>` installs or refreshes the assistant skill.
  - `graphify setup <platform>` writes project-local assistant instructions and hooks.
- Keeps deprecated install aliases working for compatibility, including `graphify install --platform <platform>` and platform-first `graphify <platform> install` forms.
- Unifies platform skill configuration, source file resolution, install paths, remove behavior, and package-data coverage across supported assistants.
- Adds `.env` loading for CLI and direct LLM usage, including project/home `.env` discovery, WSL Windows-home fallback, and Windows user environment support for common graphify/API variables.
- Adds a Codex Kimi fast path: when `MOONSHOT_API_KEY` is set, semantic extraction can use `graphify.llm.extract_corpus_parallel(..., backend="kimi")` directly instead of dispatching Codex subagents.
- Moves temporary workflow state under `graphify-out/` so skill runs avoid root-level `.graphify_*` scratch files.
- Adds graph-first Claude setup with a `UserPromptSubmit` reminder and a `PreToolUse` guard that blocks raw search/read/list tools until the graph has been used in the session.
- Fixes extracted ID remapping so file-derived and entity-derived IDs are normalized consistently before cross-file call target resolution.
- Updates README command examples and platform tables to reflect the new `skill` and `setup` command model.

## ☕️ Reasoning

The previous install surface mixed two different responsibilities: installing reusable assistant skills and configuring the current project to use a graph. This PR separates those flows while preserving old commands as aliases, which makes onboarding clearer without breaking existing users.

It also makes the graphify assistant workflow more reliable for larger or repeated runs. Kimi can be used directly when a Moonshot key is available, temporary files stay inside `graphify-out/`, Claude is nudged or guarded toward graph-first exploration, and `.env` loading makes API-key configuration work more consistently across local, Windows, and WSL environments.

## 🧪 Testing

- Adds/updates tests for CLI command parsing, deprecated aliases, skill installation paths, setup/remove behavior, package-data coverage, and no-side-effect help commands.
- Adds tests for `.env` loading precedence, quoted/exported values, process-env protection, and WSL Windows-home discovery.
- Adds tests for Claude graph guard behavior before and after graph use, including Windows-style paths.
- Adds skill contract tests for the Codex/Kimi fast path and shared Claude/Codex output locations.
- Not run locally while updating this PR description.

author: ccantynz-alt
body:
## Summary

This PR introduces three major features to GateTest: a self-sufficient direct repair engine that clones, scans, patches, and pushes fixes without external APIs; a PR/branch pruner for cleaning up stale automation branches; and Phase 1.2b cross-scanner re-validation that detects regressions introduced by fixes.

## Key Changes

### Direct Repair Engine (`src/core/direct-repair.js`)
- New `DirectRepair` class that owns the complete repair lifecycle: clone → scan → patch → verify → commit → push
- Works with any git host (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted, SSH remotes)
- Pattern cache system that stores successful repairs to avoid redundant Claude calls for known bug classes
- Built-in patterns for common fixes (console.log removal, cookie security, TLS validation, async iteration)
- Unified diff application for applying patches to files
- Comprehensive test suite (`tests/direct-repair.test.js`)

### PR + Branch Pruner (`src/core/pr-pruner.js`)
- New `PrPruner` class that identifies and cleans up stale GateTest/Claude-generated branches
- Closes abandoned open PRs (configurable staleness threshold, default 7 days)
- Deletes merged/closed PR branches
- Dry-run mode for safe preview
- Comprehensive test suite (`tests/pr-pruner.test.js`)

### Phase 1.2b Cross-Scanner Re-Validation
- `ScanResult` interface now includes `findingsByModule` map for per-module findings baseline
- `/api/scan/run` returns `findingsByModule` so the fix API can detect regressions
- `/api/scan/fix` accepts `originalFindingsByModule` and runs cross-scanner validation gate
- Validates that fixes don't introduce new findings in other modules
- Prevents regressions from being shipped

### CLI Enhancements (`bin/gatetest.js`)
- `--repair <url>` flag for direct repair workflow
- `--repair-token <t>` for git credentials (PAT, deploy token, etc.)
- `--repair-dry-run` to preview fixes without writing
- `--repair-suite <s>` to select scan suite during repair
- `--prune-prs <owner/repo>` for branch/PR cleanup
- `--prune-pattern <prefix>` to customize branch matching
- `--prune-dry-run` for safe preview
- `--prune-stale-days <n>` to configure staleness threshold

### Scan Status UI Improvements (`website/app/scan/status/page.tsx`)
- New `ScanningState` component with modern dark theme UI
- Severity badge system (critical/high/medium/low) with color coding
- Module grid showing real-time scan progress with status indicators
- Improved progress bar with gradient and glow effects
- Cleaner module label abbreviations (e.g., "Syntax" instead of "Syntax validation")
- Extracted `severityOf()` helper for consistent severity classification
- Removed dependency on external component imports (FindingsPanel, LiveScanTerminal, etc.)
- Inline issue extraction logic for better control

### Infrastructure
- `docker-compose.yml` for local development (PostgreSQL + Next.js app)
- `Dockerfile` multi-stage build for production deployment
- `scripts/sandbox-worker.js` for self-hosted cron replacement (processes queued scans, watches, learning)

### Environment Variables Module Enhancement (`src/modules/env-vars.js`)
- New "missing-from-runtime" check for CI environments

author: kylejfitzsimmons
body:
## What
Migrate `@upway/ui` to the locked 2026-05-05 brand: **Ink / Bone / Volt**.
Replaces the sage/forest/sun/coral palette and the cyan/gold accent system.

## Why
Brand reset. Volt-on-Ink is the new primary expression — premium fintech
meets travel intelligence. Volt is reserved for money, CTAs, and value
moments. Bone is the marketing surface; Ink is the app shell.

## The new system (locked)

| Token | Hex | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Ink | `#0A0E14` | primary, app shell |
| Bone | `#F4F1EA` | secondary, marketing |
| **Volt** | `#C6FF3D` | **money / CTA / value ONLY — never decorative** |
| Slate-95 | `#13181F` | surface dark |
| Bone-94 | `#EEEAE0` | surface light |
| Hairline-dark | `#1E242D` | 1px borders on Ink |
| Hairline-light | `#D9D3C5` | 1px borders on Bone |
| Text-Hi | `#F4F1EA` | text on Ink |
| Text-Mid | `#8A94A4` | secondary text |
| Text-Lo | `#4A5260` | tertiary, disabled |

- **Display:** GT Maru
- **Body:** Satoshi
- **Mono:** Söhne Mono
- **Radius:** sm 4 / md 8 / lg 12 / pill 9999
- **Default ease:** `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)` (spring)

## Files changed
- `src/styles/tokens.css` — full rewrite. New `:root` (light/Bone) and
  `[data-theme="dark"]` (Ink) blocks. Backward-compat aliases kept for
  `--gold`, `--amber`, `--neon-purple`, `--ai-accent`, `--text2`, `--chip-bg`,
  `--premium`, etc. so existing components keep rendering — burn down later.
- `tailwind-preset.js` — exposes `colors.{ink,bone,volt,slate.95,hairline,text}`,
  new `borderRadius`, `transitionTimingFunction.spring`, retuned shadows.
  Removed `colors.brand.{sage,forest,sun,coral}`, `colors.gold.*`, and
  `fontFamily.serif`.
- `package.json` — 0.1.0 → 0.2.0 (breaking).
- `CHANGELOG.md` — new file documenting migration + consumer steps.

## Breaking change?
- [ ] No — additive
- [x] Yes — list every consumer that needs updating
  - app: Upway-Travel/app
  - landing: Upway-Travel/landing
  - blog: Upway-Travel/blog
  - pitch-deck: Upway-Travel/upway-pitch-deck

## Consumer migration checklist
1. Bump pinned `@upway/ui` SHA to this PR's merge commit.
2. `npm install`, rebuild Tailwind, re-run dev server.
3. Grep for hardcoded legacy hexes (`#8fbfa0`, `#1a4d32`, `#e8d44d`, `#e8735a`,
   `#0891b2`, `#06b6d4`, `#c4961a`) and replace with token references.
4. Visual-diff dark shell (Ink) and light marketing (Bone).
5. Audit Volt usage — must be money / CTA / value only. If it's decorative,
   it's wrong.

## How tested
- [x] Local build passes (token rewrite is CSS-only, no JS surface change)
- [ ] Visual-regression checked — **deferred to consumer dogfooding before merge**
- [x] Token / API surface change documented (CHANGELOG + this PR body)

## Risk
**High** — coordinated brand change. Consumers must opt in by bumping SHA;
nothing breaks until they do, but the visual diff will be substantial.

## Rollback
Revert this PR + consumers stay on prior pinned SHA.

## Do not merge
Hold for Kyle's visual review before propagation.

body:
Linear: [JES-86](https://linear.app/39-west-design/issue/JES-86/implement-production-alertdialog-primitive)
Decision contract: [`docs/alert-dialog-primitive-decision.md`](https://github.com/jnanthak83/lead-design-system/blob/main/docs/alert-dialog-primitive-decision.md) (JES-85, merged at `a2b1db96`)

Implements the production `<AlertDialog>` primitive per the four decisions taken in JES-85.

## Files changed

**Added (4):**
- `packages/lead-ui/src/components/AlertDialog/AlertDialog.tsx` (~210 lines, 11 exports)
- `packages/lead-ui/src/components/AlertDialog/AlertDialog.test.tsx` (12 tests)
- `packages/lead-ui/src/components/AlertDialog/AlertDialog.css` (placeholder; styling reused from Dialog.css by design)
- `apps/storybook/src/stories/AlertDialog.stories.tsx` (4 stories: destructive confirmation, save-or-discard, sm-stacked, with-item-preview)

**Modified (4):**
- `packages/lead-ui/package.json` + `package-lock.json` — adds `@radix-ui/react-alert-dialog: ^1.1.4`
- `packages/lead-ui/src/components/Dialog/Dialog.css` — adds the auto-stacked-footer rule at `[data-size="sm"]` (consistency fix per decision §2; applies to both `<DialogFooter>` and `<AlertDialogFooter>`)
- `packages/lead-ui/src/index.ts` — exports the AlertDialog component family + types

## Decision contract honored

| # | Decision | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Add `<AlertDialog>` with `role="alertdialog"` semantics | ✅ 11-component family wrapping `@radix-ui/react-alert-dialog`. Tests assert `role="alertdialog"` directly. |
| 2 | Footer auto-stacks at `size="sm"`, no new prop | ✅ Single CSS descendant selector in Dialog.css: `.lead-Dialog__content[data-size="sm"] .lead-DialogFooter { flex-direction: column; ... }`. Zero new React API. Applied to `<DialogFooter>` too for consistency. |
| 3 | No confirmation summary subcomponent — document the pattern | ✅ Storybook story `With item preview (composition pattern)` shows a styled `<div>` between header and footer. No `<AlertDialogSummary>` or similar component added. |
| 4 | Cancel first / primary action last across all breakpoints | ✅ All four Storybook stories use Cancel-first / primary-last order. Test `renders Cancel and Action buttons in caller-declared order` locks in the rendering convention. |

## Visual primitives reuse

`<AlertDialog>` reuses Dialog's CSS classes verbatim — `lead-Dialog__overlay`, `lead-Dialog__content`, `lead-DialogHeader`, `lead-DialogTitle`, `lead-DialogDescription`, `lead-DialogFooter`. Future Dialog visual updates apply automatically. The only AlertDialog-specific concern (auto-stacked footer at sm) lives in Dialog.css because it's a shared rule.

This means:
- Bundle CSS delta is tiny (just the stacked-footer rule).
- Visual consistency is automatic, not maintained manually.
- The decision doc's "match Dialog's styling primitives" requirement is satisfied structurally, not by copy-paste.

## Exported API surface

```ts
// Components
AlertDialog
AlertDialogTrigger
AlertDialogPortal
AlertDialogOverlay
AlertDialogContent       // size: "sm" | "md" | "lg" (matches Dialog), withOverlay
AlertDialogHeader
AlertDialogTitle
AlertDialogDescription
AlertDialogFooter        // align: "start" | "end" | "between" — overridden at size="sm"
AlertDialogAction        // the destructive/confirmatory action; closes dialog
AlertDialogCancel        // the safe option; closes dialog

// Types (all exported)
AlertDialogProps, AlertDialogTriggerProps, AlertDialogPortalProps,
AlertDialogOverlayProps, AlertDialogContentProps, AlertDialogHeaderProps,
AlertDialogTitleProps, AlertDialogDescriptionProps, AlertDialogFooterProps,
AlertDialogActionProps, AlertDialogCancelProps
```

## Tests added (12 cases, all passing)

- `does not render content when closed`
- `opens with role='alertdialog' when the trigger is clicked` (asserts `role="alertdialog"` directly)
- `wires title and description via aria-labelledby and aria-describedby`
- `renders Cancel and Action buttons in caller-declared order`
- `invokes the action's onClick when AlertDialogAction is clicked`
- `closes when AlertDialogAction is activated`
- `invokes the cancel's onClick when AlertDialogCancel is clicked`
- `closes when AlertDialogCancel is activated`
- `propagates size to data-size attribute on content (md default)`
- `propagates size='sm' to data-size attribute on content`
- `renders the AlertDialogFooter as a child of the content` (DOM precondition for the CSS auto-stacking rule)
- `supports controlled open state`

The auto-stacking layout itself is a CSS observation; jsdom doesn't compute layout, so the test asserts the DOM precondition (`data-size="sm"` on content + `<AlertDialogFooter>` as child) that drives the CSS rule. Visual verification happens in Storybook.

## Verification

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run lead:ui:typecheck` | ✅ clean |
| `npm run lead:ui:test` | ✅ **299/299** (was 287; +12 new) |
| `npm run lead:ui:build` | ✅ 236.03 kB JS / 34.04 kB CSS, **gzipped 58.70 kB JS / 4.60 kB CSS** |
| `npm run lead:storybook:build` | ✅ 15.99s |
| `npm test` (root) | ✅ tokens (82) + schemas + decisions + lead-ui (299) all green |
| `git diff --check` | ✅ clean |
| `git status -sb` | ✅ clean working tree on commit |

### Bundle delta

| Metric | Before | After | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| JS gzipped | 57.70 kB | **58.70 kB** | +1.00 kB |
| CSS gzipped | 4.57 kB | **4.60 kB** | +0.03 kB |

**Within budget.** Lead's API-CONSISTENCY budget: 60 kB warn / 75 kB hard / 90 kB ceiling. The +1.00 kB JS is `@radix-ui/react-alert-dialog`; the +0.03 kB CSS is the auto-stacked-footer rule.

## Confirmations — Code Connect / Figma state untouched

- ✅ `FIGMA_CODE_CONNECT_ENABLED=false` (verified pre- and post-implementation)
- ✅ No Code Connect mapping/workflow/secret/variable changes
- ✅ No `*.figma.tsx` files added or modified (a Code Connect mapping for AlertDialog can land in a future PR if/when desired)
- ✅ `figma-code-connect.yml`, `token-publishing.yml` workflows unchanged
- ✅ JES-80 / JES-81 (Lane 1/2 blockers) not affected by this PR

## Out of scope (per decision doc)

- **Figma `sm` breakpoint button-order fix** — separate design ticket. The Figma sm variant currently has Continue-first; Lead's React API renders Cancel-first per decision §4. Designers updating the Figma source resolve this asymmetry.
- **`<Card variant="muted">`** — the decision doc mentioned this as a possible reusable surface for the item-preview pattern. Not added; the Storybook story uses inline styles, demonstrating the pattern compositionally without a new variant. Can be added in a follow-up if reuse pressure warrants.
- **Code Connect mapping for AlertDialog** — Lane 1 is parked; mapping can be added when Lane 1 unblocks.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI: `Test / lead-tokens` (82), `Test / lead-ui` (299), `Test / storybook` build pass.
- [ ] Reviewer: open the deployed Storybook (after merge → Pages auto-redeploys), navigate to `Components / Alert Dialog`, click triggers in all four stories. Verify:
  - Destructive confirmation renders horizontal footer (Cancel + Delete)
  - Save-or-discard renders horizontal footer
  - sm story renders **stacked** footer (Cancel on top, primary below) with full-width buttons
  - With-item-preview shows the muted-background item panel between header and footer
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm the experimental `Experimental / Figma Export / Alert Dialog` (JES-83) and the new production `Components / Alert Dialog` (this PR) are both in the deployed Storybook side-by-side.

**Not auto-merging — awaiting your review.**

body:
## Summary

Phase 15 fixes and optimizations targeting the C-303 audit findings (I-1 through I-10). 9 files changed, 171 insertions, 48 deletions.

### Critical Fixes

- **Fix 1 — Bot deploy suppression** (`scripts/ignore-build.sh`): Added `bot@mobius.systems` and `bot@mobius.internal` to the email blocklist; added `[skip deploy]` message directive; added `chore(sweep):` commit prefix pattern. Resolves the cascade of 5 CANCELED builds since Phase 14 merge (I-1).

- **Fix 3 + Opt-8 — reattest-seals exponential backoff** (`app/api/cron/reattest-seals/route.ts`): Added `shouldSkipRetry()` and `recordReattestAttempt()` using KV. Backoff schedule: 5m → 10m → 20m → 40m, capped at 2h. Applies to both the missing-agents loop and the fully-attested-stuck loop. Stops the cron from hammering the Render ledger endpoint on repeated failures (I-3).

- **Fix 4 — ATLAS confidence floor** (`app/api/agents/status/route.ts`): `applyConfidenceFloor()` enforces a 0.65 minimum on read for ATLAS, ZEUS, EVE, JADE, AUREA. Guards against pre-Phase14 KV values that let ATLAS drift to 0.62 (I-4).

### Optimizations

- **Opt-3** (`lib/agents/micro/instrument-polls.ts`): ZEUS-µ2 returns nominal 0.7 fallback when both Semantic Scholar and CORE API return 0 — treats empty response as API quota/availability issue, not a true zero-signal (I-8).

- **Opt-4** (`app/api/cron/promote/route.ts`, `app/api/epicon/promotion-status/route.ts`): Cron writes `LAST_PROMOTION_RUN_AT` to KV after a successful promote response. Promotion-status reads the KV key as authoritative and surfaces `promotion_stale: true` in diagnostics when last run > 2h ago (I-9).

- **Opt-5** (`app/api/terminal/snapshot-lite/route.ts`): Cache upgraded from `s-maxage=15` to `s-maxage=30, stale-while-revalidate=60`. Reduces MISS frequency on the ~17s poll cycle.

- **Opt-7** (`lib/agents/micro/instrument-polls.ts`): EVE-µ2 (Agify demographic probe → Congress.gov active governance bills) and EVE-µ4 (Nationalize surname geography → GovTrack enacted laws). Both include a 0.7 nominal fallback when the API is unavailable.

- **Opt-9** (`app/api/cron/heartbeat/route.ts`): `appendGiTrend()` called on every heartbeat tick. Fire-and-forget; does not block the heartbeat response.

- **Opt-10** (`app/api/vault/status/route.ts`): Vault status exposes `quarantine_cycle_range` (e.g. `"C-288–C-298"`) and `quarantine_cycle_list` for operator visibility into which cycles have quarantined seals.

## Files Changed

|------|--------|
| `scripts/ignore-build.sh` | Fix 1: bot email + pattern expansion |
| `app/api/cron/reattest-seals/route.ts` | Fix 3 + Opt-8: exponential backoff |
| `app/api/agents/status/route.ts` | Fix 4: confidence floor on read |
| `lib/agents/micro/instrument-polls.ts` | Opt-3: ZEUS-µ2 fallback; Opt-7: EVE-µ2/µ4 governance APIs |
| `app/api/terminal/snapshot-lite/route.ts` | Opt-5: s-maxage=30 SWR=60 |
| `app/api/cron/heartbeat/route.ts` | Opt-9: GI_TREND on every tick |
| `app/api/vault/status/route.ts` | Opt-10: quarantine cycle range |
| `app/api/cron/promote/route.ts` | Opt-4: write LAST_PROMOTION_RUN_AT to KV |
| `app/api/epicon/promotion-status/route.ts` | Opt-4: stale detection from KV key |

author: ishaan-berri
body:
## Problem

`litellm_remaining_api_key_requests_for_model` and `litellm_remaining_api_key_tokens_for_model` report `sys.maxsize` (~9.22e18, displayed as `9e18` in DataDog) for every request when the **v3** parallel rate limiter is in use, even though the actual remaining values are available.

> I tried to use these two metrics, but DataDog was constantly displaying '9e18', which appears to be `sys.maxsize`, the value used when prometheus.py does not find the values in the kwargs. After a short investigation, I discovered that the values are available, but under the keys `x-ratelimit-model_per_key-remaining-{tokens/requests}` in `hidden_params.additional_headers`. But prometheus.py expects to find these gauges in the metadata, under the keys `litellm-key-remaining-{tokens/requests}-{model_group}`.

## Root cause

`PrometheusLogger._set_virtual_key_rate_limit_metrics` (`litellm/integrations/prometheus.py`) only reads from request **metadata**:

```python
remaining_requests_variable_name = f"litellm-key-remaining-requests-{model_group}"
remaining_tokens_variable_name   = f"litellm-key-remaining-tokens-{model_group}"
remaining_requests = metadata.get(remaining_requests_variable_name, sys.maxsize) or sys.maxsize
remaining_tokens   = metadata.get(remaining_tokens_variable_name,   sys.maxsize) or sys.maxsize
```

That's where the **v1** limiter (`litellm/proxy/hooks/parallel_request_limiter.py`) writes the values:

```python
data["metadata"].update({
    f"litellm-key-remaining-tokens-{_model}":   _remaining_tokens,
    f"litellm-key-remaining-requests-{_model}": _remaining_requests,
})
```

The **v3** limiter (`litellm/proxy/hooks/parallel_request_limiter_v3.py`) instead writes to `response._hidden_params["additional_headers"]` using a different key scheme:

```python
prefix = f"x-ratelimit-{status['descriptor_key']}"      # "x-ratelimit-model_per_key"
_additional_headers[f"{prefix}-remaining-{status['rate_limit_type']}"] = status["limit_remaining"]
```

These keys (`x-ratelimit-model_per_key-remaining-tokens` / `…-requests`) are preserved verbatim through `StandardLoggingPayloadSetup.get_additional_headers` and reach the standard logging payload, but `prometheus.py` never reads them, so the gauge falls through to `sys.maxsize`.

## Fix

Make `_set_virtual_key_rate_limit_metrics` fall back to `standard_logging_object.hidden_params.additional_headers` when the metadata keys are absent.

- **v1 limiter** path (metadata populated) — unchanged, still reports the metadata value.
- **v3 limiter** path (additional_headers populated) — now reports the real value instead of `sys.maxsize`.
- Neither populated — still falls through to `sys.maxsize` (preserves prior contract).

## Reproduction (before / after)

Driving `_set_virtual_key_rate_limit_metrics` with v3-style data:

```python
kwargs = {
    "litellm_params": {"metadata": {"model_group": "gpt-4o-mini"}},
    "standard_logging_object": {
        "hidden_params": {
            "additional_headers": {
                "x-ratelimit-model_per_key-remaining-tokens": 1234,
                "x-ratelimit-model_per_key-remaining-requests": 17,
            }
        }
    },
}
```

| Gauge | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `litellm_remaining_api_key_requests_for_model` | `9223372036854775808` (≈ 9.22e18) | `17` |
| `litellm_remaining_api_key_tokens_for_model`   | `9223372036854775808` (≈ 9.22e18) | `1234` |

## Tests

New file `tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_prometheus_remaining_key_model_v3.py` covers:

1. `test_v3_limiter_additional_headers_populates_remaining_gauges` — v3 path emits real values.
2. `test_v1_limiter_metadata_path_still_works` — v1 metadata path is unchanged (regression guard).
3. `test_no_data_falls_back_to_sys_maxsize` — empty case still falls through.

```
pytest tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_prometheus_remaining_key_model_v3.py -v
3 passed in 0.32s
```

The existing 21 prometheus tests in `test_prometheus_missing_metrics.py`, `test_prometheus_labels.py`, and `test_prometheus_metric_name_consistency.py` continue to pass.

## Files changed
- `litellm/integrations/prometheus.py` — fallback fix (~28 lines).
- `tests/test_litellm/integrations/test_prometheus_remaining_key_model_v3.py` — regression tests (new).

body: ## Purpose This PR addresses an issue where downloading and writing large files using the `file.write` function results in a `java.lang.OutOfMemoryError`, even when the `enableStreaming` parameter is explicitly set to `true`. ## Goals The goal of this fix is to prevent JVM heap exhaustion during large file transfers by allowing the raw network `InputStream` to be fully consumed, streamed directly to the file system, and immediately discarded when streaming is enabled. It also guarantees backward compatibility for integration flows that have `enableStreaming` flag set to `false` ## Approach Currently, in `WriteFile.java`, the `MessageFormatter.writeTo()` method is invoked with the `preserve` argument hardcoded to `true`: `messageFormatter.writeTo(axis2MessageContext, format, outputStream, true);` Because `preserve` is `true`, the `ExpandingMessageFormatter` skips marking the `StreamingOnRequestDataSource` for "last use". Consequently, to preserve the "read-once" network stream for subsequent mediators, `BinaryRelayBuilder.readAllFromInputSteam()` is triggered, aggressively caching the entire payload in a `ByteArrayOutputStream`. For massive files, this immediately triggers an OOM crash. **Implementation** This PR modifies mentioned line to infer the `preserve` flag logically based on the user's streaming configuration: * **`enableStreaming=true`:** The `preserve` flag evaluates to `false`. The payload is streamed natively to disk and discarded, maintaining a flat memory footprint. * **`enableStreaming=false`:** The `preserve` flag evaluates to `true`, maintaining the same behavior for smaller files. **Potential improvement** While this patch fixes the immediate OOM streaming issue, a future improvement could introduce an explicit `preservePayload` boolean parameter to the `write` function configuration. This would cleanly decouple the transfer mechanism (`enableStreaming`) from the payload lifecycle (`preservePayload`), giving integration developers explicit control over when the message body is kept alive in the integration flow. ## Evidence Demo project: [example-project.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27416559/example-project.zip) **Stacktrace:** ```text [2026-05-05 22:06:40,676] author: abhishek8108
body:
## What this PR does

Fixes #6209.

`_check_conflicting_feature_view_names` built its lookup map from all feature views in `cached_registry_proto` without filtering by project. In a shared file-based registry with multiple projects, this caused false `ConflictingFeatureViewNames` errors when two different projects defined feature views with the same name.

## Root cause

`_existing_feature_view_names_to_fvs` iterated over all three collections (feature views, stream feature views, on-demand feature views) in the entire `RegistryProto` without scoping to the current project. The dict is keyed by name only, so a `FeatureView` named `driver_stats` in `project_a` and a `FeatureView` also named `driver_stats` in `project_b` would collide, triggering a spurious error on the second `feast apply`.

## Fix

- Added a `project: str` parameter to both `_check_conflicting_feature_view_names` and `_existing_feature_view_names_to_fvs`
- Each collection is now filtered by `fv.spec.project == project` so only feature views belonging to the current project are included in the conflict map
- The call site in `apply_feature_view` passes the `project` argument that is already in scope

## Tests

- Added `test_cross_project_feature_view_names_do_not_conflict` in `tests/unit/local_feast_tests/test_local_feature_store.py`: two `FeatureStore` instances sharing a registry file but different projects both apply a `FeatureView` named `driver_stats` — asserts no `ConflictingFeatureViewNames` is raised
- Existing `test_apply_conflicting_feature_view_names` continues to pass — same-project type conflicts are still detected correctly

author: copilot
body:
Implements the full multi-track surface and clip-edit interactions for the Timeline Editor (PRD §5.3), backed by Zustand + zundo stores.

## Stores

- **`TimelinePlaybackStore`** — `currentTimeMs`, `isPlaying`, `rate`. Isolated from clip state so playhead position updates don't re-render the track tree.
- **`TimelineUIStore`** — selection set, `msPerPx` zoom, horizontal scroll, hover, fullscreen. Separate from document state to prevent selection changes from re-rendering all clips.
- **`TimelineStore`** — zundo temporal store holding the full sequence document (tracks + clips + markers). Exposes all mutations: `moveClip`, `trimClipStart/End`, `splitClipAtTime`, `splitSelectedAtPlayhead`, `duplicateSelected`, `deleteSelected`, `addTrack`, `removeTrack`, `reorderTracks`, `setTrackHeight`. Mirrors the NodeStore undo/redo wiring pattern.

## Components (`Tracks/`)

- **`TimeRuler`** — Canvas-rendered ruler with adaptive tick density (major/minor intervals computed from `msPerPx`). Click or pointer-drag scrubs `currentTimeMs`.
- **`Playhead`** — Single absolute-positioned vertical line subscribing only to `currentTimeMs` for frame-rate updates without full tree re-renders. Drag handle at top.
- **`TrackHeader`** — Track name (double-click inline edit), visibility/lock/mute/solo toggles, bottom-edge height-resize handle.
- **`TrackLane`** — Horizontal strip; clips are absolute-positioned children (`left = startMs / msPerPx`). Pointer-drag on empty space initiates rubber-band multi-selection.
- **`Clip`** — Generic clip chrome: selection ring (single/shift/ctrl-click), move-drag (multi-select aware, snaps via candidates passed to store), trim handles on both edges, `StatusIndicator` badge slot mapped from `ClipStatus`. Alt-key disables snapping.
- **`TracksRegion`** — Composes all the above; owns keyboard shortcuts (`Delete`, `Ctrl+D`, `Ctrl+Shift+D`, `Ctrl+S`, `Ctrl+Z/Y`) and scroll-wheel zoom.

## Snapping

Snap candidates passed per-drag: all clip start/end times on the track + playhead + 1-s tick boundaries. Threshold: 8 px. Hold `Alt` to disable.

## Infrastructure

- Adds `@nodetool-ai/timeline` to `web/package.json` and `jest.config.ts` moduleNameMapper.
- Replaces the `EmptyState` placeholder in `TimelineEditor` with the real `TracksRegion`.
- 26 Jest unit tests covering all `TimelineStore` reducer mutations and undo/redo via the zundo temporal API.

> 
> * Single absolute-positioned vertical line spanning all tracks. Drag handle at the top in the ruler.
> * Subscribes to `currentTimeMs` via a fine-grained selector to avoid re-rendering everything else on each frame.
> 
> ## TrackLane / TrackHeader
> 
> * Lane is a horizontal strip; clips are absolute-positioned children with `left = clip.startMs * msPerPx` and `width = clip.durationMs * msPerPx`.
> * Header shows name, visibility toggle, lock toggle, mute/solo (audio only), height handle (drag to resize).
> * Drag a clip onto another track changes its `trackId`.
> 
> ## Clip
> 
> * `Clip.tsx` is generic; the *body* is filled by [NOD-304](https://linear.app/nodetool/issue/NOD-304/support-imported-clip-creation-and-persistence) / [NOD-308](https://linear.app/nodetool/issue/NOD-308/build-generated-clip-inspector-node-stack) children. This issue only handles the chrome: selection ring, drag region, two trim handles (start/end), status badge slot.
> * Status badge uses `StatusIndicator` primitive; mapping table from PRD §5.5 — implemented in [NOD-311](https://linear.app/nodetool/issue/NOD-311/propagate-generation-status-results-and-errors-to-ui).
> * Resizable from either edge → calls `trimClip` from `@nodetool-ai/timeline`.
> * Multi-select: shift-click to extend; rubber-band selection within a track lane.
> 
> ## Snapping (uses `snap` from [NOD-297](https://linear.app/nodetool/issue/NOD-297/implement-dependency-hash-and-timeline-math-helpers))
> 
> * Candidates: clip start/end times on the same track, playhead, every 1 s tick.
> * Snap threshold: 8 px. Hold `Alt` to disable snapping.
> 
> ## Operations (TimelineStore actions)
> 
> ```
> selectClip(id) / addToSelection(id) / clearSelection()
> moveClip(clipId, deltaMs, toTrackId?)        // batched per drag, single zundo entry per drag
> trimClipStart(clipId, deltaMs) / trimClipEnd(clipId, deltaMs)
> splitSelectedAtPlayhead()
> duplicateSelected()                           // imports only at this point; generated in NOD-313
> deleteSelected()
> addTrack(type) / removeTrack(id) / reorderTracks(...) / setTrackHeight(id, px)
> setZoom(msPerPx)
> ```
> 
> ## Performance
> 
> * 100-clip target at 60 fps (PRD §9). Use `shallow` for store subscriptions; subscribe at the leaf component (Clip, TrackLane) with a selector returning only that clip's geometry; do not re-render all clips on a single move.
> * Memoize the visible-clip list by viewport range; skip rendering off-screen clips.
> 
> ## Acceptance
> 
> * Move, trim (both edges), split, duplicate, delete all work; undo/redo restores state.
> * Snap visibly engages near boundaries; `Alt` disables.
> * Multi-select drag moves all selected clips together.
> * `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run test` (web) clean.
> * Vitest unit tests for store reducers (mutations are pure given the store's input).
> * No raw MUI imports.
> Fixes https://linear.app/nodetool/issue/NOD-302/implement-tracks-ruler-playhead-and-clip-interactions
> Branch Name should include the identifier "NOD-302"
>

### 💡 What
Added a global `:focus-visible` fallback rule to `style.css` to restore explicit outlines on focused interactive elements.

### 🎯 Why
Many interactive elements in the application (like inputs and icon buttons) currently suppress default browser outlines via `outline: none`. This completely breaks keyboard accessibility, making it impossible for users navigating via the Tab key to see which element currently has focus.

### 📸 Before/After
**Before**: Tabbing through the interface provided no visual indication of the currently focused element.
**After**: A clear 2px solid blue outline (using the existing `--fitness-color` variable) appears around the focused element when navigating via keyboard.

### ♿ Accessibility
Significantly improves keyboard accessibility by restoring clear visual focus indicators, ensuring the application is usable by individuals relying on keyboard navigation.

Combined 2 fixes: sast.javascript.nosql_injection, sast.javascript.nosql_injection

Details:
- sast.javascript.nosql_injection: The vulnerability is a NoSQL injection caused by unsanitized user input (req.params.noteId) being directly used in MongoDB query filters, allowing attackers to inject malicious query operators or JavaScript code. This can lead to unauthorized data access or manipulation.
- sast.javascript.nosql_injection: The vulnerability is a NoSQL injection in the line where the user input from the JWT token payload (result.user) is directly used in a MongoDB query without sanitization, allowing an attacker to inject malicious query operators. This can lead to unauthorized data access or manipulation.

author: prashanthkrishnan91
body:
### Motivation

- Production cards were collapsing to a global HOLD because `insufficient_data` was used as a binary gate that overrode the count of trusted signals and action posture.
- The intent is to allow missing axes to be caveats only when there is at least one trusted signal, and to reserve the global wait/HOLD language for zero trusted signals.

### Description

- Updated `v2/backend/app/services/intelligence/reasoning_v2_plain_english.py` to compute `n_trusted` from `trusted_signals` and to treat `insufficient` as a blocker only when `n_trusted == 0`, and to pass `trusted_signals` and `incomplete_signals` into `_build_caveat` and `build_intel_read`.
- Reworked `_build_caveat` to be action-consistent: produce measured-buy language for `ACCUMULATE` with trusted signals, partial-evidence wording for `HOLD` with trusted signals, and risk-aware wording for `TRIM`/`AVOID`; preserve conservative wait copy only when `n_trusted == 0`.
- Adjusted summary/caveat generation call sites in `build_intel_read` to deduplicate `incomplete_signals` and return `insufficient_data` as a backend hint without forcing global HOLD when trusted signals exist.
- Updated docs `docs/ai/HANDOFF.md` and `v2/progress_log.md` to record the fix and validation checklist.
- Extended and updated `v2/backend/tests/test_reasoning_v2_plain_english.py` to change existing assertions and add tests that verify: buys with trusted signals avoid global wait language, 1–2 trusted signals remain action-consistent, hold with zero trusted signals keeps wait copy, hold with trusted signals does not imply zero evidence, and TRIM/SELL family wording remains risk-aware.

### Testing

- Ran the module unit tests in `v2/backend/tests/test_reasoning_v2_plain_english.py` with `pytest` and the updated test cases passed.
- New tests exercise buy/hold/trim caveat permutations under `insufficient_data` and validated that the global HOLD collapse no longer occurs.

## Summary

Cssom-canary curated manifest cutover (Codex iter-3 PR-5 close-out recommendation, sequencing dictated after PR-8 reached 5+ tests).

The canary suite previously contained 3 entries (sentinel + ThemeProvider + Button). PR-8 added Input/Checkbox/Switch tests via `cssom-full-advisory` — they passed at +0% flake. PR-9 promotes them into the **required** `cssom-canary-required` gate so a regression breaks the merge instead of producing an advisory failure.

## Why curated manifest over glob

The existing canary uses an explicit list in `package.json` `test:cssom:canary`:
```
vitest run --config <browser-config> <file1> <file2> <file3> ...
```

vs `cssom-full-advisory` which uses `**/*.cssom.test.{ts,tsx}`. Each curated entry is a deliberate gate-promotion decision:
- New cssom tests live in `cssom-full-advisory` (glob) until proven stable
- Promotion to canary happens in a small explicit PR like this one
- Canary runtime stays bounded (currently 6 files, 21 tests, ~1m20s on CI)

## Changes

- `package.json` — added 3 file paths to `test:cssom:canary` script
- ADR §L5 — canary description now lists the 4 primitives explicitly + notes manifest pattern + future-additions process
- Cheat-sheet — same job-table line updated with explicit manifest contents

## Verification

```
$ npm run test:cssom:canary
 Test Files  6 passed (6)
      Tests  21 passed (21)
   Duration  3.03s
```

(Note: local Duration is 3s; CI typically runs ~1m20s due to install/checkout overhead, still well under the 20-minute timeout.)

## Test plan

- [x] All 6 manifest tests pass locally
- [ ] CI green:
  - `cssom-canary-required` — runs the new manifest (was 3 files, now 6)
  - `cssom-full-advisory` — unchanged, picks up the same files via glob (signal redundant but no harm)
- [ ] Codex peer review (cross-AI HARD RULE)

## Why this is small

Pure CI manifest update. No production code, no test logic changes. The 3 promoted tests already passed under the advisory job in PR-8 — promotion is just moving them from "informational" to "blocking" in the cssom test environment strategy.

## Future expansion

When new primitive cssom tests are added (Card, Dialog, Drawer, Tooltip, etc.), follow the same 2-PR pattern:
1. Add the cssom test (runs via `cssom-full-advisory`)
2. After it stabilizes, promote to canary via a small manifest-update PR

1. **Discover with Glob/Grep/Read, not shell.** Never use `ls`, `find`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, shell `grep`, `sed`, or `node -e` for discovery or for editing files in bulk — these are slower per call and violate caching. Substitute bash commands for the specific tool names listed below, or available tools with the closest semantics:
- List a directory → `Glob('src/components/*')` (alt names: `search_files`, `file_search`), not `ls src/components`.
- Search a string → `Grep('pattern', { path: 'src' })` (alt names: `grep_search`, `search_files`), not `grep -rn ...` or `find ... | xargs grep`.
- Read a file → `Read('path/to/file')` (alt names: `read_file`), not `cat`/`head`/`tail`.
- Bulk-edit many files → multiple `Edit` calls (alt names: `apply_patch`, `replace_in_file`, `replace`), or one `Edit` with `replace_all` (alt names: `replace` with `allow_multiple`), not `sed -i`.
2. **Never read or grep inside `node_modules`.** The imports shown in this prompt are correct — don't verify them by introspecting installed packages. If something seems off, re-read this prompt, not `node_modules`.
3. **Read budget: ~40 files for discovery.** Before writing any code you may Read at most ~40 files: `index.html`, entry, App, providers, routing, root CSS, 1–2 hooks, 1 test, and spend the rest on components. You may read direct component dependencies essential to their understanding only after having read 20 components (or all components if fewer in the codebase).
4. **Edit > Write.** For any file you've Read, use `Edit`. Use `Write` only for new files. The project already has a `.storybook/preview.tsx` from `storybook init` — **Edit** it, do not overwrite.
5. **Batch the test loop.** Write **all** stories first, then run vitest **once** across everything. No per-file vitest runs until after that first batch run reveals failures.
6. **Use `Bun` for every install** (detected from this project's lockfile).
7. **Prefer fixing the shared `.storybook/preview.tsx`** over story-local workarounds when multiple stories fail the same way.
8. **Stop when the success criteria are met** — don't keep polishing.

## Plan (do not skip steps, but keep each step lean)

### Step 1 — Discover the runtime (≤40 reads)

  Identify, in this order, using Glob/Grep first then targeted Reads:

- `index.html` — `<link rel="stylesheet">` tags, inline `<style>` blocks, fonts, and any `<div id="...">` mount or portal roots that aren't created by JS
- entry file (`main.tsx` / `index.tsx`) — providers wrapping `<App />`, root CSS imports
- `App.tsx` — top-level layout, router usage, providers it consumes
- providers / context files — what they expose
- root CSS — global styles, CSS variables, theme tokens (both JS-imported CSS **and** anything linked from `index.html`)
- data hooks — `fetch(...)`, `useQuery`, `axios`, etc. (capture base URL + endpoints actually called during render)
- browser state actually read at render — `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`/cookie keys
- portal targets — `createPortal(...)` and the DOM ids it mounts to (e.g. `#modal-root`)
- 1–20 real page or feature components (your story source-of-truth for JSX patterns)

Stop reading once you can answer: *"What providers, CSS, browser state, and network calls must the preview supply for a typical page to render? What surrounding context do components need to render?"*

### Step 2 — Monorepo preparation

Build any local monorepo dependencies identified during discovery, and keep track of existing errors in the codebase unrelated to the package changes you'll make.

### Step 3 — Build the shared preview

    Set up Storybook **once** so most stories work without per-story setup. **Edit the existing `.storybook/preview.tsx`** (created by `storybook init`) — add to its existing config object, don't replace it.

The complete shape should look like this (merge the new pieces into what's already there):

```tsx
// .storybook/preview.tsx
import type { Preview } from '@storybook/react-vite';
import '../src/index.css';
import MockDate from 'mockdate';
import { initialize, mswLoader } from 'msw-storybook-addon';
import { SessionProvider } from '../src/contexts/SessionContext';
import { mswHandlers } from './msw-handlers';

initialize({ onUnhandledRequest: 'bypass' });

const preview: Preview = {
  decorators: [
    (Story) => (
      <SessionProvider>
        <Story />
      </SessionProvider>
    ),
  ],
  loaders: [mswLoader],
  parameters: { msw: { handlers: mswHandlers } },
  async beforeEach() {
    localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark');
    MockDate.set('2024-04-01T12:00:00Z');
  },
};

export default preview;
```

Rules for the preview:

- Use the **real** provider tree and the **real** root CSS import. Don't invent providers.
- If the app's CSS is loaded via `<link>` in `index.html` (rather than imported in JS), import the same file from preview so stories render with the same styles.
- Seed only the specific browser-state keys the app actually reads. Do **not** clear all of `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`/cookies, and do not reset Storybook's own state.
- Use `mockdate` only when render output depends on the date.
- Do not mock `window`, `document`, `navigator`, observers, or `fetch` directly.

### Step 4 — Portals (in a decorator, not `preview-body.html`)

If you found `createPortal(..., document.getElementById('foo'))` in discovery, **add a decorator in `.storybook/preview.tsx` that creates the portal root** before the story renders. Do not use `preview-body.html`.

```tsx
// Add this entry to the `decorators` array of your preview config:
(Story) => {
  for (const id of ['modal-root', 'drawer-root', 'toast-root']) {
    if (!document.getElementById(id)) {
      const el = document.createElement('div');
      el.id = id;
      document.body.appendChild(el);
    }
  }
  return <Story />;
}
```

Add this decorator to the `decorators` array of your preview config. Skip this step entirely if portals only target `document.body`.

### Step 5 — MSW handlers (only what stories will hit)

Use `msw-storybook-addon`. Install with:

    ```bash
    bun add -D msw msw-storybook-addon mockdate
    npx msw init ./public --save
    ```

    Make sure `.storybook/main.ts` serves `./public`:

    ```ts
// .storybook/main.ts
import type { StorybookConfig } from '@storybook/react-vite';

const config: StorybookConfig = { staticDirs: ['../public'] };
export default config;
