author: vgao1996
body:
## Summary

Addresses a class of failures where worker pods sat Pending waiting for their PVC to bind, burning the per-pod retry budget on storage delays unrelated to replay correctness. Restructures how PVCs are managed and tightens the per-pod / per-PVC limits to match GCE's actual constraints.

This addresses the root cause that resulted in our scheduled runs to constantly timeout since the beginning of the year.

## Architecture

- **PVC creation is now a non-blocking pipeline** that runs concurrently with the worker scheduler. `start_pvc_creation_pipeline()` requests only the source PVC and returns immediately; clones spawn progressively from `_maintain_pvc_pipeline()` each scheduler iteration. No more 15+ minute idle gap at startup before any worker can run.
- **Workers can dispatch to any PVC the moment it becomes Bound**, including the source. Workers start running on the source ~3–5 minutes before any clone has bound, instead of the old "wait for source → wait for clones → start workers" sequence.
- **Slot-to-PVC mapping is dynamic.** `_pick_pvc_for_dispatch` picks the least-loaded bound PVC under the per-PVC cap. Slots stay empty when no bound PVC has capacity, so they don't burn retry budget on storage that isn't ready.
- **`MAX_CONCURRENT_PVC_CREATIONS = 5`** in-flight PVC creations at a time. Empirically matches GCE's per-source clone-concurrency limit observed on both mainnet and testnet runs (the "first 5 clones bind in 30s, 6th waits 5 min" cliff).

## Per-pod timeouts (split by phase)

- **`PENDING_TIMEOUT = 10m`** for any pod that hasn't reached Running. With the architectural fix, Pending now only covers image pull + volume attach + container start, so a long Pending reliably indicates a stuck pod — kill fast and retry rather than waste a Running-budget retry slot.
- **`running_timeout`** per-network: 30m mainnet, 40m testnet. Testnet needs the extra 10m for the 6.7B–6.8B heavy zone, where 1M chunks empirically take ~33m. Measured from the moment the pod first transitioned to Running (not pod creation), so a slow Pending doesn't eat the binary's budget.
- **`binary_timeout = running_timeout + 10m`**, **`pod_ttl = binary_timeout + 10m`**. Each layer a backstop for the previous, all per-network.

## Worker concurrency

- **`MAX_WORKERS_PER_PVC = 10`** hard ceiling, with assertion in `ReplayConfig`. GCE PD allows roughly 10 concurrent active readers per disk; going higher just queues or starves at the CSI/IO layer. Earlier testnet tuning at 20 workers/PVC nearly doubled p99 task duration vs. 15 (979s → 1177s p90, 1192s → 2351s p99) without any aggregate throughput gain.
- Testnet config: **10 PVCs × 10 workers/PVC = 100 workers** (was 35×10=350). Mainnet unchanged at 10×10.

## Logging

- Periodic status dump renamed **"Scheduler status"** and now includes a PVCs section (counts plus per-PVC detail with bind durations and current worker load) followed by a Workers section with phase breakdown.
- Header reports **"completed N/M"** (terminal-state count) instead of "dispatched N/M" (which included in-flight tasks).
- Phase-aware timeout error messages distinguish **`pending-timeout`** from **`running-timeout`** and report the threshold inline.
- **End-of-run aggregate statistics**: total/succeeded/failed counts, retry distribution, and duration percentiles (min/p50/p90/p99/max/mean) for succeeded and failed tasks separately. Failed durations cluster at the timeout ceiling, so reporting them combined would distort percentiles.
- `Started creating clone PVC X (requested K/N, in-flight M/5)` and `PVC X is now bound after Ts (source/clone)` log lines surface pipeline progress.

## Naming

Source and clone PVCs now share a single name format: `{snapshot}-{run_id}-{idx}`. Source is index 0, clones are 1..N. No more `-clone-` infix.

## Bug fixes

- **`set_end_time` was missing** in the timeout-driven max-retry path, making those failures invisible in aggregate stats and the completion header (counts wouldn't add up). Now consistent with `process_completed_pod`'s permanent-fail path.
- **`ReplayScheduler.__str__`** was referencing `worker_cnt` and `image` as bare names, relying on script-as-`__main__` globals. Fixed to use `self` attributes.

## Test plan

- [ ] Trigger `replay-verify-on-archive` on testnet with this branch
- [ ] Confirm source PVC binds, then clones spawn in waves of ≤5 with progressive logging
- [ ] Verify workers start dispatching to source the moment it binds (not waiting for all clones)
- [ ] Verify status dump shows the new PVC + Workers sections clearly
- [ ] Verify no `phase=Pending, container=no-container-status` worker timeouts (the original failure mode)
- [ ] Verify end-of-run aggregate stats appear and percentile counts add up to total
- [ ] Run mainnet to confirm 10×10 + 30m running_timeout still passes cleanly

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Moderate risk because it refactors core replay-verify scheduling/PVC provisioning logic and timeout handling, which could change throughput or failure behavior under real cluster/storage conditions.
> 
> **Overview**
> Replay-verify now provisions storage via a **non-blocking PVC pipeline**: it creates a single source PVC from the snapshot, then progressively spawns clone PVCs (capped by `MAX_CONCURRENT_PVC_CREATIONS`) while the scheduler runs, and dispatches workers to any *bound* PVC based on per-PVC load.
> 
> Worker scheduling is updated to enforce a **per-PVC worker cap** (`workers_per_pvc`, asserted against `MAX_WORKERS_PER_PVC`) and to apply **phase-aware timeouts** (separate `PENDING_TIMEOUT` vs per-network `running_timeout`, measured from first observed Running) with derived `binary_timeout`/`pod_ttl`.
> 
> Logging/stats are expanded with PVC bind progress, per-PVC load, a corrected “completed” counter, end-of-run aggregate duration percentiles, and a bug fix to mark timeout-exhausted tasks terminal; `ReplayScheduler.__str__` also stops relying on globals.

## Summary

- Add `--oauth` flag to `docutray login` so AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) and CI can drive the full OAuth flow from a non-TTY shell. The CLI prints `Open this URL to authorize: <url>` to stderr (agent-detectable prefix), opens the browser, waits for the callback, and persists the API key — without ever showing the secret to the agent.
- Add companion flags `--no-browser` (skip auto-open, just print URL) and `--timeout <seconds>` (default 180s).
- Validate API keys received via positional arg, `--api-key` flag, and stdin against the real DocuTray key format (`/^dt[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}$/`). Fixes the v0.2.1 bug where `echo "2" | docutray login` silently wrote `{"apiKey":"2"}` to `~/.config/docutray/config.json`.

## What changed

- `src/commands/login.ts`: new flags + dispatch order (direct key → `--oauth` → TTY menu → non-interactive error). Updated non-interactive error message mentions `--oauth` as a third option. `loginWithOAuth` parameterized with `{openBrowser, timeoutMs}`; SIGINT/SIGTERM handler closes the listener cleanly.
- `src/oauth.ts`: `startCallbackServer({preferredPort, host, retries})`. Defaults preserve `http://localhost:9876/callback` (matches the dashboard's current OAuth allowlist for `client_id=docutray-cli`). `EADDRINUSE` retry path remains for explicit ports.
- `src/validators.ts`: `validateApiKey()` + `DOCUTRAY_API_KEY_PATTERN`. Pattern verified against the real key format the dashboard emits (`dt` + 64 chars URL-safe base64; tightened from the proposal's initial `dt_(live\|test)_…` guess).
- README "Authentication" gains an "AI coding agents" section with the recommended `docutray login --oauth` snippet.
- `docs/commands/login.md` regenerated.
- Spec under `openspec/changes/add-agent-oauth-login/` (proposal, design, specs, tasks).

## Test plan

Automated (`npm run test`): **151/151 passing.** New cases cover happy path, timeout, callback error, `--no-browser`, `--oauth + --api-key` conflict, key validation accept/reject, updated non-interactive message, port-bind retry, help-text metadata.

Manual verification against `https://app.docutray.com` on a Mac:

- [x] `docutray login --oauth` (non-TTY, piped through `tee`) → browser opens, authorize, stdout is one JSON object, `~/.config/docutray/config.json` updated.
- [x] `docutray status` immediately after returns `authenticated: true, source: config`.
- [x] `docutray login 2` and `docutray login --api-key sk_live_…` → exit 1, JSON error on stderr, config NOT modified.
- [x] `echo "garbage" | docutray login` → exit 1, error mentions `Invalid API key format`, config NOT modified (v0.2.1 regression confirmed fixed).
- [x] `printf "" | docutray login` → exit 1, error mentions `--api-key`, an api-key argument, AND `--oauth`.
- [x] `docutray login --oauth --no-browser --timeout 2` → URL on stderr, browser NOT opened, exits 1 in ~2s with `Authentication timed out after 2s`.
- [x] SIGINT mid-flow → listener closes; immediate `docutray login --oauth` reuses port 9876 without `EADDRINUSE`.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

- **Dashboard side:** expand the OAuth allowlist for `client_id=docutray-cli` to also accept `http://127.0.0.1:*/callback` and `http://localhost:*/callback` (RFC 8252 §7.3 loopback pattern). Once that lands, switch the CLI to ephemeral ports so port 9876 collisions are no longer possible.
- Update `docutray/docutray-skills` to recommend `docutray login --oauth` as the canonical agent auth path.
- After merge: bump to `0.3.0` and `gh release create v0.3.0`.

## Summary

- Add `pull_policy: never` to all 11 custom service definitions in `compose/dev.yml` (10 GHCR services + `rustbrain/frontend:dev`). Docker Compose no longer attempts a registry pull for these images; they must exist locally (built from source).
- Update `docs/dev-stack-auto-rebuild.md` with an **Image strategy on mars** section and a first-time **Step 3: Build all custom images** (`docker compose build`) before the first `docker compose up`.

**Root cause**: `compose/dev.yml` sets `image: ghcr.io/jarnura/rustacean/*:dev` without `pull_policy`, so `docker compose up` attempts a GHCR pull on mars — which fails with "denied" since mars has no GHCR credentials. The `dev-stack-auto-rebuild.sh` script only auto-rebuilds `control-api` and `frontend`, so the other 8 services had no locally-built image and triggered a pull every time.

## GitHub Issue
Closes #251

## Checklist
- [x] `pull_policy: never` added to all 11 custom service definitions
- [x] Documentation updated with image strategy and first-time build step
- [x] Only compose/dev.yml and docs changed — no logic or schema changes

body:
## What

Adds the missing Next.js Pages Router handler at `apps/web/pages/api/trpc/apiKeys/[trpc].ts` so the `apiKeys` tRPC router (already defined in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/apiKeys/_router.tsx` and registered in `viewerRouter`) is actually reachable over HTTP.

## Why

Cal.com exposes each top-level tRPC sub-router via a per-namespace handler in `apps/web/pages/api/trpc/<name>/[trpc].ts`. The `apiKeys` namespace had its router and handler-folder structure but the `[trpc].ts` file itself was missing.

Reproduce:

1. Self-host current `main`
2. Sign up, log in
3. Navigate to Settings → Developer → API Keys
4. Click "Create"
5. Frontend calls `POST /api/trpc/apiKeys/create?batch=1` → **404 Not Found**
6. `viewer.apiKeys.create` mutation in `ApiKeyDialogForm.tsx` fails

## Fix

3-line handler matching the existing pattern (e.g. `apps/web/pages/api/trpc/webhook/[trpc].ts`):

```ts
import { createNextApiHandler } from "@calcom/trpc/server/createNextApiHandler";
import { apiKeysRouter } from "@calcom/trpc/server/routers/viewer/apiKeys/_router";

export default createNextApiHandler(apiKeysRouter);
```

## Test

After deploy, `POST /api/trpc/apiKeys/create` returns 200 and creates the API key. No other paths affected.

## Audit

Cross-checked all 28 routers registered in `viewerRouter` against handler folders in `apps/web/pages/api/trpc/`. `apiKeys` was the only mismatch. All other handler imports resolve to valid router paths.

author: rvailleux
body:
## Pattern candidature: Ambient Execution (Background Work)

### Category
AI — Context & Memory

### What problem does it solve?
A persistent run model for async AI agents that stays visible across surfaces and attention states - not just a chat transcript.

Users don't want to passively wait for AI to finish. This pattern enables parallel work while maintaining awareness of agent state, building trust through constant perceptibility.

### First seen on
- **Product:** Devin
- **URL:** https://devin.ai
- **First observed (approx. date):** 2024

### Other examples in the wild
1. **Cursor** — Background task indicators in the status bar with expandable details
2. **Paperclip AI** — Persistent ambient badge showing agent execution status even when app is backgrounded

### Why it belongs in this library
This pattern addresses a critical gap in AI UX: the transition from synchronous chat-based interactions to asynchronous agent workflows. As AI systems become more capable of long-running tasks, users need ways to maintain awareness without being blocked. The four-tier escalation model (Ambient → Progress → Attention → Summary) provides a repeatable framework applicable across SaaS products.

### What makes a good implementation
- Start with subtle indicators that don't demand attention
- Escalate gracefully only when user input is truly required
- Persist state across navigation contexts (tabs, pages)
- Allow users to drill down for details or cancel operations
- Provide clear completion summaries for transparency

### Known pitfalls
- Full-screen blocking loaders that prevent parallel work
- Losing agent state when users navigate away
- Over-eager notifications for normal operations
- Missing progress indicators leading to abandonment

---

- [x] `src/_data/demos/ambient-execution.json`

author: gurdasnijor
body:
## Summary

Removes client per-call layer construction and pulls nondeterministic platform globals out of portable kernel paths. Identity generation moves to a kernel `IdGen` service (`globalThis.crypto.randomUUID` — Node + browsers); env reads move from `process.env` to Effect `Config` at the binary edge.

- New `@firegrid/substrate/id-gen` subpath exporting `IdGen` Context.Tag and `IdGenLive`. Browser-safe; portable across Node 19+ and modern browsers.
- `SubstrateProducerLive`, `DurableWaitsLive`, `WorkClaimLive`, `EventStreamClientLive`, and `attemptClaim` now resolve identity through `IdGen` and bake `IdGenLive` into their layer/effect, so callers compose at zero remaining requirements while tests can still inject a custom `IdGen` via the kernel subpath.
- `runtime/boot/identity.generateProcessId` becomes an `Effect<string>` that self-provides `IdGenLive`; `node:crypto` removed from `producer.ts`, `internal-claim.ts`, `waits.ts`, and `runtime/boot/identity.ts`.
- `FiregridClientLive` composes `SubstrateClientLive` once at the client root via `Layer.effect` + `Layer.provide`: `send`/`result`/`call`/`observe` reuse one StreamDB for the lifetime of the `FiregridClient` layer instead of acquiring/releasing per call. `EventStream`-side identity flows through the same `IdGen` instance via `buildEventStreamService(cfg, idGen)`.
- `bin/firegrid.ts` replaces `process.env[\"DURABLE_STREAMS_URL\"]` with `Config.option(Config.string(\"DURABLE_STREAMS_URL\"))`. Empty string is treated as unset to preserve attached/embedded boot semantics; the boot-mode discriminator is now drivable through `ConfigProvider.fromMap` for tests.

## ACIDs satisfied

- **firegrid-remediation-hardening.EFFECT_CONSISTENCY.1** — Each package keeps one primary Effect service construction convention. Substrate, client, and runtime continue to publish `Context.Tag` + `*Live(config)` factories; producer/work/waits live constructors switched to `Layer.effect` only where they capture the `IdGen` service.
- **firegrid-remediation-hardening.EFFECT_CONSISTENCY.5** — Kernel ID generation is Effect-service-backed via `IdGen`; portable paths (substrate `producer.ts`, `internal-claim.ts`, `waits.ts`, runtime `boot/identity.ts`) no longer import `node:crypto`. `IdGenLive` uses `globalThis.crypto.randomUUID`.
- **launchable-substrate-host.HOST_CONFIGURATION.4** — Host boot plans are decoded from Effect Config: `bin/firegrid.ts` reads `DURABLE_STREAMS_URL` through `Config.option(Config.string(...))`.
- **launchable-substrate-host.HOST_CONFIGURATION.6** — Configured stream URL selects attached mode and does not start or own a remote Durable Streams process. The bin's `Option.match` selects `FiregridRuntimeBoot.attached` when present and falls back to `embeddedDev` otherwise; nothing in the bin owns a remote DSS lifecycle.
- **launchable-substrate-host.HOST_CONFIGURATION.7** — Process identity is generated by default; explicit `processId` remains advanced/test usage. `generateProcessId` is the default Effect; `runtime/layer.ts` only reaches for it when `opts.processId` is undefined.
- **firegrid-runtime-process.CONFIG_SURFACE.1** — Runtime process configuration is handled at the binary process edge. The single `Config.*` reader lives in `bin/firegrid.ts`; substrate and runtime layer factories continue to take plain values.
- **firegrid-runtime-process.CONFIG_SURFACE.2** — The runtime package does not expose `bootPlanFromConfig` or `attachedFromConfig` as public Firegrid APIs (no such symbols are added; `FiregridRuntimeBoot.attached`/`embeddedDev` remain the explicit-options factories).
- **firegrid-runtime-process.CONFIG_SURFACE.4** — Runtime process identity is generated by default and is not normal user-facing environment config; the bin reads no `FIREGRID_PROCESS_ID` env var, and `generateProcessId` continues to be an Effect-side concern.

## Coordination notes

- Per the scope-collision watch, this PR owns client layer hoisting, injectable ID generation, and the config/env boundary cleanup.

## Summary

The runtime-mcp tools table lists \`delegate_task_async\` and \`check_task_status\` as one-liners but the user-visible behavior they wrap is much more — a multi-state ledger with deadlines, idempotency, and one sharp argument-name gotcha.

Adds an "Async delegation lifecycle" section between Tools and Inbound delivery covering:

- When to use sync vs async delegation
- Six-state lifecycle with the "stuck" rule (no heartbeat for >10 min while in_progress)
- Forward-only terminal states (restart-safe polling)
- 6h default deadline + automatic SHA-256 idempotency
- The `check_task_status(workspace_id=...)` arg-is-ignored gotcha — it queries the *source*'s log, not the peer's

## Verification

Every behavioral claim was cross-checked against code before commit:
- Stuck threshold + 6h deadline → \`workspace-server/internal/handlers/delegation_ledger.go\`

- check_task_status arg semantics → \`workspace/a2a_tools_delegation.py:337\` (\`Ignored (kept for backward compat). Checks source_workspace_id's delegations\`)

### Motivation
- Provide a lightweight editable impression label for the app and persist it across sessions. 
- Improve theming by introducing blended mid-stop colors and a set of ready-made presets for easier customization. 
- Harden import/export and history handling by validating/sanitizing incoming data and clamping numeric values.

author: copilot
body:
`rawBody` was declared twice in the same `serve` handler scope — once as the raw request `ArrayBuffer` (used for HMAC verification and JSON parsing), and again via destructuring of the `smsResult` error object (a `string`). The inner binding silently shadowed the outer one, creating a latent type confusion hazard.

## Change
- **`supabase/functions/send-sms-twilio/index.ts`** — rename the destructured error binding at the SMS error handling site:

```diff
- const { status: smsStatus, twilioCode, rawBody } = smsResult;
+ const { status: smsStatus, twilioCode, rawBody: smsErrorBody } = smsResult;
```

author: rhysparry
body:
## Summary

Fixes a flaky test failure in `ObserveUnauthorizedPollingConnections` (Polling, InMemory queue) observed in CI build `8.1.4994-pull-712` on Windows Server 2012 R2 / net48.

## Root cause

The test was calling `clientAndBuilder.Client.TrustOnly(new List<string>())` **after** `Build()` returned, relying on that call to prevent any authorized connections from being observed. However, `Build()` starts the polling service immediately, and the service begins connecting to the client's TCP listener within milliseconds — creating a race window where the first polling connection could be fully authorized before `TrustOnly` was called.

When that happened, the sequence in `SecureListener` was:

1. Polling service connects and TLS handshake completes
2. `Authorize()` calls `verifyClientThumbprint` — cert **still trusted** at this point → returns `true`
3. `connectionAuthorizedAndObserved = true`; `ConnectionAccepted(true)` fires
4. `ExchangeMessages` begins
5. **`TrustOnly(new List<string>())` runs** — but too late for this connection
6. Connection eventually closes → `ConnectionClosed(connectionAuthorizedAndObserved)` fires as `true`
7. Assertion `ConnectionClosedAuthorized.AllSatisfy(a => a.BeFalse())` fails

The race was intermittent because the window is only a few milliseconds wide. It was more likely to trigger under load (e.g. when multiple `ConnectionObserverFixture` tests ran concurrently), as seen in the CI log where `ObserveAuthorizedConnections(Polling)` and `ObserveUnauthorizedPollingConnections(Polling)` overlapped in time.

The listening variant of this test (`ObserveUnauthorizedListeningConnections`) has never had this issue because it uses `WithServiceTrustingTheWrongCertificate()`, which configures the wrong certificate **before** `Build()` — so connections are unauthorized from the very first attempt.

## Fix

Adds `WithClientTrustingNoThumbprints()` to `LatestClientBuilder` and `LatestClientAndLatestServiceBuilder`. When set, the builder skips the `client.Trust(thumbprint)` call, leaving the client's trust provider empty before `Build()` starts the polling service. This eliminates the race entirely: no connection can ever be authorized because trust is never established.

The test now mirrors the pattern used by the listening variant — unauthorized behaviour is configured at builder time rather than mutated post-build.

## Test results

- `net48`: 2 passed (InMemory + Redis queue variants) — the target framework from the failing CI run
- `net8.0`: Redis variant skipped due to Docker not available locally; InMemory variant passes

## Summary

Two adjacent enhancements per Human Lead, building on PR #198 (v0.58.51 spacing + click-to-Maps InfoWindow):

1. **MapPanel InfoWindow enrichment.** Each venue pin's hover info now shows `name (bold) + 📇 address + 🚊 transit + 🚘 drive + ⭐ rating + "Tap pin → Google Maps"`. The user-anchor (blue) pin gets its own hover InfoWindow showing the reverse-geocoded area name (e.g. *"📍 Downtown Core · your search anchor"*), passed via new `anchorName` prop from `App.jsx`'s `locationName` state.
2. **Pick-list templates (T1/T2/T3)** — new 🚊/🚘 row inserted immediately above the 📍 Maps URL line in `formatVenueBlock`. Both modes when available; either alone when only one route succeeds; row skipped silently when neither.

## Implementation

- **New `travel-times.js`** — `enrichTravelTimes(userLat, userLng, venues)` fans out two parallel `computeRouteMatrix` calls (TRANSIT + DRIVE), populates `v.transitMinutes` / `v.driveMinutes` when condition is `ROUTE_EXISTS`. Best-effort: any failure logs and returns venues unchanged. Pattern mirrors `vibe-suggest.rankByWalkingTime` (which already handles WALK).
- **`venue-templates.js`** — new `formatTravelLine(p)` helper, exported and inserted in `formatVenueBlock` immediately before `formatMapsLine`. Applies to all three variants (T1/T2/T3).
- **`index.js`** — `enrichTravelTimes` called in three search paths after the result list is finalised, before the response/payload: `/api/cuisine/search`, `/api/cuisine/warm-start`, `/api/cuisine/nl-query`, plus `runFreeTextSearch`.
- **`web/cuisine/src/v2/components/MapPanel.jsx`** — venue InfoWindow HTML expanded with address + travel-time rows; anchor-pin `onmouseover`/`onmouseout` listeners attached when `userLoc` resolves.
- **`web/cuisine/src/v2/App.jsx`** — `anchorName={locationName}` prop wired to `MapPanel`.

## Cost

Two extra Routes API calls per `/cuisine` search and per free-text chat reply (~$0.01 per call). Within free tier for typical use.

## Stacking

This branch is stacked on `claude/v0-58-51-spacing-mapinfo` (PR #198). Once #198 merges, GitHub will auto-narrow this PR's diff to just v0.58.52 changes.

### Motivation

- Produce machine-readable missingness and complete-case flow summaries for appendix tables to document exclusions used in adjusted models.
- Clarify outcome measurement across analysis and manuscript text by explicitly framing vaccination as self-reported any-dose uptake and separating awareness from uptake. 
- Improve reproducibility by adding Python helper tools to redraw publication figures and validate bibliography links, and augment Stata outputs with additional event counts for clearer tables.

### Description

- Updated the Stata analysis (`HPV_thesis_merged.do`) to write CSV/DTA outputs for variable missingness (`tableA_missingness`) and complete-case exclusion profiles (`tableA_complete_case_profile`), to include unweighted event counts in bivariate table postfiles, and to post additional `event_n` fields for subpopulation proportions. 
- Revised LaTeX content across Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusion, and Appendix to consistently describe the vaccination outcome as self-reported any-dose uptake, add appendix tables documenting missingness and complete-case exclusions, and refine wording around decomposition interpretation and policy framing. 
- Added two Python tools under `Latex_Thesis/tools`: `regenerate_figures.py` to redraw publication-quality PNG figures from Stata-generated tables, and `check_references.py` to audit DOI/URL links and emit a CSV report; also updated thesis metadata (`main.tex`) and bibliography entries to reference a 2025 EPI plan. 
- Adjusted table structures and captions (separate adjusted-model tables, added unweighted n columns, formatting changes) and updated generated BBL/BIB entries to reflect new citations and ordering.

### Testing

- No automated tests were executed as part of this change; recommend running the Stata do-file end-to-end to regenerate `HPV thesis/Output` and then running the new Python scripts (`tools/regenerate_figures.py` and `tools/check_references.py`) as smoke checks in CI to validate outputs.

author: golovinelics
body:
💡 What
在 `apps/blog/app/components/ViewModeToggle.tsx` 中为 `ViewModeToggle` 组件添加了 `React.memo` 包装。

🎯 Why
`ViewModeToggle` 是一个纯展示型组件，除了 `compact` 参数外不接受任何复杂 props，且内部状态仅依赖 `usePathname()` 钩子（当路由改变时会自动重新渲染）。当它所在的父组件（如 `BlogHeader` 或侧边栏组件）因为悬浮状态、滚动状态变化而触发频繁重渲染时，`ViewModeToggle` 也会跟着无意义地重新渲染，白白消耗性能。添加 `React.memo` 能切断这一不必要的渲染链条。

📊 Impact
显著减少首页、时间线页面的 Header 或 Navigation 区域在发生交互时的组件树更新开销，将该组件的重渲染次数在父组件状态变动时降为 0（O(n) 降至 O(1)）。

🔬 Measurement
可通过 React DevTools 的 Profiler 面板录制操作（例如在页面中上下滚动导致 Header 出现/隐藏，或鼠标在 Header 区域移动触发聚光灯效果），观察 `ViewModeToggle` 是否在父组件更新时被跳过渲染（显示为 "Did not render"）。

author: nevadah
body:
## Summary
- After saving a bookmark, fires an async AI call to `provider.suggestTags` in the background
- Bookmark appears in the list immediately; tags fill in when the AI responds
- Suggested tags stored as `aiSuggestedTags`; also applied to `tags` unless `userModifiedTags` is true
- AI call is skipped entirely if no API key is configured
- AI failures are silently swallowed — the bookmark is already saved without tags
- Uses `updated` (the just-saved RootData) as the base for the tag update to avoid stale closure issues

## Test plan
- [ ] Configure an AI provider and API key in Settings
- [ ] Save a page — bookmark appears immediately
- [ ] Shortly after, tags appear on the bookmark automatically
- [ ] Manually add a tag before AI responds — `userModifiedTags` is true, AI tags stored in `aiSuggestedTags` but don't overwrite manual tags
- [ ] With no API key configured — bookmark saves normally, no AI call made

- Validate required tool arguments before permission-mode classification when auto-approving/denying approval requests.

- Add a regression test for memory-mode Bash approvals missing the required `command` parameter.

## Context
Separate follow-up to PR #2089. Rollout trajectories showed malformed Bash approval requests with only `description` were denied by memory mode before schema-required args were checked. author: ryans-posthog
body:
## Problem

When `asyncify` runs sync functions inside Temporal activities, we have no visibility into how long the wrapped call sits queued versus how long it actually executes. With `sync_to_async`'s default `thread_sensitive=True`, every asyncified call funnels through asgiref's single shared thread, so a slow ORM query in one activity can stall every other asyncified activity in the worker. Without timing data, that contention is invisible — the only signal is downstream timeouts.

## Changes

- Wrap the body of `asyncify` with timing instrumentation that captures three numbers:
  - `submit_time` (when the coroutine handed work to `sync_to_async`)
  - `start_time` (when the work actually began running on the executor thread)
  - completion time
- Emit an `asyncify_slow` warning via `activity.logger` when running inside a Temporal activity, with structured fields:
  - `thread_wait_seconds` — time spent queued before the executor picked the task up (the thread-lock signal)
  - `execution_seconds` — actual time spent running the wrapped function
  - `function`, `thread_name`, `activity_id` — for correlating across retries and identifying contended threads
- The warning is emitted in a `finally` block so it covers both success and exception paths.

The `thread_wait_seconds` field is the key signal: a non-trivial value indicates the asyncify executor is contended and asyncified activities are blocking each other.

## How did you test this code?

Agent-authored. No automated tests were added in this PR. Verification will come from observing `asyncify_slow` log lines in production once deployed.

## Publish to changelog?

no

## Docs update

n/a

## 🤖 Agent context

Co-authored with Claude Code. Human (@rsiil) wrote the implementation; agent was used to summarize and push the stack. Key intent: surface thread-lock-time as a first-class metric so we can see when asyncified Temporal activities are starving the shared `sync_to_async` thread. This PR is the observability half; the follow-up [#57839](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/57839) flips to `thread_sensitive=False` to actually fix the contention.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a self-contained VHDL implementation of a voice-note playback timer that counts elapsed time up to `5:00` with selectable playback speeds (1x, 1.5x, 2x) for use in lab/simulation exercises.
- Meet the constraints of using only basic combinational/sequential elements (counters, adders, frequency divisors) and expose BCD outputs suitable for display wiring and classroom tools like Logisim.

### Description
- Added `vhdl/voice_note_player.vhd` implementing the top-level entity and RTL architecture with a tick generator, MM:SS BCD counters, `start` control, target-time validation, and one-hot speed indicator outputs. 
- Implemented selectable-speed tick generation where `1x` uses a 1 Hz tick, `2x` uses a 0.5 s tick, and `1.5x` uses an alternating +1/+2-second increment pattern to achieve an average 1.5x rate. 
- Counter logic uses BCD-style units/ tens/ minutes (`cur_min`, `cur_sec_t`, `cur_sec_u`) and stops with `done_led` when the configured target is reached; a helper `is_invalid_time` function validates inputs against `0:00..5:00`. 
- Added `vhdl/README_voice_note_player.md` with a modular design explanation, a text block diagram, speed behavior notes, and suggestions for implementing the design in Logisim.

### Testing
- Committed the new files and verified repository state with `git status`, and file contents were printed successfully with `nl`/`sed`, all commands completed successfully. 
- No VHDL simulations or synthesis runs were executed as part of this change; functional verification (testbench/simulation) should be performed separately.

## Goal

Per Luke's brief: "observe, see what it has to say about each, lets see its intentions, you can even have it go as far as to draft changes, but not merge."

## Changes

1. **`perceive.py`**: add `lkmotto/appraisalos-bidding` to `DEFAULT_WATCH_REPOS`. Highest-volume stuck-issue surface (24 open issues) per `director-pointshoot-v2-targets.md`.
2. **`policy.py`**: new `DIRECTOR_DISABLED_KINDS` env (comma-separated MoveKind list). Drops matching kinds before eligibility evaluation, emitting `policy.decision` events with the reason `kind disabled by DIRECTOR_DISABLED_KINDS env`.

## Operator runbook (post-merge)

Set on the `motto-director` Northflank job:
```
DIRECTOR_DRY_RUN=0
DIRECTOR_DISABLED_KINDS=merge_pr
```

This shape is **observe + draft, no merge**:
| Move kind | Allowed | Output |
|---|---|---|
| file_issue | ✅ | Draft GitHub issue (no auto-close) |
| compound_pr | ✅ | Draft compound PR on `director/compound` branch (no merge) |
| spawn_session | ✅ | Claude Code session that drafts a PR via the session host |
| merge_pr | ❌ | Dropped at policy layer + would already need `auto-merge-ok` label |
| nudge_pipeline | ✅ | Non-destructive HTTP nudge |

`merge_pr` already requires the `auto-merge-ok` label via `is_eligible_for_auto_merge`. The env gate is belt-and-suspenders for first-touch repos.

## Review surfaces after first tick

- `policy.decision` events for each dropped kind with rationale
- Draft PRs / issues filed against `appraisalos-bidding`
- Langfuse traces (provider, tokens, cost, latency)
- Neon control-plane: `runs`, `tasks`, `decisions`, `events` rows
- OTel spans for any GitHub API or HTTP bottlenecks

## Tests

`test_filter_moves_drops_disabled_kinds` (new) verifies merge_pr + spawn_session are dropped while file_issue passes through. All 121 tests pass.

body:
## Summary

- Adds **R37** (`regex-template`, ERROR severity) to detect Dataverse Web API `$filter` equality expressions that use a Lookup attribute's bare logicalname (e.g., `appmoduleidunique eq <guid>`) instead of the required `_<logicalname>_value` annotation form. The bare form produces `0x80060888 — Could not find a property named 'appmoduleidunique'` at runtime.
- Rule seeded with `appmoduleidunique` (confirmed Lookup, Type=Lookup, Targets=appmodule on `appmodulecomponent`). Extensible via `node src/rule-manager.js set-variables R37 <name> ...`.
- 6 adversarial probes: 2 positive (bare filter / combined predicate), 4 negative (correct `_value` form / PK equality / `$select` clause / `$expand` navigation property).
- README rule table + failure modes section + probe count updated. Package bumped to v0.4.3.

## Substrate citations (URL-verified, in rule message and README)

1. `appmodulecomponent.appmoduleidunique` Type=Lookup, Targets=appmodule: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/reference/entities/appmodulecomponent
2. OData Lookup `_<logicalname>_value` filter pattern: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/query/filter-rows (section "Filter on lookup property")

## Design notes

- **Hard-coded list over heuristic** (implementation option (a)): a broad `\w+id\b eq` heuristic would catch unlisted Lookup names but risks false positives on Uniqueidentifier attributes whose logicalnames happen to end in `id`. The hard-coded watch list has zero false positives for names outside it and a documented extension path.
- **`\b` word boundary is the false-positive guard**: `_appmoduleidunique_value eq` does NOT match because `_` is `\w` — no word boundary exists between `_` and `a`. No negative lookbehind required.
- **Branches cleanly from main** (not entangled with the concurrent v0.4.2 PR branch which has already merged).

## Test plan

- [x] `node tests/run-battery.js` passes (81 probes, 0 failures)
- [x] P1 (bare filter) fires R37
- [x] P2 (combined predicate) fires R37
- [x] N1 (`_value` form) does NOT fire R37
- [x] N2 (PK equality `appmodulecomponentid`) does NOT fire R37
- [x] N3 (`$select` clause) does NOT fire R37
- [x] N4 (`$expand` navigation property) does NOT fire R37
- [x] All prior probes (75) still pass — no regressions

body:
## Plan

- Original plan: [Implementation Plan — Phase 4 of #229](https://github.com/mikejmckinney/ai-repo-template/issues/229#issuecomment-4374253148)
- Latest in 1–2 sentences: ADR-017 (template-repo-only pre-commit shellcheck + actionlint, ADR-013 unchanged for derived repos) + cap-override justification rule in `pr-resolve-all.md` enforced by Judge gate item 15 and mirrored in BUGBOT.md / styleguide.md.

## Plan revision sync

- [x] No post-open plan revisions yet — the original plan is the latest version.

## What changed

**ADR-017 + .pre-commit-config.yaml (template-repo-only):**

- `docs/decisions/adr-017-template-repo-pre-commit-default.md` (new) — installs pre-commit shellcheck + actionlint for the template repo's own development. Explicit "Non-reversal of ADR-013" subsection: ADR-013 governs derived repos and stays `Accepted`. ADR-017 is **additive**, not superseding.
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` (new at repo root) — minimal config: `shellcheck-precommit v0.10.0` + `rhysd/actionlint v1.7.7`. Hook flags pinned to match `.github/workflows/lint-and-format.yml` (severity, SC1091 exclude, SC2016/2086/2129/2153/2018/2019 actionlint ignores) so a clean local run signals a clean CI run for these two tools.
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml.template` — preserved verbatim; top-of-file comment cross-links ADR-017 so the two-track design (template-internal vs derived-repo) is legible.
- `docs/decisions/README.md` — index row for ADR-017.

**Cap-override justification rule:**

- `.github/prompts/pr-resolve-all.md` — new "Override justification" subsection in Round disciplines. When `cap-override` is in effect AND round count > 3, every Resolution Report from round 4 onward must include a literal `Override justification: <category>` line directly under `### Summary`. Categories (verbatim): `sandbox-class | legitimate refactor | complex semantic dependency | other: <≤80-char reason>`. Resolution Report template updated to show the field.
- `.github/agents/judge.agent.md` — gate item 15 BLOCKs at diff-gate when override is in effect, the latest Resolution Report's round number is > 3, and the justification line is missing or malformed.
- `.cursor/BUGBOT.md` + `.gemini/styleguide.md` — mirror entry under "Repo-specific Judge gates"; both files bumped from "eight gates" to "nine gates".
- `docs/guides/agent-pipeline.md` — `PR_RESOLVE_MAX_ROUNDS` row + Manual Intervention Points cap-override row reference the new rule.

**Tests:** `test.sh` +12 invariants (ADR-017 `Status: Accepted`; ADR-013 non-supersession guard; decisions README index; `.pre-commit-config.yaml` existence + shellcheck/actionlint hooks; `.pre-commit-config.yaml.template` cross-link; pr-resolve-all override rule; judge gate item 15; BUGBOT.md / styleguide.md mirrors). **278 passed / 0 failed / 1 warning** (matches Phase 1.5 baseline).

## Verification

```bash
bash test.sh                                    # 278 passed / 0 failed
bash scripts/lint-shell-conventions.sh scripts/ # all checks passed
python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open('.pre-commit-config.yaml'))"
```

Maintainer-side (one-time): `pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files`.

## Outcome (15-minute test)

A maintainer cloning fresh:

1. Reads `README.md` / `AI_REPO_GUIDE.md` and finds `.pre-commit-config.yaml` listed alongside `.pre-commit-config.yaml.template` with the ADR-017 / ADR-013 audience split called out.
2. Runs `pip install pre-commit && pre-commit install` (one-time) — subsequent commits run shellcheck + actionlint locally on changed files.
3. Reads `docs/decisions/adr-017-template-repo-pre-commit-default.md` and understands why this template repo (only) installs the hooks while ADR-013 still applies to derived repos.
4. Reads `.github/prompts/pr-resolve-all.md` "Override justification" subsection and sees what the Resolution Report must include from round 4 onward when `cap-override` is in effect.

## Doc sync

- [x] `AI_REPO_GUIDE.md` — `.pre-commit-config.yaml` entry added to file tree + Development Tools table; verification commands list `pre-commit run --all-files`.
- [x] `README.md` — `.pre-commit-config.yaml` entry added to file tree + reference table.
- [x] `docs/decisions/README.md` — ADR-017 indexed.
- [x] `docs/guides/agent-pipeline.md` — `PR_RESOLVE_MAX_ROUNDS` row + Manual Intervention Points table updated.
- [x] `.cursor/BUGBOT.md` — Cap-override justification gate mirrored; "eight gates" → "nine gates".
- [x] `.gemini/styleguide.md` — Cap-override justification gate mirrored; "eight gates" → "nine gates".
- [x] `test.sh` — 12 new invariants cover ADR-017, the cap-override rule wiring, and reviewer-mirror parity.
- [x] `.context/state/_active.md`, `.context/state/coordination.md`, `.context/sessions/latest_summary.md` — task-boundary updates per AGENTS.md §"Session-state cadence".

## Risks

- pre-commit hooks block local commits in the template repo. Mitigation: ADR-017 explicitly accepts this; `--no-verify` remains available and surfaces in `git log`.
- Override justification rule could be ignored. Mitigation: the Judge diff-gate BLOCK is mechanical — no justification line on a Resolution Report past round 3 with override active = BLOCK.
- ADR-013 readers may suspect a reversal. Mitigation: ADR-017's "Non-reversal of ADR-013" subsection is explicit; the new `test.sh` invariant guards ADR-013's Status line against accidental supersession edits.

Refs #229

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Moderate process/tooling risk: introduces a new repo-root `.pre-commit-config.yaml` that can affect derived repos if left in place, and adds a new BLOCK-level Judge gate that could block PRs based on Resolution Report formatting.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **ADR-017** and a new repo-root `.pre-commit-config.yaml` to run *template-repo-only* pre-commit hooks (shellcheck + actionlint) with args/version pinned to match `.github/workflows/lint-and-format.yml`, while explicitly keeping ADR-013’s derived-repo stance unchanged and cross-linking this split from `.pre-commit-config.yaml.template`.
> 
> Introduces a **cap-override justification** requirement in `pr-resolve-all.md` (mandatory `Override justification: <category>` line from round 4+ when `cap-override` is active) and enforces it via new Judge gate item 15, mirrored into `.cursor/BUGBOT.md`, `.gemini/styleguide.md`, and referenced in `docs/guides/agent-pipeline.md`.
> 
> Updates `AI_REPO_GUIDE.md`/`README.md` to document the new pre-commit file and local run command, and extends `test.sh` with Phase 4 invariants to mechanically assert ADR/indexing, non-supersession of ADR-013, pre-commit config presence, and the new gate/mirror wiring.

body:
This PR updates [django](https://pypi.org/project/django) from **3.1.2** to **6.0.5**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 6.0.5
   ```
   ==========================

*May 5, 2026*

Django 6.0.5 fixes three security issues with severity "low" and several bugs
in 6.0.4.

CVE-2026-5766: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ASGI requests via file upload limit bypass
======================================================================================================

ASGI requests with a missing or understated ``Content-Length`` header could
bypass the :setting:`FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE` limit, potentially loading
large files into memory and causing service degradation.

As a reminder, Django :ref:`expects a limit to be configured
<user-uploaded-content-security>` at the web server level rather than solely
relying on :setting:`FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE`.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-35192: Session fixation via public cached pages and ``SESSION_SAVE_EVERY_REQUEST``
===========================================================================================

Response headers did not :ref:`vary on <using-vary-headers>` cookies if a
session was not modified, but :setting:`SESSION_SAVE_EVERY_REQUEST` was
``True``. A remote attacker could steal a user's session after that user visits
a cached public page.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-6907: Potential exposure of private data due to incorrect handling of ``Vary: *`` in ``UpdateCacheMiddleware``
=======================================================================================================================

Previously, :class:`~django.middleware.cache.UpdateCacheMiddleware` would
erroneously cache requests where the ``Vary`` header contained an asterisk
(``'*'``). This could lead to private data being stored and served.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a misplaced ``</div>`` in the
  ``django/contrib/admin/templates/admin/change_list.html`` template added in
  Django 6.0 that could be problematic when overriding the ``pagination`` block
  (:ticket:`37029`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 6.0 where deprecation warnings incorrectly skipped
  lines from third-party packages prefixed with "django" (:ticket:`37067`).


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.4
   ```
   ==========================

*April 7, 2026*

Django 6.0.4 fixes one security issue with severity "moderate", four security
issues with severity "low", and several bugs in 6.0.3.

CVE-2026-3902: ASGI header spoofing via underscore/hyphen conflation
====================================================================

``ASGIRequest`` normalizes header names following WSGI conventions, mapping
hyphens to underscores. As a result, even in configurations where reverse
proxies carefully strip security-sensitive headers named with hyphens, such a
header could be spoofed by supplying a header named with underscores.

Under WSGI, it is the responsibility of the server or proxy to avoid ambiguous
mappings. (Django's :djadmin:`runserver` was patched in :cve:`2015-0219`.) But
under ASGI, there is not the same uniform expectation, even if many proxies
protect against this under default configuration (including ``nginx`` via
``underscores_in_headers off;``).

Headers containing underscores are now ignored by ``ASGIRequest``, matching the
behavior of :pypi:`Daphne <daphne>`, the reference server for ASGI.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-4277: Privilege abuse in ``GenericInlineModelAdmin``
=============================================================

Add permissions on inline model instances were not validated on submission of
forged ``POST`` data in
:class:`~django.contrib.contenttypes.admin.GenericInlineModelAdmin`.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-4292: Privilege abuse in ``ModelAdmin.list_editable``
==============================================================

Admin changelist forms using
:attr:`~django.contrib.admin.ModelAdmin.list_editable` incorrectly allowed new
instances to be created via forged ``POST`` data.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-33033: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ``MultiPartParser`` via base64-encoded file upload
===============================================================================================================

When using ``django.http.multipartparser.MultiPartParser``, multipart uploads
with ``Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64`` that include excessive whitespace
may trigger repeated memory copying, potentially degrading performance.

This issue has severity "moderate" according to the :ref:`Django security
policy <security-disclosure>`.

CVE-2026-33034: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ASGI requests via memory upload limit bypass
=========================================================================================================

ASGI requests with a missing or understated ``Content-Length`` header could
bypass the :setting:`DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE` limit when reading
``HttpRequest.body``, potentially loading an unbounded request body into
memory and causing service degradation.

This issue has severity "low" according to the :ref:`Django security policy
<security-disclosure>`.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a regression in Django 6.0 where :func:`~django.contrib.auth.alogin`
  and :func:`~django.contrib.auth.alogout` did not respectively set or clear
  ``request.user`` if it had already been materialized (e.g., by sync
  middleware) (:ticket:`37017`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 6.0 in admin forms where
  ``RelatedFieldWidgetWrapper`` incorrectly wrapped all widgets in a
  ``<fieldset>`` (:ticket:`36949`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 6.0 where the ``fields.E348`` system check did not
  detect name clashes between model managers and
  :attr:`~django.db.models.ForeignKey.related_name`\s for non-self-referential
  relationships (:ticket:`36973`).


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 6.0.3
   ```
   ==========================

*March 3, 2026*

Django 6.0.3 fixes a security issue with severity "moderate", a security issue
with severity "low", and several bugs in 6.0.2.

==============================================================================================================

The :class:`~django.forms.URLField` form field's ``to_python()`` method used
:func:`~urllib.parse.urlsplit` to determine whether to prepend a URL scheme to
the submitted value. On Windows, ``urlsplit()`` performs

disproportionately slow for large inputs containing certain characters.

body:
### Motivation

- Evitar que la columna DEMO quede indefinidamente en HOLD cuando un bot estuvo en REAL y quedó desfasado, permitiendo avance seguro cuando el resto de bots ya cerró la ronda.

### Description

- Añade la excepción temporal REAL_OWNER_LAG / EXENTO_TEMPORAL_POST_REAL que detecta cuando falta exactamente un bot (5/6) y ese faltante es el owner REAL o ex-owner reciente; en ese caso se libera la siguiente ronda sin exigir su ACK y se registra `RELEASE_CON_EXENTO_REAL_OWNER`.
- Nuevas funciones y estructuras: `_SYNC_REAL_OWNER_LAG_TS`, `SYNC_POST_REAL_EXEMPT_WINDOW_S`, `_sync_real_order_viva_any`, `_sync_mark_recent_real_owner`, `_sync_is_recent_real_owner`, `_sync_ack_round_absurd_for_exempt`, `_sync_eval_real_owner_lag_exempt`; y se marca owner reciente al ejecutar `_sync_round_release_after_real_close`.
- Cambios en el flujo maestro: en `_sync_round_tick_maestro` se evalúa `post_real_exempt = _sync_eval_real_owner_lag_exempt(...)`; si es válido se llama a `_sync_round_release_next_round(..., "EXENTO_TEMPORAL_POST_REAL", extra=...)` y emite evento compacto y línea de estado `SYNC_STATUS_LINE` indicando `POST_REAL_EXENTO`.
- Mejoras diagnósticas/watchdog/HUD: mensajes HOLD reemplazados por diagnósticos legítimos (`SYNC HOLD LEGÍTIMO`, `HOLD_POR_REAL_ACTIVO`, `HOLD_POR_REAL_CLOSE_PENDING`), cooldown configurable (`SYNC_REAL_HOLD_DIAG_COOLDOWN_S`), y una línea compacta `SYNC_STATUS_LINE` añadida al HUD con estados: HOLD_REAL_ACTIVO / POST_REAL_EXENTO / NORMAL.
- No se modifica la lógica de trading (compra DEMO/REAL), Martingala, tokens, orden REAL, IA/modelos, zonas o bots externos; la liberación con exento no crea órdenes REAL ni altera martingala.

### Testing

- Ejecutado `python -m py_compile 5R6M-1-2-4-8-16.py`; compilación sin errores (OK).
- Se realizaron inspecciones estáticas del diff y verificación de las funciones afectadas (`_sync_round_tick_maestro`, `_sync_round_release_next_round`, `_sync_round_release_now`, `_sync_round_release_after_real_close`, `_sync_round_detect_future_ack_consensus`, lectura de `SYNC_ROUND_STATE_PATH`, `REAL_CLOSE_PENDING`, `owner_real`, `REAL_OWNER_LOCK`, `released_round`) para asegurar que la excepción se aplica sólo en las condiciones descritas y que las protecciones anteriores (REAL_CLOSE_PENDING, orden REAL viva, contratos pendientes, ACK absurdos) siguen bloqueando la liberación.

author: cleanexpo
body:
## Summary

Closes RA-1995 (Wave 2 / 6). Foundational primitive for the Margot Wave 5 research pipeline + marketing-icp-research workflows. Pure deterministic extraction (no LLM call); ICP / research skills consume the parsed output.

## Components

- \`app/server/pi_ceo_docparser.py\` — \`parse_document(path, max_pages) -> ParsedDoc(text, pages, tables, metadata, error)\`. Auto-detects type by extension (.pdf / .docx / .txt / .md).
- \`scripts/run_doc_parse.py\` — CLI with \`--json\` / \`--tables\` / \`--max-pages\`.
- \`skills/pi-ceo-docparser/SKILL.md\` — public-API contract.
- \`skills/marketing-icp-research/SKILL.md\` — \`documents\` input added referencing \`parse_document\`; page-number citations preserved.
- \`tests/test_pi_ceo_docparser.py\` — 16 tests.

## Design choices

- **Optional deps with fail-soft.** PDF tries \`pymupdf\` (preferred — high fidelity, AGPL) → \`pypdf\` (BSD pure-Python). When neither installed, returns \`ParsedDoc(error="missing_pdf_dep")\` with \`fix\` hint. **Never raises.**
- **python-docx already in venv** so DOCX always supported. No binary-blob fixtures — tests synthesise + round-trip.
- **No OCR.** Scanned PDFs without embedded text layer return empty per-page text. Separate ticket if needed.
- **Page boundaries preserved** via \`\\f\` form-feed in \`text\` and structured \`pages\` list, so downstream LLMs can cite \`"p. 3 of interview-2026-05-06.pdf"\`.
- **DOCX hard page-breaks** parsed via element XML inspection — independent of python-docx internal API churn.

author: marcelo393
body:
Reescreve o projeto como FlowDesk, uma SaaS estilo Chatwoot/WhatsApp
Business focada em escritórios de advocacia. Substitui a stack legada
(Vite 5 + React 18 + Tailwind v3 + react-router-dom) por TanStack Start v1
+ React 19 + Vite 7 + Tailwind v4, com SSR habilitado e file-based
routing em src/routes/.

Funcionalidades:
- Inbox compartilhada por setor (Recepção, Trabalhista, Previdenciário,
  Financeiro), com filtros, busca, etiquetas e contadores de não lidas
- Painel de conversa com bolhas de mensagem, notas internas, atalhos de
  resposta rápida via "/", transferência entre setores (com validação
  agente↔setor) e atribuição
- Painel lateral de detalhes do contato com etiquetas, histórico de
  transferências e conversas anteriores
- Admin com 4 CRUDs (setores, agentes, etiquetas, respostas rápidas) e
  visão geral com KPIs e gráfico por setor
- Auth fake via localStorage, mock store reativo (useSyncExternalStore)
  com selectors memoizados, seed completo de 10 conversas

Detalhes técnicos:
- Tokens HSL semânticos em @theme inline (Tailwind v4), modo escuro via
  .dark{}; sem tailwindcss-animate (animações via @keyframes)
- Timestamps formatados com timeZone fixo America/Sao_Paulo p/ evitar
  hidratação inconsistente; useNow() para "tempo relativo" só após mount
- Avatares com cor derivada (FNV-1a + paleta fixa) determinística
- Indicadores de seleção via data-active + opacity (sem render
  condicional) p/ evitar mismatch SSR/cliente
- contain: content nos painéis de chat e lista; touch-action:
  manipulation em botões/links

author: willie-yao
body:
The `cloud-provider-azure-conformance-multi-zone-vmss-capz` job is failing on
 `[sig-network] Services should implement NodePort and HealthCheckNodePort correctly when ExternalTrafficPolicy changes`.
 
 The test asserts that source IP is preserved through kube-proxy's
 `externalTrafficPolicy=Local` short-circuit path, which is incompatible with
 CAPZ's default Calico VXLAN encapsulation (the source IP gets rewritten to the
 node's `vxlan.calico` tunnel address).
 
 Only this job is affected because it uses `WORKER_MACHINE_COUNT: "3"`; the test
 requires ≥3 schedulable workers and is skipped automatically elsewhere.
 
 Refs: https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cloud-provider-azure/issues/9863, https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cluster-api-provider-azure/pull/6252
